items.title: Prevalence of psychological distress among family caregivers of children with cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.authors: Dias de Jesus EE, Carminatti M, Bastos Matos Schlichting J, Sudatti Delevatti R, Lopez P, de la Rocha Freitas C.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: This study aimed to systematically review and quantify the prevalence of anxiety and depressive symptoms in family caregivers of children with cancer and to explore potential determinants that may influence these outcomes.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This systematic review and meta-analysis. Searches were conducted across multidisciplinary, health, and psychology databases, supplemented by grey literature sources. Observational studies reporting validated measures of caregiver anxiety or depression were included. Data extraction and risk-of-bias assessments (JBI tool) were performed independently by multiple reviewers. Random-effects single-proportion meta-analyses, subgroup analyses, and meta-regressions were conducted to estimate pooled prevalence rates and explore heterogeneity.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A total of 2,089 records were identified through database searches. After screening and eligibility assessment, 30 studies were included in the systematic review and meta-analysis. Most studies were cross-sectional and conducted in North America or Europe. The pooled prevalence of anxiety symptoms was 25% (95% CI: 16-36%), based on 19 studies (n = 2,116), while the pooled prevalence of depressive symptoms was 27% (95% CI: 17-39%), based on 23 studies (n = 2,091). High heterogeneity was observed across analyses (I^2 > 95%). Meta-regressions showed no associations between prevalence rates and caregiver or child age, sex distribution, or leukemia prevalence. Subgroup analyses revealed higher anxiety prevalence in studies conducted in Asia and Europe and in those using combined assessment tools. No significant subgroup differences were found for depression. Risk-of-bias assessments indicated considerable methodological limitations, particularly regarding sampling and reporting. Therefore, the pooled prevalence estimates should be interpreted with caution due to the substantial between-study variability.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Approximately one in four caregivers of children with cancer experience clinically significant anxiety or depressive symptoms. These results emphasize the importance of care strategies that include family members and address their mental health needs throughout the entire cancer treatment process.

items.title: Effectiveness of Psychosocial Interventions to Promote Mental Health and Psychological Well-Being Among Older Persons With Depression and Anxiety: Systematic Review.
items.authors: Bayu EH, Hawkins N, Usher K, Shahidul Islam M, Jones R.
items.journal: International journal of mental health nursing

sections.text: Depression and anxiety are among the most common mental health problems experienced by older persons. Despite several studies advocating psychosocial treatment for depression and anxiety, little is known about evidence of the effectiveness of psychosocial intervention to promote mental health and psychological well-being among older persons with depression and anxiety. The objective of this review is to explore and examine the effectiveness of psychosocial interventions designed to promote mental health and psychological well-being among older persons with depression and anxiety. We searched and included articles published from 2015 to December 18, 2025, in five databases, including PubMed, ProQuest, Scopus, EBSCOhost, and Google Scholar. The Mixed Method Appraisal Tool (MMAT-18) was used for quality appraisal of the included studies. Due to the heterogeneity of intervention types and outcome measures, as well as the lack of sufficient reported numerical data, we didn't conduct a meta-analysis. Therefore, data were analysed using narrative synthesis, and findings were grouped by intervention type and outcomes. From 2830 retrieved articles, 27 randomized controlled trials met inclusion criteria. A total of 11 distinct types of psychosocial interventions were identified, all of which demonstrated effectiveness in reducing depressive symptoms. Furthermore, 6 intervention types demonstrated effectiveness in reducing anxiety symptoms, and 5 intervention types demonstrated improvements in psychosocial well-being and quality of life. Among the 11 psychosocial interventions identified in this review, Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT), behavioural activation, and reminiscence therapy were the most frequently evaluated interventions with demonstrated effectiveness for treating depressive and anxiety symptoms in older persons. The effect sizes of the interventions varied across intervention types and settings. In conclusion, the result of this review suggests that psychosocial interventions significantly reduce symptoms of depression and anxiety while also improving the psychological well-being and quality of life for older adults. The significant variation of intervention effect sizes across settings and intervention types indicates psychosocial interventions need to be adapted and evaluated in local contexts, depending on the culture and needs of the population.

items.title: Empowering Communities for Prevention: The HAMA Model of Positive Psychology, Resilience, Substance Use, and Problematic Screen Use Prevention Among Adolescents.
items.authors: Shoshani A, Kor A.

sections.text: This study evaluated HAMA, a municipality-based model integrating positive psychology, resilience promotion, and prevention of substance use and problematic digital-media use among youth-serving professionals and adolescents. Four Israeli municipalities were randomly assigned to HAMA or wait-list control conditions. Participants were 1399 professionals (702 intervention, 697 control) and 1666 adolescents (845 intervention, 821 control). HAMA combined data-informed municipal roundtables, 30-academic-hour professional training, a school-based curriculum, parent engagement, and coordinated municipal initiatives. Outcomes were assessed before and immediately after the 2024-2025 academic-year intervention. Compared with controls, intervention participants showed more favorable changes in emotional well-being, anxiety, depression, somatization, and general distress. Professionals also reported greater prevention self-efficacy, while professionals and adolescents showed more favorable patterns of substance use and problematic digital-media engagement. Findings provide initial short-term support for an integrated model connecting evidence-based prevention content with professional development, school intervention, parent engagement, and municipal coordination.

items.title: Evidence for anterior cingulate cortex glutathione levels as a biomarker of oxidative stress and antioxidant response in people with bipolar disorder.
items.authors: Prisciandaro JJ, Prescot AP, Murali-Manohar S, Edden RAE, Ye Z, Zhang J, Townsend DM, Brand K, Hix S, Mellick WH, Tolliver BK.

sections.text: Glutathione (GSH), the brain's primary antioxidant, confers a critical first line of defense against oxidative-stress-induced cellular damage, with some evidence supporting compensatory upregulation of anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) GSH in bipolar disorder (BD). N-acetylcysteine (NAC), which increases GSH by providing cells with the rate-limiting substrate of GSH synthesis (i.e., cysteine), has been investigated as an adjunctive treatment for BD and has been found to reduce residual depressive symptoms, though no studies have evaluated whether NAC affects brain GSH levels in these patients. To further evaluate brain GSH levels as a candidate oxidative-stress biomarker and interventional target for adjunctive treatment for BD, we present data from two independent proton MR spectroscopy (^1H-MRS) investigations; a cross-sectional comparison of dorsal ACC (dACC) GSH levels in BD (n = 29) vs HC (n = 26) individuals, followed by a pilot (n = 12), randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, crossover study of 3 g/day of NAC versus placebo on dACC GSH levels. We demonstrate that BD individuals have significantly elevated dACC GSH levels (Cohen's d = 0.56, p = 0.046), which are associated with a greater number of past-year depressive episodes (r = 0.39, p = 0.041), relative to HC individuals, and that NAC treatment is associated with significantly higher dACC GSH (Cohen's d = 0.45, p = 0.040) but not glutamate (p = 0.325) levels, relative to placebo, in people with BD. These preliminary results, which should be interpreted with caution given the small sample sizes therein, further pave the way for ACC GSH levels to serve as a primary mechanistic target for novel antioxidant treatments for BD that overcome the bioavailability limitations of NAC.

items.title: Three latent subtypes of suicide risk and network characteristics of scale item associations among adolescents with major depressive disorder: a cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Liu M, He X, Mo P, Luo W, Luo J.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study aimed to identify latent suicide risk subtypes among first-episode, treatment-naive adolescents with major depressive disorder (MDD), and to explore the item-level association patterns across subtypes, so as to provide evidence for optimizing stratified suicide risk screening and supporting future longitudinal intervention research.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Latent profile analysis (LPA) and regularized partial correlation network analysis were adopted to analyze data from 930 first-episode, treatment-naive adolescents with MDD aged 12-18 years. Suicide risk subtypes were identified based on the Suicide Behaviors Questionnaire-Revised (SBQ-R). Scale item association networks were constructed using items from the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), SBQ-R, and dimensions of Adolescent Self-Rating Life Events Checklist (ASLEC). Differences in high-centrality items and network structural characteristics were compared across subtypes.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Three suicide risk subtypes were identified among adolescents with MDD: a low suicide risk group (n = 248, 26.7%), a low-disclosure, high suicide vulnerability group (n = 329, 35.4%), and an overt, high suicide risk group (n = 353, 38.0%). Significant differences were observed between the groups in terms of total SBQ-R and ASLEC scores. PHQ-9 total scores were significantly lower in the low suicide risk group than in the other two groups, which did not differ from each other. The low-disclosure, high-suicide-vulnerability group exhibited a depressive symptom burden and partial suicide risk indicators comparable to those of the overt, high-suicide-risk group, yet demonstrated lower active disclosure of suicide-related information. Among the low suicide risk group, items with the highest strength centrality were PHQ-9 Item 1 (loss of interest), ASLEC dimension I (punishment) and PHQ-9 Item 2 (depressed mood). In the low-disclosure, high-suicide-vulnerability group, PHQ-9 Item 2, ASLEC dimension III (interpersonal relationships) and PHQ-9 Item 1 showed elevated node strength. In the overt high suicide risk group, ASLEC dimensions I and III, and PHQ-9 Item 4 (fatigue/loss of energy) had the strongest node connections. Network comparison test detected no significant differences in global strength for all pairwise subtype contrasts; significant structural divergence emerged only between the low suicide risk group and the overt high suicide risk group. SBQ-R Item 4 (future likelihood of suicide) was the only differentially weighted node. Given that this item contributed to latent profile derivation, this node-level difference is subject to partial mechanical circularity and must be interpreted cautiously.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Marked heterogeneity exists in suicide risk among adolescents with MDD. The low-disclosure high suicide vulnerability subtype presents depressive burden and partial suicide risk indicators similar to the overt high-risk group, accompanied by insufficient disclosure of suicide-related information. Across subtypes, network structures showed considerable overlap with only limited item-level correlational discrepancies. Centrality metrics merely reflect correlational patterns among scale items, rather than causal relationships or definitive intervention targets. These findings inform stratified risk screening and warrant validation via longitudinal research.

sections.heading: Trial registration
sections.text: This study was prospectively registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (Registration No.: ChiCTR2400088411; Registration Date: August 19, 2024). Registration website: https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=235322.

items.title: Conversational AI chatbots: a double-edged sword for mental health and social well-being among medical students.
items.authors: Ahmed A, Mohamed MAE, Ali WBA, Eldouma MYM, Abdalla MohammedAli RM, Barakat HOM, Alapoud MM, Ali ASH, Alngar YAA, Ahmed SAM, Osman MMA, Gassemalseed TFA, Gadallah AA, Eljack MMF.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Medical students face a significant burden of depressive symptoms and social isolation, particularly in conflict-affected regions like Sudan, where access to formal mental health services is severely restricted. While AI chatbots are increasingly adopted for academic and emotional assistance, their relationship with psychological outcomes in such unstable, resource-constrained environments remains poorly characterized. This study aimed to evaluate the association between conversational AI utilization, depressive symptoms, and social isolation among Sudanese medical students to guide evidence-based policy and the responsible development of digital support tools.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A large-scale, cross-sectional survey was conducted between November 2025 and March 2026. Data were collected from 2,507 medical students using validated instruments, including the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) for depressive symptoms and the Revised UCLA Loneliness Scale-6 (RULS-6) for social isolation. Structured questionnaires assessed sociodemographic characteristics, chatbot usage patterns, and perceived psychological benefits.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Chatbot adoption was nearly universal, with 41.9% of participants reporting daily use. Although academic perceived support was the primary driver of engagement (88.8%), significant subsets also used AI for companionship (22.2%) and to cope with stress or loneliness (23.1%). High prevalence rates were observed for both mild-to-severe depressive symptoms (70.6%) and moderate-to-high loneliness (65.0%). Students exhibiting higher levels of psychological distress were significantly more likely to report emotional connectivity, perceived companionship, and subjective well-being benefits from AI interactions, although these correlations remained statistically weak.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Conversational AI chatbots have become a ubiquitous tool among Sudanese medical students, fulfilling both pedagogical and relational roles. In a conflict-affected context with restricted access to formal mental health services, AI provides a scalable, low-barrier support mechanism. However, the potential for digital reliance to exacerbate social withdrawal warrants caution. These findings emphasize the need for responsible AI integration and longitudinal research to delineate the long-term effects of AI-mediated support on student well-being.

Conversational AI chatbots have become a ubiquitous tool among Sudanese medical students, fulfilling both pedagogical and relational roles. In a conflict-affected context with restricted access to formal mental health services, AI provides a scalable, low-barrier support mechanism. However, the potential for digital reliance to exacerbate social withdrawal warrants caution. These findings emphasize the need for responsible AI integration and longitudinal research to delineate the long-term effects of AI-mediated support on student well-being.

items.title: Cost-utility study of cognitive-behavioural management of auditory hallucinations in schizophrenia: a study protocol.
items.authors: Raffard S, Fongaro E, Hayward M, Picot MC, Kamidian A, Mercier G, Bortolon C, Capdevielle D.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Auditory verbal hallucinations (AVHs) affect 60-80% of patients with schizophrenia, causing significant distress and functional impairment. Although cognitive-behavioural therapy (CBT) has been shown to reduce AVH-related distress and relapse risk, its use remains limited in many countries, including France, due to insufficient clinician training and time constraints. Consequently, treatment continues to rely mainly on second-generation antipsychotics, which have moderate efficacy and notable adverse effects. A structured CBT program combining Coping Strategy Enhancement, relational therapy, third-wave CBT, and imagery-focused techniques has the potential to further reduce the intensity of AVHs and associated distress. This study evaluates the clinical effectiveness and cost-utility of this intervention, with a view to its broader integration into psychiatric care.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This randomized controlled trial will assess the cost-utility and clinical effectiveness of CBT for AVHs in patients with schizophrenia spectrum disorders. A total of 240 patients, aged 15-60 years, experiencing distressing AVHs for at least three months, will be recruited from outpatient psychiatric services. Patients will be randomly assigned (1:1) to either the intervention group (CBT + treatment as usual, TAU), receiving 16 weekly one-hour individual CBT sessions in addition to standard care, or the control group (TAU alone), receiving standard psychiatric follow-up and pharmacological treatment without CBT. The primary outcome is the incremental cost-utility ratio at 12 months, expressed as cost per quality-adjusted life years (QALY) derived from the EuroQuality of life 5-dimension 5-Level questionnaire (EuroQol EQ-5D-5 L), comparing TAU alone with CBT + TAU. Secondary outcomes include changes from baseline at 4, 8, and 12 months in AVHs severity, depressive symptoms, suicidal ideation, quality of life, functioning, sleep quality, substance use, psychiatric comorbidity, pharmacological treatment exposure, and medication adherence. All endpoint assessments will be conducted by independent evaluators blinded to treatment allocation.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: This is the first large-scale medico-economic trial evaluating CBT for AVHs in France. Strengths include a randomized controlled design, stratification by illness severity, and blinded outcome assessment. By jointly assessing clinical efficacy and economic value, the findings could inform healthcare policy and support the implementation of CBT as a standard component of schizophrenia treatment.

items.title: Neural dynamics of resting-state EEG microstates in youth major depressive disorder with suicidal ideation.
items.authors: Bao C, Zou H, Chen W, Zhang Q, Zhou Q, Yan R, Yao Z, Lu Q.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Youth major depressive disorder (MDD) is a debilitating condition associated with high rates of suicidal behavior. Although abnormal neuroimaging alterations have been reported in MDD patients with suicidal ideation (SI), little is known about the mechanisms of brain dynamics at high temporal resolution.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This cross-sectional study included 177 participants aged 15-30 years: 95 with drug-naïve MDD (53 with SI, 42 without SI) and 82 healthy controls. All participants underwent a standardized 5-minute resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) acquisition. Comprehensive clinical assessments were administered, including the collection of psychosocial data and evaluation of suicide risk using the Beck Scale for Suicide Ideation (BSI-C). Group differences in microstate parameters were analyzed, and correlations between these parameters and clinical variables were examined.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Resting-state EEG microstate analysis indicated that the SI group, relative to the NSI group, exhibited higher occurrence, coverage, and duration of microstate A, along with decreased indices for microstate B and reduced occurrence (but not coverage or duration) of microstate D. Alterations in transition probabilities were most prominent in microstates A and B, highlighting specific network-level differences associated with SI. In the SI group, BSI-C scores were positively correlated with the transition probability from C to B.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Our findings suggest that young individuals with MDD and SI show specific changes in microstates, especially A and B. These findings reveal altered EEG microstate dynamics associated with SI in young MDD patients and may inform future research on neurophysiological correlates of suicidal ideation.

items.title: Temporoparietal structural-functional coupling abnormalities in drug-naïve youths with major depressive disorder and suicidal ideation.
items.authors: Wang Y, Bao C, Bao J, Chen W, Zhang Q, Yan R, Yao Z, Lu Q.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Major depressive disorder (MDD) in youth is associated with higher suicide risk. Although white matter and functional connectivity abnormalities have been reported in MDD patients with suicidal ideation (SI), how brain structure and function interact abnormally remains unclear.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We conducted a cross-sectional study of participants aged 15-30, including 97 drug-naive MDD patients with SI, 44 without SI (nSI), and healthy controls (HC). We analyzed global and local structural-functional connectivity (SC-FC) coupling across groups and assessed its correlation with clinical features.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The study revealed significant differences in SC-FC coupling among the three groups (SI, nSI, and HC). At the local level, differences were identified in the left superior temporal gyrus (STG.L) and left Heschl's gyrus (HES.L). Specifically, the SI group exhibited the weakest negative SC-FC coupling in the HES.L compared to both the nSI group and HC group (P_FDR < 0.001). Additionally, a decrease in negative SC-FC coupling in the STG.L was observed in the SI group when compared to the HC group (P_FDR = 0.003). The HES.L SC-FC coupling alterations were negatively correlated with clinical symptoms of rumination and suicidal risk in the SI group.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The findings suggest that MDD patients with SI exhibit disrupted SC-FC coupling, particularly in the HES.L and STG.L regions. These alterations were associated with higher levels of rumination and suicidal risk, underscoring the potential of SC-FC coupling as a candidate neurobiological correlate of suicidal ideation in MDD.

items.title: Pesticide use intensity and hospitalized suicide attempts among agricultural populations in France: ecological associations across French departments, 2020-2022.
items.authors: Chatard A, Daviller B, Doolub D, Leblanc PM, Besnier M, Delbreil A, Harika-Germaneau G, Jaafari N.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Suicide risk is elevated in agricultural populations, and pesticide use intensity has been proposed as a potential contributing factor. However, nationwide ecological evidence linking pesticide use intensity to suicidal behavior remains limited. This study examined ecological associations between pesticide use intensity and hospitalized suicide-attempt rates among agricultural populations in France.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Department-level pesticide use indicators were obtained from French Ministry of Agriculture open databases, and hospitalized suicide-attempt data were obtained from the French agricultural health insurance system (MSA) for 2020-2022. Associations between pesticide use intensity and hospitalized suicide-attempt rates were examined using Poisson regression models adjusted for MSA population size and historical standardized suicide mortality. Additional sensitivity analyses adjusted for territorial covariates.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Higher pesticide use intensity was consistently associated with higher suicide-attempt rates across the three study years. Associations remained robust in sensitivity analyses adjusting for MSA population structure, healthcare-access indicators, socioeconomic indicators, rurality, and overall departmental suicide-attempt rates in the general population. Associations were strongest for conventional chemical pesticide use, whereas herbicide-specific associations were weaker and less consistent.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Greater agricultural pesticide use intensity was associated with higher hospitalized suicide-attempt rates among MSA affiliates in France. Limitations include the ecological design, the absence of individual exposure and method-specific suicide-attempt data, and the inability to identify the underlying mechanism. Further individual-level and longitudinal research is needed to clarify the pathways underlying this association.

items.title: Effects of Online and Offline Psychotherapies on Anxio-Depressive Symptom Severity in Depression and Anxiety Disorders: A Follow-Up Research in Hungary.
items.authors: Tóth EH, Böngyik Á, Kelemen O, Kovács I.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: During the COVID-19 pandemic, the demand for online psychotherapeutic interventions has increased significantly, underscoring the necessity to investigate this type of therapy both independently and in comparison with traditional in-person psychotherapy. This study examines the effects of online, audio-visually synchronous psychotherapy compared to in-person psychotherapy.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Fifty-six participants completed the baseline assessment; follow-up assessments were conducted after the sixth and final psychotherapy sessions: (1) before the first psychotherapy session (baseline), (2) after the sixth session (mid-treatment), and (3) after their final psychotherapy session (posttreatment). Trial design is quasi-experimental, as patients were divided into two groups by their preference: those who received in-person (offline) and those who received online psychotherapeutic care. For symptom measurement the following questionnaires were used: Beck Depression Inventory (BDI), State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI), Paykel Life Event Questionnaire (PLEQ), Short Health Anxiety Inventory (SHAI), World Health Organization (WHO)-5-Well-Being Index, and Symptom Checklist-90-Revised. We hypothesized that (1) patients with more severe symptoms would choose in-person treatment and (2) symptom reduction could also be measured in online psychotherapeutic treatment.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: At baseline, the offline group had a significantly higher score only on the life event questionnaire ( t (37,804) = -2.109, p = 0.042). In the online group, depressive symptoms ( χ ^2(2) = 8.000, p = 0.018), anxiety symptoms ( χ ^2(2) = 8.400, p = 0.015); ( F (2) = 24.743, p < 0.001), health anxiety ( F (2) = 7.038, p = 0.027), and general psychological symptoms ( F (2) = 10.390, p = 0.011) showed significant decrease. In the offline group, depressive symptoms ( χ ^2(2) = 6.867, p = 0.032), anxiety symptoms ( χ ^2(2)0 = 10.457, p = 0.005); ( F (2) = 6.968, p = 0.007), and general psychological symptoms ( F (1.096) = 8.227, p = 0.018) decreased significantly. The offline group exhibited no difference in terms of health anxiety. Concerning therapeutic modality, both the online and offline settings were effective in reducing symptoms of depression, anxiety, as well as psychological symptoms, while no significant difference emerged between them.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Among participants who remained engaged and completed follow-up assessments, both online and in-person psychotherapy were associated with significant reductions in anxio-depressive and general psychopathological symptoms over the course of the study. No significant differences in symptom reduction were observed between the two treatment modalities. However, the high and differential attrition, particularly in the online group, precludes conclusions of equivalence or noninferiority between online and in-person psychotherapy. Our findings nevertheless suggest that online psychotherapy may be an effective treatment option for patients who remain engaged in care and support the need for further clinical studies to better understand its effectiveness, acceptability, and suitability across different patient groups.

items.title: Evaluation of Blood-Brain Barrier-Related Tight Junction Proteins in Children Diagnosed with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder.
items.authors: Şenel ME, Usta MB, Avcı B, Taflan FB.

sections.text: The potential role of blood-brain barrier (BBB)-associated tight junction proteins in attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) has not yet been fully elucidated. This cross-sectional case-control study aimed to evaluate serum claudin-5, claudin-11, claudin-12, and claudin-25 levels in children with ADHD, investigate their associations with symptom severity, and assess their diagnostic performance. The study included 40 children diagnosed with ADHD according to the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5) criteria and 40 age-matched healthy controls. Diagnostic assessment was performed using the Turkish adaptation of the Schedule for Affective Disorders and Schizophrenia for School-Age Children-Present and Lifetime Version for DSM-5 (K-SADS-PL-DSM-5), and ADHD symptom severity was evaluated using the teacher form of the Turgay DSM-IV-Based Child and Adolescent Behavior Disorders Screening and Rating Scale. Serum claudin levels were measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Serum claudin-12 and claudin-25 levels were higher in the ADHD group than in controls (both p < 0.001), whereas claudin-5 and claudin-11 levels did not differ significantly between groups. Within the ADHD group, serum claudin levels were not significantly correlated with teacher-reported symptom severity, except for a weak negative correlation between claudin-25 and hyperactivity/impulsivity (rs = -0.330, p = 0.037) that did not withstand correction for multiple comparisons. After adjustment for age, sex, and body mass index (BMI), higher claudin-12 (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 1.006, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.003-1.010; p < 0.001) and claudin-25 levels (adjusted OR = 1.002, 95% CI: 1.001-1.004; p = 0.010) remained associated with ADHD status. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses yielded areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.817 for claudin-12 and 0.782 for claudin-25. In this limited study, serum claudin-12 and claudin-25 concentrations were higher in children with ADHD than in healthy controls. However, these findings do not establish blood-brain barrier dysfunction or the clinical diagnostic utility of these proteins. Their tissue origin, biological significance, and diagnostic performance require further investigation and independent validation.

items.title: GABAergic and Glutamatergic Deficits in Schizophrenia: Pathophysiological Mechanisms Underlying Negative Symptoms and Cognitive Impairment.
items.authors: Zakrzewska AM, Gabryelska A, Strzelecki D.

sections.text: Schizophrenia is a complex neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by positive, negative, and cognitive symptoms. While classical dopaminergic models explain psychotic features, they fail to address the debilitating negative and cognitive deficits that dictate long-term disability. We aim to synthesize contemporary evidence on the impairment of the excitatory/inhibitory (E/I) balance within cortical microcircuits as a central pathophysiological hypothesis of the disorder. The cascade is hypothesized to be driven by N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor hypofunction, which impairs parvalbumin-positive (PV+) interneurons and consequently downregulates glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD67)-mediated gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) synthesis. Weakened PV+ interneuron function disrupts Pyramidal-Interneuron Network Gamma (PING) dynamics, reducing gamma-band synchronization and fronto-temporo-thalamic connectivity. At the macroscopic and cellular levels, the E/I imbalance is linked to reduced neuropil volume and aberrant synaptic pruning that disturbs dendritic architecture. Clinically, this triggers severe working memory dysfunction, cognitive rigidity, avolition, and anhedonia. This paper presents emerging glutamatergic and GABAergic pharmacological strategies, including glycine, D-serine, and metabotropic glutamate receptor (mGluR) modulators. We highlight key directions for future research, emphasizing the use of translational biomarkers (e.g., mismatch negativity (MMN), magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS), and gamma oscillations) to normalize PV+ interneuron function and network-level synchronization.

items.title: Impacts of COVID-19 on Modifiable Lifestyle Behaviors and Associations With Mental Well-Being Among Medical Students and Health Care Workers in Vietnam: Cross-Sectional Online Survey.
items.authors: Nguyen TT, Nguyen HT, Boyer L, Auquier P, Fond G, Nguyen DC, Do H, Latkin C, Vu GT, Ho CSH.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The COVID-19 pandemic has disrupted daily life and mental health globally; yet, little is known about how multiple modifiable lifestyle behaviors shape psychological outcomes among young health-affiliated populations in low- and middle-income settings such as Vietnam.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study aimed to examine changes in modifiable lifestyle behaviors during the COVID-19 pandemic and their associations with depression, anxiety, and perceived stress among medical students and health care workers in Vietnam, most of whom were young people aged 16 to 20 years.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted from September to November 2021 among 817 medical students and health care workers recruited through medical universities and health care facilities across Vietnam using snowball sampling. The sample was predominantly young, with 72.5% (591/815) aged 16 to 20 years, and 68.8% (558/811) were female individuals. This period captured the late Delta-driven fourth wave and Vietnam's transition from heterogeneous local restrictions to "safe and flexible adaptation," when daily routines, mobility, online learning/work, and mental well-being remained disrupted. The questionnaire assessed demographics, 14 lifestyle behaviors grouped into positive, diet/media-related, substance use, and violence-related domains, alongside validated Vietnamese-language measures of depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9 [PHQ-9]), anxiety (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 [GAD-7]), and stress (Perceived Stress Scale-4 [PSS-4]). Separate multivariable Tobit regression models were applied to account for bounded-scale outcomes with potential floor effects. Results are reported as unstandardized coefficients with 95% CIs.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: High stress was common (n=522, 63.9%; mean PSS-4 6.9, SD 2.2). Mean PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores were 5.2 (SD 4.7) and 3.1 (SD 3.6), respectively, and participants with higher stress had higher PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scores than those with lower stress (both P <.001). Central and Southern participants reported significantly higher scores than those in the North (Central: coefficient 0.47, 95% CI 0.06-0.87 and Southern: coefficient 0.53, 95% CI 0.17-0.88). Positive behaviors correlated with lower anxiety (coefficient -0.31, 95% CI -0.59 to -0.03) and stress (coefficient -0.36, 95% CI -0.48 to -0.24). By contrast, diet/media-related negative behaviors were associated with higher depression, anxiety, and stress (coefficient range 0.18-1.10), while violence-related behaviors showed similar adverse associations across all 3 outcomes (coefficient range 0.13-0.56).

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Lifestyle behaviors were associated with mental well-being under pandemic conditions among a predominantly young, health-affiliated sample in Vietnam. Because participants were recruited through an online snowball-sampling approach and were largely affiliated with medical universities or health care facilities, the findings should be interpreted as context-specific evidence rather than as estimates for the general Vietnamese adult population. Public health responses, particularly in educational and health-related settings, should incorporate behavior-focused strategies, promoting healthy routines, balanced diets, constructive digital use, and nonviolent coping to strengthen resilience in future crises.

items.title: A Structured Exercise Intervention for Individuals With Psychotic Disorders Treated With Long-Acting Injectable Antipsychotics: Protocol for a Nonrandomized Controlled Study.
items.authors: Silva S, Maia D, Coelho E, Mota MP.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Individuals with psychotic disorders have high rates of physical comorbidity and considerably reduced quality of life, often aggravated by the adverse metabolic effects associated with injectable antipsychotic treatment. Physical exercise has been identified as a promising strategy for improving physical and mental health in this population. This article describes the protocol for a structured multimodal physical exercise program designed to be implemented within outpatient psychiatric services for individuals treated with long-acting injectable (LAI) antipsychotics.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study aims to evaluate the impact of a structured exercise program on psychotic symptomatology in individuals with psychotic disorders receiving LAI antipsychotics. Secondary objectives include assessing the effects of the intervention on metabolic outcomes, particularly body composition and cardiometabolic risk factors. Exploratory analyses will be performed to investigate potential associations between exercise participation and longitudinal changes in antipsychotic treatment patterns, as well as variations in circulating biomarkers such as brain-derived neurotrophic factor, dopamine, and serotonin.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This is a prospective, controlled, longitudinal study developed in accordance with SPIRIT (Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials) recommendations. The study will recruit a clinical population of 151 eligible participants diagnosed with psychotic disorders (mean age 46.40, SD 13.60 years) receiving LAI antipsychotics. This protocol describes the implementation and evaluation of a 24-week supervised multimodal exercise program integrated into routine psychiatric outpatient care. Participants receiving LAI antipsychotics will be allocated to either the exercise program or a treatment-as-usual control group. The intervention will include supervised circuit-based sessions combining aerobic, resistance, mobility, and balance exercises, performed twice weekly, with a progressive training load and an additional autonomous walking component introduced in the second phase of the program. Clinical, functional, psychological, and cardiometabolic outcomes will be assessed at baseline (preintervention), after 12 weeks, after 24 weeks, and at an 8-week follow-up. The study has obtained ethical approval from the Ethics Committee of the Local Health Unit of Trás-os-Montes e Alto Douro, and written informed consent will be obtained from all participants.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The study was funded in January 2026. Recruitment and data collection began on January 1, 2026, and are expected to be completed by November 30, 2026. As of manuscript submission (May 2026), 25 participants had been recruited. Data analysis is projected for December 2026, with findings expected to be published in spring 2027.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Structured exercise interventions integrated into routine psychiatric care may represent an important strategy to improve the physical health, functional capacity, and overall well-being of individuals with psychotic disorders treated with LAI antipsychotics.

items.title: The mental health and adaptive functioning of adults with subdiagnostic autistic traits.
items.authors: Pan PY, Yeh CB, Bölte S.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Autistic traits in the general population share the genetic liability with autism and distribute as a quantitative continuum. In addition, the risk for co-occurring psychotic and emotional symptoms, physical health conditions, and the associated functional impairment may increase along with the level of autistic traits. This study aimed to examine the potential clinical relevance of subdiagnostic autistic traits in adults, focusing on co-occurring mental health and neurodevelopmental problems and low adaptive dysfunctioning.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A total of 659 adult participants (age range 20 to 83 years, mean age 34.49 ± 11.08 years, 53.3% female) were recruited from two teaching hospitals and a university, of whom 167 reported having psychiatric disorders. The Social Responsiveness Scale (SRS-2) was used to measure autistic traits and to categorize respondents into high, moderate, modest, and low autistic trait groups. Anxiety, depressive, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms and adaptive functions were measured by self-report instruments. Path analysis with structural equation modeling was applied to explore the relationship between autistic traits, ADHD symptoms and adaptive functioning and the mediating effects of emotional symptoms.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Participants with psychiatric diagnoses had increased likelihood for high (OR 9.55, p < 0.001) and moderate (OR 5.05, p < 0.001) but not modest autistic traits. Of note, compared to the group with low autistic traits, even participants with only modest autistic traits had higher risk for anxiety, depressive and ADHD symptoms, as well as lower adaptive functioning which was measured by the Adaptive Behavior Assessment System (ABAS-II) (all p < 0.001). Among the mental health conditions, autistic traits was found the largest effect size directly explaining adaptive functioning (standardized ß - 0.39, p < 0.001) while paritally mediated by emotional symptoms.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Beyond a dichotomous autism diagnosis, adults with subdiagnostic autistic trait levels have higher risk for psychiatric symptoms and disorders and adaptive functioning difficulties in various contexts, in line with the notion that there might be support needs along the autistic trait continuum. Our findings highlight that support for adults should be based on actual functional and mental health challenges across different levels of autistic traits, rather than clinical diagnosis only.

items.title: The ADHD Paradox: Why Are Recorded Diagnoses Rising? A Structured Narrative Review of Prevalence, Diagnostic Coverage and the Limits of the Current Evidence.
items.authors: Bonea M, Vamanu A, Fodor VB, Tecar C, Livinț-Popa L.

sections.text: Recorded diagnoses of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) have risen steeply in several healthcare systems, and the rise is read either as evidence that ADHD is becoming more common or that it is overdiagnosed. This structured narrative review examines how far the increase reflects underlying population prevalence and how far it reflects diagnostic coverage: recognition, referral, assessment capacity, thresholds and the incentives attached to a formal diagnosis. Evidence from prevalence meta-analyses, routinely collected healthcare data, national surveys, quasi-experimental studies and service reports was kept separate by the quantity each source estimates. The three quantities have diverged. Meta-analytic estimates of underlying prevalence cluster between 5.29% and 7.2% in children, with 5.9% in young people and 2.5% in adults; those that tested year of study directly report no temporal trend once diagnostic criteria, impairment requirements and information source are accounted for, while the others were not designed to detect one. Recorded diagnosis among UK boys aged 10-16 years rose from 1.4% in 2000 to 3.5% in 2018, and reached 1.19% across all ages in England in 2025, with incidence accelerating from 2020. Screen-positive reporting among English adults rose from 8.2% in 2007 to 13.9% in 2023/24. Recorded prevalence spans a 72-fold range, from 3.60% in males aged 18-24 years to 0.05% at 65 years and over, where the estimated coverage gap approaches 93.5%. The same divergence appears in Danish, Swedish, Norwegian and United States data. Definitional changes alone raise estimated prevalence by 27% to 47%. The increase is better read as a change in diagnostic coverage than in disease frequency, and overdiagnosis near the diagnostic threshold and under-recognition in the tail occur simultaneously, in different population strata.

items.title: Exploring Alcoholic Dementia: Integrated Bioinformatics of Alzheimer's Disease and Alcohol Use Disorder with Preliminary EGCG Evaluation.
items.authors: Lv MT, Li CX, Tu H, Han M, Zhang HT.

sections.text: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a major cause of cognitive impairment, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying alcoholic dementia remain unclear. Epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), the major catechin in green tea, has shown neuroprotective potential, but its targets in alcoholic dementia are undefined. This study aimed to explore disease-associated candidate molecular markers and potential EGCG-related targets in alcoholic dementia through integrated bioinformatics, machine learning, molecular docking, and experimental analyses. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) from GEO datasets GSE5281 and GSE62699 were subjected to functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis, and machine learning-based feature selection. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, immune infiltration analysis, molecular docking, and experimental assays were subsequently performed. We identified 60 overlapping DEGs enriched in synaptic signaling, postsynaptic structure, GABA-A receptor activity, and cytokine receptor activity. IL-1R1 and ID3 were identified as candidate genes associated with immune infiltration, and both were upregulated in the hippocampus of ethanol-exposed mice. These findings highlight IL1R1 and ID3 as exploratory candidate genes and provide a preliminary basis for further investigation of EGCG in the context of alcohol-associated cognitive impairment.

items.title: The associations between smart elderly care products use and patterns of mental health among older adults in China.
items.authors: Wang Q, Zheng C, Chen W.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study aimed to identify heterogeneous mental health profiles among Chinese older adults using latent profile analysis (LPA) and to examine the associations between smart elderly care product use and membership in these profiles.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We analyzed data from 9,836 adults aged 60 years or older who participated in the 2023 China Longitudinal Aging Social Survey (CLASS) and had complete data on the core variables. Latent profile analysis (LPA) was used to identify distinct mental health patterns among older adults based on the four mental health indicators. Subsequently, multinomial logistic regression was applied to examine the associations between smart elderly care product use and mental health patterns.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: LPA identified three distinct mental health profiles: Class 1 (Moderate psychological health pattern, 57.0%), Class 2 (High psychological health pattern, 15.3%), and Class 3 (Low psychological health pattern, 27.7%). Regarding product-specific effects, adopters of smart bands or smartwatches (OR = 1.56) and blood lipid monitors (OR = 1.33) had significantly higher odds of belonging to Class 1, while smart band or smartwatch use (OR = 1.53) and smart speaker use (OR = 1.47) were positively associated with Class 2. Cumulative use analyses showed that adopting two products was most strongly associated with both Class 1 (OR = 2.15) and Class 2 (OR = 2.92). Heterogeneity analyses further indicated that the associations varied meaningfully by urban-rural residence, though not significantly by age group.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Distinct mental health patterns are observed among Chinese older adults, and smart elderly-care product use is significantly associated with these patterns. This study provides evidence on the potential relationship between smart elderly-care product use and mental health among older adults and offers insights for developing technologies tailored to their needs.

items.title: 24-hour movement-behavior guideline attainment and school functioning in children with and without co-occurring ADHD and learning disability: evidence from the NSCH 2018-2024.
items.authors: Yang Z, Shao J, Shen Y.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Twenty-four-hour movement behaviors, including physical activity, recreational screen time, and sleep, have been linked to child health and functional outcomes. However, most studies have examined general populations or single-diagnosis groups. We examined the association between 24-hour movement-behavior guideline attainment and school-related functioning in U.S. children, using ADHD × learning disability (LD) cross-classification to distinguish the overall movement-behavior gradient from diagnostic differences in baseline functioning.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We analyzed pooled cross-sectional data from the 2018-2024 National Survey of Children's Health public-use topical files and included children aged 6-17 years. The survey was completed by parents or caregivers about selected children. Children were classified into four current ADHD/LD groups: neither ADHD nor LD, ADHD-only, LD-only, and ADHD + LD, with explicit handling of questionnaire-design skips and indeterminate current diagnostic status. The exposure was the number of 24-hour movement-behavior guidelines met, from 0 to 3. Outcomes were higher caregiver-reported school functioning and caregiver-reported school-initiated contact regarding school problems. Survey-weighted logistic regression models adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, family-structure, and survey-year covariates.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Among 209,556 age-eligible children, 206,636 had classifiable current ADHD/LD status. Adjusted analytic samples included 196,143 children for higher school functioning and 197,776 for school-initiated contact regarding school problems. Compared with meeting 0 guidelines, meeting 3 guidelines was associated with higher odds of higher school functioning (OR 3.87, 95% CI 3.50-4.28) and lower odds of school-initiated contact regarding school problems (OR 0.49, 95% CI 0.44-0.54). The favorable graded pattern for higher school functioning appeared across all four ADHD/LD groups, while the ADHD + LD group remained on the lowest functional baseline. A non-monotonic school-contact pattern in the ADHD-only group at 3 guidelines was treated as an exploratory subgroup signal requiring replication. Additional component-specific, pattern-based, original-category, and sequential-adjustment analyses did not materially alter the primary interpretation.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Greater 24-hour movement-behavior guideline attainment was associated with more favorable school-related functioning among U.S. school-aged children. ADHD × LD cross-classification added clinically relevant information by separating the overall movement-behavior gradient from persistent diagnostic differences in baseline school-functioning burden. Exploratory variation across strata should be interpreted cautiously.

items.title: Religiosity and obsessive-compulsive phenomena in Turkey: associations with obsessive beliefs and symptom dimensions.
items.authors: Erim C.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Leveraging Turkey's unique socio-cultural context, this cross-sectional study aimed to investigate the specific relationships between religious motivation, dysfunctional cognitive beliefs, and symptom dimensions in individuals with Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD) compared to healthy controls.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: The sample comprised 169 participants: a clinical group with primary OCD without current psychiatric comorbidities (n = 93) diagnosed via SCID-5-CV, and a healthy control (HC) group (n = 76). Participants completed the Motivational Religiosity Scale (MRS), Obsessive Beliefs Questionnaire (OBQ-44), and Padua Inventory (PI-WSUR). Group comparisons were evaluated using unadjusted t-tests and Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) adjusting for sociodemographic confounders (education, income, employment, marital status, alcohol use). items.title: Assessment of a discharge planning program on treatment adherence for inpatients with psychiatric disorders.
items.authors: Moghadam M, Sharifi V, Nabavi HR, Eftekhari F, Shams-Alizadeh N, Rahmani K.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Treatment adherence is a critical challenge in managing both physical and mental health conditions. For psychiatric patients, enhancing adherence significantly lowers readmission rates, thereby reducing healthcare costs and improving satisfaction levels among both patients and caregivers. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of a specifically designed discharge program on improving treatment adherence in severely ill psychiatric inpatients at an Iranian teaching psychiatric hospital during 2022.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This pre-post case-control study, conducted as a pre- and post-intervention design at the Psychiatric Teaching Hospital in Sanandaj, Iran, involved designing (based on literature review, hospital assessment, and an evidence-based model) and implementing a discharge program. It included adults (≥ 18 years) with schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, or bipolar disorder, divided into a control group (n = 133) and an intervention group (n = 136). The control group was sampled in the first quarter of 2022, and the intervention group was sampled in the third quarter of the same year. Participants were followed for six months post-discharge, with outcomes measured including treatment adherence (using the MMAQ-8 via phone at one month), attendance at the first scheduled follow-up visit (dichotomous, via phone at one month), and the number of readmissions (determined via hospital records within six months). Data analysis was performed using Stata version 16, employing independent t-tests, chi-square tests, and Fisher's exact tests.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Following the discharge plan implementation, the intervention group demonstrated significantly higher treatment adherence, a considerably higher rate of attendance at the first scheduled post-discharge visit, and a significantly lower readmission rate within six months compared to the control group (p < 0.001 for all outcomes).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Overall, the discharge program-rooted in patient and family education and implemented through collaboration between the treatment team and families-proved highly effective, significantly improving treatment adherence, boosting attendance at the first post-discharge visit, and reducing patient readmissions.

sections.heading: Registration reference
sections.text: IRCT20180114038350N4. Registration date: 2026-08-20.

items.title: Health impacts of climate change on children and adolescents: an umbrella review.
items.authors: Yahaya R, Alhassan SS, Ayebi-Arthur RS, Berchie RB, Ansah EW.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Climate change is a pressing global public health concern of the twenty-first century. Though the crisis affects everyone, its severity on children and adolescents is disproportionate. This umbrella review synthesized evidence from existing reviews on the impacts of climate change on children's and adolescents' health, identified vulnerability factors, and evaluated available public health interventions.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Following Arksey and O'Malley's framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, we conducted an umbrella review, searching five databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, JSTOR) and Google Scholar for peer-reviewed reviews published between January 2000 and December 2025. Four authors, supported by 10 graduate students, independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed quality using the AMSTAR tool. Thematic content analysis synthesized findings on climate exposures, health impacts, vulnerability factors, and interventions.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Twelve reviews (six scoping, three systematic, and three other types of review) were included from 1,962 initial records. Climate exposures affecting children and adolescents included extreme weather events, temperature extremes, air pollution, changes in disease vectors, and indirect exposures through food and water insecurity and psychological stress. Health impacts spanned mental, physical, and developmental domains. Vulnerability factors included biological susceptibility, socioeconomic disadvantage, and geographic location. Effective interventions included educational programs, mental health support, heat action plans, early warning systems, and climate mitigation policies that yield health co-benefits through improved air quality.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Climate change poses severe, immediate threats to child and adolescent health, disproportionately affecting vulnerable populations in LMICs. Evidence shows a triple burden: biological, socioeconomic, and geographic vulnerabilities compound to create cumulative health risks. Critical research gaps remain in LMICs, slow-onset exposures, intervention effectiveness, and standardized measurement tools. Urgent action on mitigation and adaptation is essential to prevent the reversal of decades of progress in child and adolescent health.

items.title: Gameful Digital Mental Health Interventions for University Students: Systematic Review and Three-Level Meta-Analysis of Package Effects with Component and Mechanism Evidence.
items.authors: Lu W, Shi S, Chen J.

sections.text: Gameful digital mental health interventions are increasingly used to support university students, but evidence for the effectiveness of complete intervention packages should be distinguished from evidence that specific game mechanics independently improve mental health outcomes. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the short-term package effectiveness of gameful digital mental health interventions for depression, anxiety, and stress/distress among university students, while separately examining active-comparator, component-level, and mechanism-oriented evidence to distinguish package effects from the incremental effects of gameful features and other intervention processes. We searched PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, CINAHL, CNKI, Embase, and APA PsycINFO (EBSCOhost) from database inception through 3 September 2026. Two reviewers independently screened titles/abstracts and full texts, with disagreements adjudicated by a third reviewer. Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2, and outcome certainty was evaluated with GRADE. Randomized package-effect trials were synthesized using outcome-specific random-effects models, and an integrative three-level model retained multiple symptom effects within studies. Dependence was examined using study-cluster robust inference and sensitivity analyses across plausible within-study sampling correlations. Component- and mechanism-oriented studies were synthesized separately from package-effect trials. Database searches identified 4267 records. Twenty-three reports were retained through the database pathway, and backward citation chasing identified 1 additional report, yielding 24 retained reports overall; 3 reports were not retrieved. Compared with inactive controls, gameful interventions showed moderate short-term effects for depression (4 studies; Hedges' g = 0.52, 95% CI 0.32-0.72) and anxiety (3 studies; g = 0.51, 95% CI 0.22-0.80), whereas stress/distress was highly imprecise (2 studies; g = 0.19, 95% CI -1.68 to 2.06). The integrative synthesis included nine symptom effects from five independent studies and yielded g = 0.410 (95% CI 0.245-0.575; study-cluster robust 95% CI 0.182-0.638), with a 95% prediction interval of -0.013 to 0.834, which includes no benefit and a small harmful effect in a future setting. Active-control effects were smaller in the full moderator model but were not leave-one-study-out stable. Expanded component and mechanism-oriented evidence did not show a consistent independent symptom benefit attributable to gameful features, although some studies reported differences in engagement, adherence, enjoyment, or related intervention processes. Gameful digital mental health intervention packages may reduce short-term depression and anxiety symptoms among university students, but certainty is low for depression and anxiety and very low for stress/distress; only five independent studies informed the integrative model. Generalizability across interventions and settings remains uncertain. Evidence against active comparators is sparse and unstable. Component and mechanism-oriented evidence indicates that gameful or contextual design choices may influence engagement, adherence, enjoyment, or training processes, but does not support a consistent independent symptom benefit from adding game mechanics. Future research should use meaningful active comparators and factorial or dismantling designs to identify which gameful features support therapeutic mechanisms, engagement, or potentially interfere with treatment processes.

items.title: Prediction Models for Suicidal Behavior Among Adolescent Students Based on Longitudinal Study Data: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.authors: Xu H, Sun Z, Jiang S, Liu Z, Yu C.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Suicidal behavior is common among adolescents, yet most affected individuals do not receive medical care. Predicting suicidal behavior in school settings may support early prevention.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We systematically reviewed longitudinal studies of machine-learning models predicting future suicidal behavior in adolescent students. Eight databases were searched through September 2026; risk of bias and applicability were assessed using PROBAST + AI. A bivariate random-effects model jointly pooled sensitivity and specificity and generated a summary receiver operating characteristic curve; study-reported AUCs were pooled separately as a supplementary analysis.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Seven models were included. Under the bivariate random-effects model, pooled sensitivity was 0.70 (95% CI: 0.52-0.83) and pooled specificity was 0.80 (95% CI: 0.71-0.87); the summary AUC was 0.83. The supplementary univariate analysis yielded a pooled AUC of 0.79 (95% CI: 0.75-0.83; 95% prediction interval: 0.63-0.89). Heterogeneity was substantial (I^2 = 95.5% for sensitivity and 99.1% for specificity). Exploratory subgroup and meta-regression analyses identified no statistically significant moderators, but the small number of models limited statistical power. All models were evaluated using internal validation and were judged to be at high overall risk of bias.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Current models show moderate discrimination, but their sensitivity remains insufficient for use as standalone early-warning tools. Because the synthesis was based on the final models selected by the original study authors, the pooled performance estimates may be optimistic.

items.title: Resource Loss, Loneliness, and Depressive Symptoms Among Middle-Aged and Older Adults During COVID-19: A Moderated Mediation Analysis and LLM-Based Computational Replication.
items.authors: Liu J, Ding P.

sections.text: Public health emergencies impose lasting mental health burdens worldwide. Conservation of resources (COR) theory suggests resource loss increases depressive symptoms, yet how multiple resources relate to depressive symptoms remains unclear. Using 8485 respondents from the 2020 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), we estimated a COR-guided moderated mediation model with robust OLS and bootstrap resampling. The 2018 data supplied baseline symptom information for agent initialization. Loneliness was examined as an indicator of relational deprivation and a statistical mediator. We also evaluated 300 DeepSeek-R1 virtual agents calibrated to the real data distribution to test whether large language model (LLM) agents could reproduce these associations. Higher work-time-change scores were associated with more depressive symptoms (B = 0.415, p < 0.001), whereas greater ease in making ends meet (B = -1.216, p < 0.001) was associated with fewer depressive symptoms. Loneliness was positively associated with depressive symptoms (B = 2.913, p < 0.001). Its interaction with intergenerational satisfaction was negative (B = -0.175, p = 0.015), and bootstrap intervals supported indirect associations that varied with relationship satisfaction. The agents reproduced several broad directions of association, but their score distribution and coefficient magnitudes differed from the survey data. These findings support a COR-guided statistical account of resource conditions during COVID-19 and identify the current limits of LLM-based computational replication.

items.title: Substantial Treatment-Seeking Interest, Narrow Eligibility: Diagnostic Heterogeneity and External Validity in the PRIDE Psilocybin Trial-Relevance to Precision Psychiatry.
items.authors: Inserra A, Persico L, Rosati A, Fabale M, Cavallotto C, D'Andrea G, Zoratto F, Pettorruso M, De Risio L, Ventriglio A, Bellomo A, Nicolò G, Martinotti G.

sections.text: Public and patient interest in psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy is increasing, but people seeking access to psychedelic trials may be more clinically heterogeneous than the populations these trials can enrol. We conducted a cross-sectional descriptive analysis of previously unreported aggregate telephone-screening data from the coordinating site of PRIDE, an ongoing Italian multicentre phase II randomized trial comparing psilocybin with personalized neuromodulation for treatment-resistant depression (TRD). Among 67 candidates screened between November 2025 and June 2026, 54 were excluded (80.6%), eight were enrolled and treated (11.9%), and five were preliminarily eligible (7.5%). The leading reason for exclusion was absence of protocol-defined TRD or another psychiatric diagnosis (27/54, 50.0%), followed by age outside the protocol range (18.5%), current suicidal or self-harm ideation (13.0%), and substance use disorder or dependence (9.3%). The diagnostic diversity of excluded candidates highlights the gap between a narrowly defined trial population and heterogeneous treatment-seeking individuals. These screening data do not address treatment response or individualized treatment selection, but they help contextualize recruitment yield and the external validity of psychedelic trials. Trial registration: Clinical Trials Information System, EU CT No. 2024-519844-34-03.

items.title: Who Benefits from School-Based Mindfulness? Attention-Related Moderators of Adolescent Intervention Response.
items.authors: Wang Y, Weng Y, Chen Z, Chen C.

sections.text: Although adolescence constitutes a malleable developmental window for mental health interventions targeting self-regulatory capacities, little is known about which adolescents benefit the most from widely adopted school-based mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs). This longitudinal study included 1307 Grade 10 students whose classes were randomly assigned to one of three conditions: an 8-week school-based MBI, an active control condition receiving mental health education, and a passive control condition. We tested whether baseline attention-related characteristics-mind wandering, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms, and cognitive disengagement syndrome (CDS)-moderated intervention effects on psychological distress, attentional control, and subjective well-being across baseline, post-intervention, and follow-up assessments. We further explored group differences in post-intervention cognitive control capacity (CCC) between the MBI and the active control groups. Results showed that higher baseline CDS was associated with greater reductions in psychological distress from baseline to follow-up in the MBI group than in either control condition, whereas ADHD symptoms showed a less consistent pattern and mind wandering showed little evidence of differential response. The CDS pattern weakened when the attention-related characteristics were considered together. Exploratory analyses also suggested higher post-intervention CCC in the MBI group than in the active control group. These findings highlight the value of considering attention-related individual differences to better understand variation in adolescents' responses to school-based MBIs.

items.title: Younger Among Peers, Higher at Risk? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of the Relative Age Effect on ADHD Diagnosis and Treatment.
items.authors: Luo Y, Liu B, Guo J, Hou Y, Lu J, Zhang F, Xie Y, Zhang Q, Tong HHY, Liang Y, Li K, Rao W.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Numerous studies suggest that relative age plays a significant role in child development and may influence the diagnosis and management of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). However, comprehensive research quantifying the association between relative age and ADHD outcomes remains limited. To address this gap, we conducted a meta-analysis to systematically explore the correlation between relative age and the diagnosis and treatment of ADHD.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A systematic literature search was conducted using EBSCO, Embase, Ovid, PubMed, and Web of Science. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated to assess the strength of the association between relative age and ADHD outcomes.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A total of 4404 relevant records were identified. Finally, 28 studies (across 31 reports) meeting strict inclusion criteria were selected for quantitative synthesis. The analysis revealed that children with a younger relative age faced a significantly higher risk of being diagnosed with ADHD (OR = 1.209, 95% CI: 1.044-1.400, p = 0.011). Furthermore, a statistically significant association was observed between relative age and the receipt of ADHD treatment (OR = 1.133, 95% CI: 1.031-1.245, p = 0.01).

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: These findings indicate that being relatively younger within a school cohort may increase the likelihood of an ADHD diagnosis, as well as the receipt of ADHD-related treatment. This review highlights the critical impact of the "relative age effect" and provides a theoretical basis for future research and the refinement of clinical diagnostic guidelines.

abstract.text:
Numerous studies suggest that relative age plays a significant role in child development and may influence the diagnosis and management of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). However, comprehensive research quantifying the association between relative age and ADHD outcomes remains limited. To address this gap, we conducted a meta-analysis to systematically explore the correlation between relative age and the diagnosis and treatment of ADHD.

A systematic literature search was conducted using EBSCO, Embase, Ovid, PubMed, and Web of Science. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated to assess the strength of the association between relative age and ADHD outcomes.

A total of 4404 relevant records were identified. Finally, 28 studies (across 31 reports) meeting strict inclusion criteria were selected for quantitative synthesis. The analysis revealed that children with a younger relative age faced a significantly higher risk of being diagnosed with ADHD (OR = 1.209, 95% CI: 1.044-1.400, p = 0.011). Furthermore, a statistically significant association was observed between relative age and the receipt of ADHD treatment (OR = 1.133, 95% CI: 1.031-1.245, p = 0.01).

These findings indicate that being relatively younger within a school cohort may increase the likelihood of an ADHD diagnosis, as well as the receipt of ADHD-related treatment. This review highlights the critical impact of the "relative age effect" and provides a theoretical basis for future research and the refinement of clinical diagnostic guidelines.

items.title: Peripheral S100B, Cell-Free DNA, and Circulating RNA Biomarkers in Psychotic Disorders: A Systematic Review of Schizophrenia-Spectrum Findings and Primary-Secondary Comparisons.
items.authors: Yuchshuk SA, Ilichev AB, Ponamareva OA, Lyubchenko MY, Shaymerdenova DS, Stupina TA, Mekhraliyeva LA, Yakovleva AS, Kenzhegulova AK, Shutilina NN, Zernayeva DS.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: Peripheral S100B, circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and circulating cell-free RNA (cfRNA)-related biomarkers have been investigated in psychotic disorders, but their relevance to etiological differentiation remains uncertain. This systematic review assessed patient-healthy-control comparisons and direct comparisons between primary and secondary psychoses. Methods: Five databases were searched through 11 October 2026 without publication-year or participant-age restrictions, and reference lists of six reviews were screened. The review followed a pre-existing protocol and was subsequently registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261437487). Results: Of 1262 identified records, 101 full-text reports were assessed and 36 were included: 23 investigated S100B, eight cfDNA-related measures, and five circulating microRNAs. An exploratory random-effects meta-analysis of nine serum S100B comparisons (340 patients; 305 controls) showed higher concentrations in schizophrenia-spectrum patients (Hedges' g = 0.78, 95% CI 0.32-1.24; I^2 = 80.5%), although the 95% prediction interval spanned zero (-0.54 to 2.10). Three total-plasma cfDNA effects (g = 0.35-1.12) were not pooled because of analytical heterogeneity and possible cohort overlap. Circulating microRNA studies examined distinct targets. Risk-of-bias assessment using review-adapted Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) tools identified recurrent concerns regarding biomarker measurement, residual confounding, and statistical reporting. Only two included cfDNA reports directly compared schizophrenia with alcohol-induced psychotic disorder; one reported an unadjusted area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.6684 without external validation. Conclusions: Neither S100B nor microRNA reports directly compared etiologies; clinical utility remains unestablished.

items.title: Effects of Cognitive Behavioral Interventions on Core Symptom Dimensions of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder in Children and Adolescents: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.authors: Guo X, Yang H, Liu Q, Lu C, Zhang T.

sections.text: Background: Previous research on psychosocial interventions for children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) has primarily focused on overall symptom severity, with less attention to treatment effects across core symptom dimensions. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effects of cognitive behavioral interventions on overall ADHD symptoms, inattention, and hyperactivity/impulsivity and explored the influence of intervention type, treatment duration, and weekly session frequency. Methods: PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to 30 June 2026 for randomized controlled trials. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2. Effect sizes were calculated as Hedges' g and pooled using random-effects models, with sensitivity and exploratory subgroup analyses conducted. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261376097). Results: Ten randomized controlled trials involving 849 participants were included. Cognitive behavioral interventions significantly reduced overall ADHD symptoms (g = -0.389, 95% CI -0.773 to -0.005), inattention (g = -0.415, 95% CI -0.749 to -0.082), and hyperactivity/impulsivity (g = -0.366, 95% CI -0.658 to -0.075). Inattention showed the numerically largest pooled effect. Exploratory subgroup analyses showed numerical differences across intervention type, treatment duration, and weekly session frequency, but formal moderator tests found no statistically significant between-subgroup differences. Conclusions: These findings support the potential benefits of cognitive behavioral interventions for ADHD symptom management, with the most consistent results observed for inattention. Future randomized controlled trials should compare intervention components and treatment schedules while assessing actual treatment exposure, including home practice, to inform more targeted cognitive behavioral interventions.
