items.title: Anxiety and Depressive Symptoms in Psoriatic Arthritis: Prevalence and Associations With Sleep, Lifestyle, and Inflammatory Markers.
items.authors: Rao VK, Charitha SM, Kothari S, Biswas M, N T, Patel R, Anand C, Gosavi S.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Anxiety and depressive symptoms are clinically important but frequently under-recognized comorbidities in psoriatic arthritis (PsA). We aimed to estimate the prevalence of anxiety and depressive symptoms in patients with PsA and to explore their associations with demographic, lifestyle, sleep, treatment-related, and inflammatory characteristics.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This single-center analytical cross-sectional study included 110 adults receiving treatment for PsA at a specialist rheumatology clinic in Bengaluru, India. Participants completed the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS). Scores of 8-10 and 11-21 on either subscale were classified as borderline and abnormal, respectively; a score of at least 8 was considered screening-positive. Clinical, lifestyle, treatment, baseline erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), C-reactive protein (CRP), and self-reported sleep data were obtained from the study dataset. Associations were tested using two-sided Pearson chi-square tests; exploratory paired sleep responses were assessed with the continuity-corrected McNemar chi-square test.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The mean age was 47.4 years (SD 13.7), and 67 participants (60.9%) were women. Twenty-nine participants screened positive for anxiety (26.4%; 95% CI 18.4-35.6), 22 for depression (20.0%; 95% CI 13.0-28.7), and 18 for both (16.4%; 95% CI 10.0-24.6). Baseline sleep disturbance was significantly more frequent among participants with depressive symptoms than among those without depressive symptoms (77.3% vs. 47.7%; Pearson χ²(1)=6.18; p=0.013). Sleep disturbance was also more frequent among participants with anxiety symptoms (69.0% vs 48.1%), although this association did not reach statistical significance (Pearson χ²(1)=3.72; p=0.054). In an exploratory retrospective self-reported comparison, sleep disturbance was reported by 53.6% of participants before treatment and 1.8% after treatment (continuity-corrected McNemar χ²(1)=55.02; p<0.001); this was not a formal prospective follow-up assessment.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Approximately one in four participants screened positive for anxiety and one in five for depression. Depressive symptoms were associated with disturbed sleep, whereas baseline ESR and CRP did not distinguish participants with and without psychological symptoms. Routine screening and multidisciplinary assessment may help identify unmet mental health needs in PsA; longitudinal studies with validated disease activity and sleep measures are required.

items.title: Disulfiram Repurposing Across Therapeutic Indications: Molecular Mechanisms, Evidence Appraisal, and a Systematic Review of Its Use in Lyme Borreliosis.
items.authors: Popovici V, Ciumasu-Rimbu M, Boca R, Ozon EA.

sections.text: Disulfiram (tetraethylthiuram disulfide, DSF), licensed for alcohol use disorder since 1951, is among the most studied drug-repurposing candidates and has been prescribed off-label for Lyme borreliosis since 2016. This hybrid review asks what supports that practice, appraising the Lyme evidence against disulfiram's record in other repurposing indications. We provided a narrative review of DSF and its bioactive metabolites' pharmacology, molecular targets, and toxicology. We also included a separate section systematically reviewing DSF in Lyme borreliosis following the PRISMA 2020 Guide. PubMed, Europe PMC, CENTRAL, bioRxiv, medRxiv, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception, while risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I, RoB 2, and SYRCLE; certainty was analyzed using GRADE. DSF is a prodrug acting through twenty-one documented targets, yet only alcohol use disorder rests on regulatory-grade evidence; oncology results are contradictory, and other indications remain preclinical. Nine primary studies addressed Lyme borreliosis, with five human reports contributing 96 participant entries and 93 unique individuals. Preclinical findings conflict, the largest dataset is uncontrolled, and the only randomized trial stopped early. Evidence on DSF repurposing shows strong preclinical support and small or inconsistent controlled results; a few well-powered randomized trials comparing it to standard care reported no clear benefits, but increased toxicity. In Lyme borreliosis, certainty of DSF benefits is very low, and certainty of dose-dependent harm is moderate, including one fatal outcome. No human study measured a microbiological endpoint, and all preclinical work used B. burgdorferi sensu stricto, leaving the evidence indirect for European genospecies.

items.title: Heterogeneous social capital patterns and mental health in older adults relocated for poverty alleviation: a cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Wang J, Feng H, Pang Y, Yao D, Yang L, Cheng J.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: The aim of this study was to identify distinct profiles of social capital across of levels of family, kinship and friend, and community among poverty-alleviation relocated (PAR) older adults and to explore their associations with mental health status (depressive symptom and life satisfaction).

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A total of 1,8,155,115 older adults were included in the final analysis, drawn from an initial sample of 1,882 selected participants were surveyed by using a multi-stage stratified sampling method in Shanxi Province, China, under in a cross-sectional study design. Latent profile analysis (LPA) was conducted using six social capital-related variables. Linear regression models were applied to examine the independent associations between social capital profiles, depressive symptoms, and life satisfaction after adjusting for sociodemographic characteristics, chronic disease status and health-related behaviors.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The LPA identified the model with three social capital profiles as being most optimal. The profiles were named highly integrated (29%), moderately adapted (58%), and generally weak (13%). Compared to the moderately adapted group, the highly integrated group reported significantly lower depressive symptom scores and higher life satisfaction scores, whereas the generally weak group exhibited showed the poorest mental health outcomes. Significant intergroup differences in education, chronic disease, physical activity and drinking behavior were observed.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Distinct latent social capital profiles exist among relocated older adults. Social capital stratification is closely linked to depressive symptoms and life satisfaction, reflecting forming evident mental health inequalities differential vulnerability. Targeted interventions tailored to heterogeneous social capital groups may be are urgently needed to strengthen support social capital reconstruction, improve mental health, and promote community adaptation among relocated older adults.

items.title: Comparative Efficacy and Acceptability of Psychological and Virtual Reality-Based Interventions for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
items.authors: Cheong MJ, Lee DE, Kang HW.

sections.text: Background: Virtual reality exposure therapy (VRET) may support engagement in trauma-focused treatment, but its standing relative to established psychotherapies for post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is uncertain. Methods: Six databases and other sources were searched through 30 July 2026 (PROSPERO CRD420261469444) for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in adults with PTSD. Post-treatment symptom severity was synthesized as standardized mean differences (SMDs) in a random-effects network meta-analysis; trial-defined dropout as odds ratios (ORs) versus prolonged exposure (PE). Results: Of 6028 records, 166 reports (165 studies) were included; 48 RCTs (73 contrasts, 33 nodes) entered the symptom network; the others lacked compatible data or comparisons, and were synthesized narratively. VRET (5 RCTs, 209 participants; indirect evidence only) outperformed inactive control (SMD -1.20, 95% CI -2.07 to -0.34) and showed no statistically significant difference compared to PE (SMD 0.13, 95% CI -0.66 to 0.91) or other established therapies. Thirteen of the 19 nodes ranked above VRET were informed by a single trial. Across 12 RCTs (26 arms), dropout with VRET did not differ significantly from PE (OR 0.86, 95% CI 0.51-1.45), whereas written exposure therapy (WET) had lower dropout (OR 0.22, 95% CI 0.12-0.38). Heterogeneity was substantial (I^2 = 77%), and global inconsistency was present. Excluding three influential trials lowered the WET P-score from 0.637 to 0.389, after which global inconsistency was no longer detected. Conclusions: VRET outperformed inactive control (low certainty) but showed no statistically significant differences from established trauma-focused therapies in efficacy or dropout; equivalence was not tested. The current evidence is insufficient to position VRET relative to first-line therapies, in either direction.

items.title: Psychosocial Interventions in Reducing Anxiety and Depression in CABG Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
items.authors: Kılınç Zİ, Kılınç ND, Tümkaya S, Tümkaya MN, Kozan Çıkırıkçı EH, Kutlu O.

sections.heading: Background and objectives
sections.text: Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is associated with substantial psychological distress, including anxiety and depression, which can impair postoperative recovery. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effectiveness of psychosocial interventions in reducing anxiety and depression in patients undergoing CABG.

sections.heading: Materials and methods
sections.text: The review followed the PRISMA 2020 statement and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251022254). Six databases were searched for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published in English between 1 January 2015 and June 2025. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. Hedges' g was pooled using a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model, with one independent estimate per trial and outcome.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Six reports of five RCTs (947 unique participants) met the inclusion criteria; two reports described the same trial (PSY-HEART). Interventions included psychoeducation, web-based support, and multicomponent rehabilitation. In the meta-analysis of four trials, psychosocial interventions produced a small reduction in anxiety ( g = -0.30, 95% CI -0.50 to -0.10, p = 0.003; I ^2 = 37%), although this finding was not robust in all sensitivity analyses. For depression, only two trials could be pooled, and the effect was small and not statistically significant ( g = -0.29, 95% CI -0.60 to 0.01, p = 0.061; I ^2 = 50%).

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Psychosocial interventions may produce a small reduction in anxiety in patients undergoing CABG, although this finding is based on four trials and should be interpreted with caution. The evidence for depression is inconclusive. Larger, well-reported trials are needed before firm recommendations can be made; in the meantime, structured psychosocial care, in which nurses can play a central role, is a reasonable component of perioperative care and cardiac rehabilitation.

items.title: ApoE4 and Psychosis in Neurodegenerative and Non-Neurodegenerative Disease: A Scoping Review.
items.authors: Wasef V, Rashidi-Ranjbar N, Churchill NW, Fornazzari LR, De Luca V, Graham SJ, Munoz DG, Schweizer TA, Fischer CE.

sections.text: Psychosis is a neuropsychiatric feature found across neurodegenerative conditions including Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD). It is also a common feature in psychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia. The apolipoprotein E epsilon 4 (ApoE4) allele is an established genetic risk factor for AD that may also increase the risk of psychosis. However, evidence regarding the association between ApoE4 and psychosis remains unclear. This paper evaluates the relationship between ApoE4 carrier status and psychosis in both neurodegenerative (Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease) and non-neurodegenerative disorders (schizophrenia). Additionally it explores whether sex and zygosity modulate this association. A literature review of studies identified through PubMed and Scopus was conducted. Thirty-one studies were included that investigated the relationship between ApoE4 and psychosis in select neurodegenerative and psychiatric populations. Studies were included if they assessed ApoE4 status in relation to the presence, severity, or age of onset of psychosis. Among the 16 AD-focused studies, a positive association was reported in 11 while four showed no significant association and one showed an inverse correlation. ApoE4 carriers and ApoE4 homozygotes that were female were reported to have the strongest association. The three studies examining PD resulted in inconsistent findings limited by small sample sizes. Schizophrenia studies produced findings that were predominantly null or equivocal, with no clear evidence that sex or zygosity influenced outcomes. Notably, the risk was enhanced in female carriers and ApoE4 homozygotes. Overall, ApoE4 positivity appears to be most consistent in AD, whereas evidence in PD and schizophrenia ae heterogeneous and limited, precluding direct comparison. Some studies suggest that this relationship may be modified by sex and ApoE4 zygosity, with female ApoE4 homozygotes being particularly vulnerable especially in AD cohorts. Larger studies are needed to clarify the role of ApoE4 in psychosis, particularly in non-AD cohorts.

However, evidence regarding the association between ApoE4 and psychosis remains unclear. Additionally it explores whether sex and zygosity modulate this association. A literature review of studies identified through PubMed and Scopus was conducted. Thirty-one studies were included that investigated the relationship between ApoE4 and psychosis in select neurodegenerative and psychiatric populations. Studies were included if they assessed ApoE4 status in relation to the presence, severity, or age of onset of psychosis. Among the 16 AD-focused studies, a positive association was reported in 11 while four showed no significant association and one showed an inverse correlation. ApoE4 carriers and ApoE4 homozygotes that were female were reported to have the strongest association. The three studies examining PD resulted in inconsistent findings limited by small sample sizes. Schizophrenia studies produced findings that were predominantly null or equivocal, with no clear evidence that sex or zygosity influenced outcomes. Notably, the risk was enhanced in female carriers and ApoE4 homozygotes. Overall, ApoE4 positivity appears to be most consistent in AD, whereas evidence in PD and schizophrenia ae heterogeneous and limited, precluding direct comparison. Some studies suggest that this relationship may be modified by sex and ApoE4 zygosity, with female ApoE4 homozygotes being particularly vulnerable especially in AD cohorts. Larger studies are needed to clarify the role of ApoE4 in psychosis, particularly in non-AD cohorts.

items.title: Astrocytic Glutamate- and Potassium-Associated RNA Expression in Postmortem Depression Samples.
items.authors: Zhang J, Zhang X.

sections.text: Postmortem studies have reported altered astrocyte-associated RNA in depression, but its relationship with recovered cellular composition remains unclear. Public prefrontal single-nucleus data included 71 donors; a total of 30 depression cases and 32 controls met primary analysis criteria. After adjustment for batch and platform, SLC1A2 - SLC1A3 - GLUL expression was lower in cases (mean log_2 counts-per-million difference, -0.83; 95% CI, -1.28 to -0.37). Exploratory KCNJ10 - ATP1A2 - ATP1B2 expression was also lower (-0.76; -1.19 to -0.34). Both reductions exceeded changes in the original six-marker reference and an external 50-gene astrocyte reference. The indices remained correlated after adjustment for reference expression and astrocyte nuclear fraction (r = 0.48; 0.23-0.67), although comparable correlations occurred among 10,000 abundance- and detection-matched gene set pairs. Nuclear fraction adjustment attenuated diagnosis coefficients to -0.27 and -0.41, with intervals crossing zero; estimates also changed after excluding extreme fractions. Four tissue cohorts yielded negative estimates, with imprecise pooled effects: -0.42 control SD (-0.89 to 0.04) and -0.29 (-0.71 to 0.14). These findings describe relative reductions in selected astrocytic transcripts alongside differences in nuclear representation, with covariance comparable with that of matched gene sets. Suicide, tissue source differences and missing individual postmortem covariates limit attribution to depression and the separation of cellular regulation from sampling effects.

items.title: Risk and prevalence of non-suicidal self-injury in individuals with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.authors: Jan A, Ullah A, Sulthana H, Kumar S, Shabil M, Waheed B, Dubwa D.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is a significant public health concern and may be more common among individuals with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) because of difficulties with emotional regulation and impulsivity. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the prevalence of NSSI among individuals with ADHD and examine the association between ADHD and NSSI.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: PubMed, Web of Science, and EMBASE were searched from inception to June 1, 2026, for observational studies reporting NSSI outcomes among individuals with ADHD. Eligible studies used standardized diagnostic criteria for ADHD, including DSM-IV, DSM-5, DSM-5-TR, or ICD-10. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted to estimate pooled prevalence and odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Heterogeneity was assessed using the I^2 statistic.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Sixteen studies met the inclusion criteria. The pooled prevalence of NSSI among individuals with ADHD was 32% (95% CI: 22%-44%), based on 574 NSSI events among 2088 individuals with ADHD. The pooled OR for the association between ADHD and NSSI was 1.54 (95% CI: 0.84-2.82; p  = 0.158), indicating higher but non-significant odds of NSSI among individuals with ADHD. Considerable heterogeneity was observed in the prevalence analysis ( I ^2 = 94.4%), while moderate heterogeneity was present in the risk analysis ( I ^2 = 50.6%).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: NSSI is common among individuals with ADHD, affecting approximately one-third of this population. Although ADHD was associated with increased odds of NSSI, the overall association was not statistically significant, suggesting that ADHD may represent an overlapping vulnerability factor rather than a direct causal driver of NSSI. Routine screening for NSSI in individuals with ADHD may facilitate early identification and intervention. Future prospective studies using standardized assessment methods are needed to clarify the relationship between ADHD and NSSI and to identify the clinical and developmental factors that may contribute to this association.

items.title: Effects of Adjunctive Online Therapist-Guided Receptive Music Therapy on Quality of Life and Psychological Outcomes in Adults with Psoriasis: A Three-Arm Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.authors: Tarcau BM, Vata D, Popescu IA, Olinici DT, Postu A, Halip IA, Gheuca Solovastru DF, Mocanu M, Duca ST, Gaina MA, Solovastru LG.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: Psoriasis frequently impairs quality of life and mental health. Evidence for online therapist-guided music therapy is limited. This trial evaluated four weeks of individualized receptive music therapy added to treatment as usual (TAU), compared primarily with an audio-based active control added to TAU (TAU + AC). Methods: In this single-center, three-arm randomized controlled trial, 75 adults with moderate-to-severe psoriasis and psychological or quality-of-life burden were allocated 1:1:1 to TAU, TAU + AC, or TAU plus therapist-guided receptive music therapy (TAU + MT). The audio programs comprised 12 sessions delivered over four weeks. The Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI), perceived stress visual analog scale (VAS), Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) were assessed at baseline, at the end of the intervention, and 3 and 6 months after intervention completion. The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05894759). Results: At the 3-month follow-up, 63 participants (84.0%) were assessed. Compared with TAU + AC, TAU + MT produced lower adjusted scores for DLQI (difference, -1.52; 95% confidence interval [CI], -2.77--0.28; Holm-adjusted p = 0.034), perceived stress VAS (-0.84; 95% CI, -1.42--0.27; Holm-adjusted p = 0.014), GAD-7 (-1.31; 95% CI, -1.91--0.70; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001), and PHQ-9 (-0.68; 95% CI, -1.31--0.05; Holm-adjusted p = 0.036). A DLQI improvement of at least four points occurred in 59.1% and 45.0%, respectively. Conclusions: In this exploratory trial, therapist-guided receptive music therapy was associated with modest improvements in dermatology-specific quality of life and psychological outcomes compared with an audio-based active control. The strongest evidence concerned anxiety. The clinical relevance of the mean DLQI difference and the effect on clinician-rated psoriasis severity remain uncertain, and confirmatory trials are required before clinical efficacy can be established.

items.title: Patient-Reported Symptoms and Daily-Life Outcomes Approximately 30 Days After Psychiatric Discharge in Children and Adolescents with Physician-Recorded Depressive Disorders: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
items.authors: Cao Q, Li Y, Xu J, Zhang J, Zhou K, Li W, Zhang Y, Huang X, Li Y, Jiang L.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: Symptoms and daily-life outcomes after psychiatric discharge may differ from those near discharge. We compared these assessments in children and adolescents with recorded depressive-disorder discharge diagnoses. Methods: This retrospective cohort linked admission assessments, clinical records and electronic follow-up questionnaires from West China Hospital, China, during May 2025-August 2026. Participants were aged 9-18 years. Random-intercept linear mixed-effects models adjusted for age, sex and the corresponding admission score; paired analyses estimated within-person differences. Results: Of 333 participants, 243 contributed 400 observations to the main model. Among 265 participants with a fully elapsed day-30 window, 132 (49.8%) had a selected questionnaire. Only 81 of 333 participants had both peridischarge and day-30 assessments. The adjusted day-30 local Beck Depression Inventory (BDI)-based score was 7.10 points higher than peridischarge (95% confidence interval [CI], 4.37-9.83); the complete-pair mean difference was 6.54 points (95% CI, 3.25-9.84). Six secondary contrasts had false-discovery-rate-adjusted p values below 0.05; the functional-impact CI included zero. Conclusions: Scores were less favorable at approximately one month in available assessments, including higher depressive-symptom scores among observed pairs. Selective questionnaire availability limits generalization to the entire cohort. Without validated meaningful-change thresholds for the local measures, statistically significant score differences do not establish clinically important deterioration or diagnostic relapse.

items.title: Association Between Caregiver-Reported ADHD Symptom Categories and Sleep-Related Quality of Life in Primary School Children: A Community-Based Cross-Sectional Study.
items.authors: Sritipsukho P, Kitthitima Y, Sritipsukho N, Chaiyakulsil C.

sections.text: Background: Sleep problems and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) can substantially affect quality of life (QOL) in children. This study aimed to assess sleep-related QOL using the scores from the caregiver-administered OSA-18 questionnaire among primary school children. The association between ADHD symptom screening categories and caregiver-reported sleep-related QOL, based on the scores, was also examined after adjustment for potential confounders. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among primary school students aged 6-8 years from 10 schools in Bangkok. A caregiver-administered OSA-18 questionnaire was used to assess sleep-related QOL, and the caregiver-administered SNAP-IV was used to screen for ADHD and classify children into ADHD symptom screening categories. Separate multivariable linear regression models examined the association between ADHD symptom screening category and OSA-18 total and subscale scores, adjusting for obesity status, sex, household income, caregiver-reported asthma, and caregiver-reported allergic rhinitis. Results: A total of 2263 children were included. Positive ADHD symptom screening results were identified in 4.8% for inattention, 2.1% for hyperactivity/impulsivity, and 3.2% for children exhibiting both inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity symptoms as mutually exclusive symptom categories. Compared with the ADHD symptom screen-negative group, children with inattention, hyperactivity/impulsivity, and combined symptoms had significantly higher OSA-18 total scores, with adjusted mean differences of 9.4 (95% CI, 6.9-12.0), 15.0 (95% CI, 11.1-18.9), and 19.3 (95% CI, 16.0-22.5), respectively (all p < 0.001). Similar significant associations were observed across all five OSA-18 subscales, with the largest adjusted mean differences generally among children with a positive screening for combined symptoms. Conclusions: Positive ADHD symptom screening results were significantly associated with higher OSA-18 scores reflecting greater caregiver-reported impact on sleep-related QOL, with the largest difference observed among children with positive screening for combined symptoms. The clinical significance of these score differences warrants further investigation.

items.title: Dental Scaling Within the Previous Year and Depressive Symptoms Among Korean Adults: A Nationwide Cross-Sectional Study.
items.authors: Cho BJ, Ahn JW, Ko JS, Kim SR.

sections.text: Background and Objectives: Dental scaling may be associated with mental health, but whether this reflects dental care itself or broader healthcare engagement is unclear. We examined the association between dental scaling within the previous year and depressive symptoms among Korean adults and its attenuation after sequential adjustment. Materials and Methods: We analyzed 231,410 adults aged ≥ 19 years from the 2024 Korea Community Health Survey. Scaling was self-reported; depressive symptoms were defined as a Patient Health Questionnaire-9 score ≥ 10. Survey-weighted logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Model 2 was the primary confounder-adjusted model, whereas Model 3 (exploratory attenuation model) was additionally adjusted for oral health, healthcare access, and general health. Sensitivity analyses included an alternative PHQ-9 threshold, expanded covariate models, multiple imputation, E-values, and restricted cubic splines. Results: Depressive symptoms were less prevalent among participants reporting scaling than those not reporting scaling (3.2% vs. 5.3%). The crude OR was 0.58 (95% CI: 0.55-0.61); the Model 2 OR was 0.74 (95% CI: 0.70-0.78) and was attenuated to 0.88 (95% CI: 0.83-0.93) in Model 3. Expanded models and multiple imputation yielded similar estimates. The Model 3 E-value was 1.54 (confidence-limit E-value: 1.36). With flexible modeling of age and sleep duration, the Model 3 OR was 0.93 (95% CI: 0.87-0.98). Conclusions: Self-reported scaling within the previous year was inversely associated with PHQ-9-defined depressive symptoms, with attenuation after additional adjustment and flexible modeling. The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, and these findings do not establish that scaling prevents or treats depressive disorders.

items.title: Eating Disorder Risk and Social Anxiety Symptoms in Young Adults: Differential Associations of Perfectionism, Avoidance, and Desire for Control.
items.authors: Triguero-López MJ, Moreno-García MI, Morales-Ortiz M.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: Eating disorder (ED) risk and social anxiety (SA) symptoms frequently co-occur in young adults, yet psychological processes associated with their co-occurrence may show different patterns of association with each symptom domain. This study examined maladaptive perfectionism, psychological avoidance, and general desire for control in relation to ED risk and SA symptoms and examined the residual ED-SA association in the joint structural model. Methods: Participants were 890 Spanish young adults aged 18-25 years (M = 20.02, SD = 1.94) recruited through convenience sampling from multiple educational institutions in a cross-sectional study. Participants receiving psychological or psychiatric treatment were excluded based on self-report. Structural equation models were estimated in an analytical sample of 705 participants using diagonally weighted least squares. Results: Maladaptive perfectionism was positively associated with ED risk and SA symptoms, whereas higher scores on reverse-scored avoidance and greater general desire for control were inversely associated with both outcomes. The standardised latent ED-SA correlation was 0.366 in the two-factor measurement model, whereas the standardised residual covariance was 0.199 in the five-factor structural model (both p < 0.001). The avoidance factor showed the strongest association with SA symptoms, whereas maladaptive perfectionism showed the strongest positive association with ED risk. Conclusions: Perfectionism, avoidance, and desire for control showed differential concurrent associations with eating-related and social anxiety difficulties, and a positive residual association between ED risk and SA symptoms remained in the structural model. These findings support the relevance of examining transdiagnostic psychological processes when considering the co-occurrence of eating-related risk and social anxiety symptoms in young adults. The cross-sectional design, self-report measures, and convenience sampling limit causal interpretation and generalisability.

items.title: The Role of Monoamine Oxidases in ADHD: A Narrative Review of Plant-Derived Inhibitors.
items.authors: Pietrasik D, Szwajgier D, Baranowska-Wójcik E.

sections.text: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is one of the most commonly diagnosed neurodevelopmental disorders, occurring in both children and adults, with its etiology and clinical presentation being multifactorial. Despite significant progress in diagnostics and treatment, available therapeutic strategies-particularly pharmacotherapy-are characterized by limited efficacy in some patients and the risk of numerous adverse effects. In recent years, natural bioactive compounds capable of modulating monoaminergic neurotransmission are gaining increasing interest; one of the mechanisms is the inhibition of the activity of monoamine oxidases (MAO-A and MAO-B), key enzymes involved in the metabolism of selected neurotransmitters. This paper provides a narrative review of the current state of knowledge on ADHD, covering its clinical characteristics, diagnostic process, currently used therapeutic methods, and the role of MAO enzymes in the regulation of central nervous system functions. Particular attention is devoted to natural MAO inhibitors, with an emphasis on plant-derived compounds. Due to the fact that the extraction and analysis of bioactive substances from flower petals remains a poorly explored area, this can be a significant research topic for developing new, potentially safer and better tolerated alternatives or adjuncts to conventional drugs used in ADHD therapy.

items.authors: Wessel Andersson H, Nordfjærn T, Loe H, Flemmen G, Mosti MP.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Treatment goal self-efficacy, defined as confidence in one's ability to achieve a specified treatment goal, has been linked to substance use outcomes following discharge from substance use disorder (SUD) treatment. Identifying factors associated with discharge self-efficacy may support more personalized treatment and strengthen relapse prevention efforts.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: To examine patient characteristics associated with discharge self-efficacy for achieving treatment goals of abstinence or reduced substance use among SUD inpatients.

sections.heading: Design
sections.text: Prospective cohort study including patients from two specialized inpatient SUD treatment units in Central Norway.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: The study included 236 patients who completed assessments at both intake and discharge. Predictor variables comprised SUD diagnoses, co-occurring psychiatric disorders, and psychological factors (self-control and psychological health). Hierarchical regression analyses were conducted to examine associations between these characteristics and discharge self-efficacy while controlling for baseline self-efficacy and demographic variables.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Baseline self-efficacy and demographic covariates explained 22.1% of the adjusted variance in discharge self-efficacy. An ADHD diagnosis and higher psychological health at baseline were independently associated with greater discharge self-efficacy. The final model explained 27.9% of the adjusted variance.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The findings underscore the importance of psychological health for patients' confidence in achieving treatment goals. Interventions targeting psychological well-being may strengthen treatment outcomes among SUD inpatients. The association between ADHD and higher discharge self-efficacy may reflect a positive illusory bias and warrants further investigation.

items.title: Polygenic risk score analysis for major depressive disorder in a Chinese cohort: single-phenotype and pathway-based approaches.
items.authors: Xu Z, Shao Y, Li Y, Liu R, Tang H, Cai Y, Dang X, Sun J, Zhang B, Chen B, Zhang Z, Yuan Y.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a global mental health challenge characterized by high prevalence, disability, and recurrence, with its susceptibility showing substantial polygenic inheritance. Polygenic risk scores (PRS) provide a novel method to explore cumulative polygenic effects on MDD pathogenesis.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Initial study inclusion comprised 721 patients meeting Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of the American Psychiatric Association, fourth edition (DSM-IV) diagnostic criteria for MDD and 960 healthy controls. Using summary statistics from the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium (PGC) East Asian cohort for MDD and schizophrenia (SCZ) phenotypes, as well as from the BioBank Japan (BBJ) for insomnia and body mass index (BMI) phenotypes as the base dataset, we performed stringent quality control (QC) on the data using PLINK v1.90. Subsequently, PRSice v2.3.5 with its PRSet function was employed to generate optimal PRSs for the four phenotypes in QC-passed patients and controls, and pathway-specific PRSs based on Gene Ontology (GO) gene sets. Statistical comparisons of PRS differences between MDD patients and healthy controls were conducted using independent two-sample t-tests or Mann-Whitney U tests in R v4.3.0. Furthermore, logistic regression analyses, adjusted for age, sex, and ancestry principal components as covariates, were performed to assess associations between phenotypic PRSs, pathway PRSs, and MDD status.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A significant difference was demonstrated in MDD-PRS between patients and controls (p < 0.001), with a significant logistic prediction model (empirical p = 9.999 × 10⁻⁵, pseudo-R² = 2.1%). In contrast, cross-phenotype PRS models did not reach statistical significance. Pathway analysis identified 16, 13, and 12 significant pathway PRSs in the Biological Process, Molecular Function, and Cellular Component GO subsets, respectively. Notably, most pathway PRS models exhibited greater explanatory power than the single-phenotype model.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: These findings support the predictive value of MDD-PRS and highlight how pathway-specific PRS may contribute to understanding of MDD's genetic basis, providing statistically prioritized pathways for future functional investigation.

items.title: Associations of cognitive beliefs and metacognitive processes with eating behavior in adults with obesity and healthy-weight controls: a cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Kayıkcı S, Gül A, Karakuş BS, Büyükkasap AÇ, Battal S.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Emotional and uncontrolled eating are common in obesity and may persist despite pharmacological or surgical treatment. Automatic thoughts and metacognitive beliefs may contribute to maladaptive eating, but have rarely been examined together while accounting for depression, anxiety, and stress. We examined whether metacognitive beliefs were associated with eating behaviors in adults with obesity and whether these associations differed from healthy-weight controls.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This cross-sectional study included 67 adults with obesity (body mass index [BMI] ≥ 30 kg/m²) from a psychiatric outpatient clinic and 70 healthy-weight hospital employees (BMI ≤ 25 kg/m²). Current DSM-5 psychiatric disorders were excluded using the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-5. Participants completed the Three-Factor Eating Questionnaire-21, Automatic Thoughts Questionnaire, Metacognitions Questionnaire-30, and Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21. Multi-group path analysis assessed direct and indirect associations, adjusting for age and sex. Indirect effects used 5,000 bootstrap samples, and selected coefficients were compared with Wald-type z tests. Because sample size was calculated for the primary group comparison rather than the structural model, path analyses were exploratory.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Participants with obesity had higher emotional eating (d = 1.05), uncontrolled eating (d = 1.10), automatic thoughts (d = 0.58), metacognitive beliefs (d = 0.55), and depression, anxiety, and stress scores (d = 0.69-0.96), whereas cognitive restraint did not differ (d = - 0.07). In the obesity group, metacognitive beliefs were associated with emotional eating independently of emotional symptoms (β = 0.46, p =.006); the corresponding association was not statistically significant in controls (β = -0.06, p =.688), and the between-group difference was significant. In controls, automatic thoughts were indirectly associated with uncontrolled eating through anxiety, although indirect effects were not formally compared. The principal finding remained after adjustment for education.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Metacognitive beliefs showed a selective association with emotional eating in adults with obesity. Most other associations were non-significant, and the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference. These findings require confirmation in larger longitudinal and interventional studies and do not establish metacognitive beliefs as a causal treatment target or the effectiveness of metacognitive therapy for obesity.

items.title: Coping with a planet in crisis: psychological distress and climate-policy-related conspiracy beliefs in youth.
items.authors: Phan D, Spirkl N, Kauk J, Asbrand J.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Adolescence and young adulthood are developmentally vulnerable periods in which climate-related distress may reflect environmental experiences, anticipated consequences, and social and cultural influences. Climate-policy-related conspiracy beliefs attribute climate policy decisions or scientific claims to concealed political or economic motives. However, their association with climate-related distress in young people remains poorly understood. This study examined whether psychological distress and eco-anxiety are associated with climate-policy-related conspiracy beliefs and whether meaning- and problem-focused coping moderates these associations.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A preregistered cross-sectional study was conducted in a German youth sample (N = 413; M_age = 20.26, SD_age = 2.77, age range: 15-25). Hierarchical multiple regression analyses examined associations between psychological distress (eco-anxiety, depression, anxiety, and stress) and climate-policy-related conspiracy beliefs, as well as the moderating role of meaning- and problem-focused coping. Exploratory analyses included hierarchical regression models controlling for general conspiracy mentality and belief in science.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Higher anxiety, depression, stress, and eco-anxiety were positively associated with increased climate-policy-related conspiracy beliefs. After controlling for conspiracy mentality and belief in science, only the cognitive components of eco-anxiety remained statistically significantly associated with climate-policy-related conspiracy beliefs. Meaning- and problem-focused coping showed positive main effects, but no statistically significant moderating effects.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Contrary to the hypotheses, coping showed no statistically significant moderating effects. The findings suggest that climate-specific, rather than general, psychological distress remained associated with climate-policy-related conspiracy beliefs beyond a general conspiratorial worldview. Further research is necessary to improve the understanding of how eco-anxiety and coping relate to climate-policy-related conspiracy beliefs, as this may help identify promising targets for preventive and psychosocial interventions to support young people during this critical developmental period.

items.title: Parental Control and Nonsuicidal Self-Injury Among Adolescents in China: A Latent Profile Analysis.
items.authors: Liu N, Xie Q, Shi R, Yue M, Li A.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Parents have a profound impact on the growth of adolescents, especially in terms of their mental health. Parental control is a key parenting dimension comprising two forms: behavioral control and psychological control. However, the relationship between different patterns of parental control and adolescent nonsuicidal self-injury (NSSI) remains underexplored. This study aimed to fill this gap by examining how various parental control profiles are associated with NSSI, with the parent-child relationship tested as a mediator.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Using a cluster sampling approach, a total of 4032 junior high school students were recruited from eight middle schools in China. A latent profile analysis was conducted in Mplus (Version 7.8) to identify patterns in two dimensions of parental control: behavioral and psychological. The PROCESS macro in SPSS (Version 26) was then used to test the hypothesized parallel mediation model, in which parent-child conflict and parent-child cohesion mediated the association between parental control profiles and NSSI.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Three psychological-behavioral parental control profiles were identified among the adolescent participants: low-moderate (40.67%), moderate-moderate (45.58%), and high-high (13.75%). Adolescents in the high-high profile reported higher NSSI levels than those in the other two profiles, whereas the NSSI levels did not significantly differ between the low-moderate and moderate-moderate profiles. Parental control was associated with adolescent NSSI through the parallel mediation of parent-child conflict and parent-child cohesion. Using the moderate-moderate profile as a reference, the low-moderate profile was associated with lower parent-child conflict, whereas the high-high profile was associated with higher parent-child conflict and correspondingly higher NSSI levels.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The findings suggest that parental control is significantly associated with adolescent NSSI, with the co-occurrence of high psychological and high behavioral control being the primary distinguishing feature of the highest-risk profile. Parent-child cohesion and parent-child conflict played important mediating roles in this association. This study provides a scientific basis for selecting high-risk forms of parental control for targeted interventions to reduce the incidence of NSSI in adolescents.

items.title: The Self- and Parent-Report Versions of the Spence Children's Anxiety Scale: Internal Structure and Multi-Informant Construct Validity in Portuguese Adolescents and Their Parents.
items.authors: Vagos P, Felix D, Oliveira F, Silva JR.

sections.text: The Spence Children's Anxiety Scale (SCAS) and its parent version (SCAS-P) are widely used and psychometrically supported measures that contribute meaningfully to multi-informant assessment of adolescent anxiety. However, their internal structure and convergent validity within a multitrait-multimethod framework have not been examined. This study addressed this gap by evaluating the internal structure of the SCAS and SCAS-P in Adolescent ( n = 302; 12-19 years; 60.3% female) and Parent samples ( n = 314; 30-70 years; 83.8% female). The original six-factor model showed acceptable fit and was retained for both the SCAS and the SCAS-P measuring separation anxiety, social anxiety, obsessive-compulsive symptoms, panic/agoraphobia, generalized anxiety, and fear of injury. A nested Dyad sample ( n = 198) was then used to test the multitrait-multimethod construct validity of this model. Results generally supported multi-informant construct validity of the SCAS and the SCAS-P, though the specific perspective of each informant introduced substantial unique variance into the scores. Furthermore, the validity of specific dimensions was qualified: multi-informant convergence was limited for obsessive-compulsive symptoms, and generalized anxiety was insufficiently distinct from the remaining measures. Still, findings support the SCAS and SCAS-P as useful and flexible tools for assessing adolescent anxiety as reported by the adolescent and/or their parents, supporting the assessment of anxiety-related difficulties and providing a multi-informant understanding of adolescents' anxiety symptoms in both research and clinical contexts.

items.title: Explainable AI-Based Medical Image Segmentation and Radiomics for Brain Disorder Classification over Structural MRI.
items.authors: Alqahtani A, Zarafshan, Najam S, Shorfuzzaman M, AlHammadi DA, Almotiri J, Alonazi M, Jalal A.

sections.text: Neuropsychiatric disorders including attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), bipolar disorder (BD), and schizophrenia (SZ) exhibit significant clinical heterogeneity and overlapping symptom profiles, which severely limits the diagnostic specificity of conventional symptom-based assessments. While structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) provides objective insights into anatomical brain alterations, existing computational frameworks often rely on single-plane or binary patient-control analyses, lack anatomical interpretability, or risk data leakage through inconsistent validation protocols. To address these challenges, this study proposes a segmentation-guided AI framework for medical image processing and recognition that fuses FastSurfer-derived regional handcrafted features encompassing Fourier shape descriptors, two-dimensional wavelet and second-order local directional gradient pattern (LDGP) textures, and ROI-filtered XFeat keypoints with complementary multi-view (axial, sagittal, coronal) EfficientNetB0 deep representations extracted from whole-brain T1-weighted sMRI. The segmentation stage provides anatomically defined regions for radiomic feature extraction, while explainable representations maintain anatomical traceability. A key contribution of this work is its dual evaluation strategy within a unified structural feature space: it addresses both broad transdiagnostic four-class classification (Healthy Control (HC) vs. ADHD vs. BD vs. SZ) and focused binary patient-control contrasts (SZ vs. HC and BD vs. HC). To ensure rigorous evaluation, feature fusion, feature standardisation, Salp Swarm Optimizer (SSO) feature selection, hyperparameter selection, and early stopping are performed exclusively within the training partitions of a participant-level nested cross-validation (five outer and three inner folds), and held-out participants are used only once for evaluation. Evaluated on the UCLA Consortium for Neuropsychiatric Phenomics (CNP) dataset, the framework achieved 79.3% accuracy in four-class transdiagnostic classification. In focused binary tasks, the framework reached 84.3% accuracy for SZ versus HC and 82.7% accuracy for BD versus HC. These results indicate that combining segmentation-guided radiomic descriptors with multi-view deep representations provides a promising research framework for structural MRI analysis of neuropsychiatric disorders, while external validation is required before clinical application.

items.title: PHQ-9-Guided Ordinal Contrastive Learning for Severity-Aware EEG Depression Representation Learning.
items.authors: Elnaggar K, El-Gayar MM, Elmogy M.

sections.text: Electroencephalography (EEG)-based depression detection studies commonly reduce clinical severity scores, such as the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), to binary diagnostic labels, thereby discarding ordinal information that may be useful for representation learning. This study proposes PHQ-9-guided ordinal contrastive learning (CE+OC), a training objective that uses PHQ-9 scores as privileged ordinal supervision during training while requiring only EEG at inference. PHQ-9 severity distances guide contrastive pair selection and scale the embedding separation margin, using clinical distances to guide the latent EEG space without an explicit patient-ranking objective. The method was evaluated on the Multi-modal Open Dataset for Mental-Disorder Analysis (MODMA) using strict leave-one-subject-out cross-validation across 53 subjects with 128-channel resting-state EEG. The primary representation finding was improved full-cohort PHQ-9 recoverability: a cross-validated held-out PHQ-9 probe showed that CE+OC increased recoverable PHQ-9 rank correlation from 7.8% to 33.6% (paired two-sided permutation p=0.031), an absolute gain of 25.7 percentage points, and reduced mean absolute PHQ-9 error from 27.8% to 22.8% of the 27-point PHQ-9 range (18.1% relative reduction; paired two-sided Wilcoxon p=0.011; bootstrap 95% CI for Δρ: 3.0% to 49.6%). CE+OC also showed descriptive diagnostic differences on MODMA: AUC increased from 59.8% to 69.3%, balanced accuracy from 59.5% to 66.0%, specificity from 69.0% to 86.2%, precision for major depressive disorder (MDD) from 57.1% to 73.3%, and MDD-F1 from 53.3% to 56.4%. False positives decreased from 31.0% to 13.8% of healthy subjects, although sensitivity decreased from 50.0% to 45.8%. A separate LOSO diagnosis evaluation on the independently acquired Mumtaz cohort achieved an AUC of 85.1%; it provides secondary evidence that the pipeline is feasible in a second cohort, but it is not a cross-dataset transfer experiment. A true-diagnosis-only control achieved ρ=0.502 and MAE 2.142 points, and within-MDD probe correlation remained negative (ρ=-0.424). The findings support increased full-cohort PHQ-9 recoverability relative to CE-only, not established information beyond diagnosis; diagnostic difference intervals include zero, and the model is not validated for stand-alone screening.

PHQ-9 severity distances guide contrastive pair selection and scale the embedding separation margin, using clinical distances to guide the latent EEG space without an explicit patient-ranking objective. The method was evaluated on the Multi-modal Open Dataset for Mental-Disorder Analysis (MODMA) using strict leave-one-subject-out cross-validation across 53 subjects with 128-channel resting-state EEG. The primary representation finding was improved full-cohort PHQ-9 recoverability: a cross-validated held-out PHQ-9 probe showed that CE+OC increased recoverable PHQ-9 rank correlation from 7.8% to 33.6% (paired two-sided permutation p=0.031), an absolute gain of 25.7 percentage points, and reduced mean absolute PHQ-9 error from 27.8% to 22.8% of the 27-point PHQ-9 range (18.1% relative reduction; paired two-sided Wilcoxon p=0.011; bootstrap 95% CI for Δρ: 3.0% to 49.6%). CE+OC also showed descriptive diagnostic differences on MODMA: AUC increased from 59.8% to 69.3%, balanced accuracy from 59.5% to 66.0%, specificity from 69.0% to 86.2%, precision for major depressive disorder (MDD) from 57.1% to 73.3%, and MDD-F1 from 53.3% to 56.4%. False positives decreased from 31.0% to 13.8% of healthy subjects, although sensitivity decreased from 50.0% to 45.8%. A separate LOSO diagnosis evaluation on the independently acquired Mumtaz cohort achieved an AUC of 85.1%; it provides secondary evidence that the pipeline is feasible in a second cohort, but it is not a cross-dataset transfer experiment. A true-diagnosis-only control achieved ρ=0.502 and MAE 2.142 points, and within-MDD probe correlation remained negative (ρ=-0.424). The findings support increased full-cohort PHQ-9 recoverability relative to CE-only, not established information beyond diagnosis; diagnostic difference intervals include zero, and the model is not validated for stand-alone screening.

items.title: Baclofen at the Crossroads: Pharmacological Ambivalence in Multiple Sclerosis and Alcohol Use Disorder.
items.authors: Schiavon C, Silva FAM, Rodrigues CF.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: Baclofen, a GABA_B receptor agonist, has been a cornerstone in the management of spasticity in multiple sclerosis (MS) for decades, and its repositioning at high doses for alcohol use disorder (AUD) has generated clinical and ethical debate. This narrative review examines the pharmacological, clinical, and safety ambivalence of baclofen across these two indications, comparing efficacy, dosing, and safety profiles, and investigating the "plasticity paradox": the possibility that baclofen facilitates remyelination in MS while impairing motor learning and cognitive adaptation. Methods: The review draws on clinical trials, meta-analyses, cohort studies, regulatory guidance, and neurobiological research indexed in PubMed/MEDLINE and ScienceDirect (2015-2025), synthesized narratively around the two indications and their clinical overlap. Results: In MS, oral and intrathecal baclofen show a well-defined safety profile, with emerging evidence for neuroprotective effects on remyelination. In AUD, high off-label doses carry risks of toxicity, withdrawal, and cognitive blunting, with efficacy for craving reduction that remains context-dependent and debated. In patients with comorbid MS and AUD, the doses required for anti-craving effects may abolish the compensatory spasticity that preserves motor autonomy, creating competing therapeutic priorities. Conclusions: Baclofen therefore remains versatile but double-edged: indispensable for MS spasticity, yet requiring an individualized, risk-stratified approach in AUD. Selective GABA_B allosteric modulators may help resolve this therapeutic tension and represent a promising direction for future neuromodulation research.

items.title: Tryptophan-Based Imaging Agents for Major Depressive Disorders.
items.authors: Stauff E, Karimi H, Fu X, Kecskemethy HH, Averill LW, Yue X.

sections.text: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is one of the most prevalent mental diseases; early intervention and treatment are crucial. Unfortunately, the complexity of this disorder makes timely intervention challenging. A clear understanding of the biochemical mechanisms in depression will benefit the diagnosis, stratification, and treatment of prevalent mental disorders. One chemical pathway that has attracted interest is the kynurenine (KYN) pathway, which plays several complex roles in the human body, including regulating immune and inflammatory responses. Dysregulated tryptophan metabolism is widely involved in neuropsychiatric disorders, including depression. Decreased tryptophan and its metabolites and the imbalance between the neuroprotective and neurotoxic arms of the KYN pathway are consistently found in patients with major depression. Tryptophan-based radiotracers provide valuable information in studying whole-body tryptophan depletion-related depression and antidepressant mechanisms. Understanding the relationship between the peripheral and central KYN pathway and the biological mechanisms underlying the heterogeneous symptoms with functional imaging in depression is a pivotal part of enhancing potential patient stratification, developing effective diagnostic tools for subtypes, guiding personalized drug development, and improving treatment strategies. We review tryptophan-based radiopharmaceuticals in the study of depression. We summarize the key findings, noting both broad consensus and inconsistencies, as well as limitations. Finally, we offer our perspective on the future development of tryptophan radiopharmaceuticals in guiding depression diagnosis, targeted interventions, treatment evaluation, and drug development in these prevalent mental disorders.

items.title: ADHD-Related Symptom Dimensions and Suicidality After Hospitalization for Bipolar Disorder: A Lebanese Cross-Sectional Survey.
items.authors: Hallal C, Kassab A, Louak M, El Toum Y, Abi Khalil L, Zahran F, Dirani E, Bou Khalil R.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)-related symptoms overlap with bipolar presentations, but associations between individual ADHD-related symptom dimensions and suicidality remain uncertain.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: In this exploratory cross-sectional study, adults previously hospitalized for bipolar disorder at Hôtel-Dieu de France, Beirut, between 2017 and 2025 completed a post-discharge online survey. Retrospective childhood ADHD-related symptoms were screened using the Wender Utah Rating Scale-25 (WURS-25), current adult ADHD symptoms using the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS), and suicidality using the P4 screener and reported previous suicidal behavior. Neither the interval since discharge nor current mood state was systematically assessed.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Forty-nine participants completed the survey (mean age 35.9 ± 11.9 years; 71.4% women). The composite suicidality outcome was present in 73.5%; 34.7% had a positive WURS-25 screen and 22.4% a positive ASRS Part A screen. Categorical ADHD screening positivity was not significantly associated with suicidality. Participants with suicidality were younger and more frequently reported increased alcohol or substance use since hospitalization. In exploratory age-adjusted models, the associations involving inattentiveness and impulsivity varied with the included WURS-25 subdimensions: higher inattentiveness scores were associated with lower odds of suicidality, whereas higher impulsivity scores were associated with higher odds when the negative mood subdimension was excluded.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: These preliminary findings highlight the potential clinical relevance of examining individual ADHD-related symptom dimensions alongside categorical screening results when investigating suicidality in bipolar disorder. However, the observed associations between retrospective ADHD-related symptom dimensions and suicidality in this small bipolar disorder sample were exploratory and sensitive to model specification. They require replication with larger samples, diagnostic ADHD assessment, and concurrent mood-state measurement.

items.title: Aberrant Regional Homogeneity in First-Episode, Drug-Naïve Adolescents with Major Depressive Disorder.
items.authors: Deng J, Yuan Y, Ling Y, Liu Y, Wang Y, Lu K, Zhou X, Yin Y, Qiu L.

sections.text: Background: Adolescent major depressive disorder (MDD) is common, but the neural mechanisms that underlie it remain poorly understood. Imaging work has been carried out mainly in adults, and data from adolescents with a first, untreated episode are still scarce. In this cross-sectional resting-state functional MRI study, we assessed spontaneous local activity using regional homogeneity (ReHo) together with caudate-seeded functional connectivity (FC), and related both measures to the clinical profile of first-episode, drug-naïve adolescent MDD patients. Methods: The sample comprised 31 adolescents with MDD (aged 10-19 years) and 25 age-matched healthy controls (HC). ReHo and caudate-seeded FC were computed for each participant, and we tested whether these measures were related to symptom severity on the 17-item Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression (HAMD-17). Results: Compared with HC, adolescents with MDD showed significantly increased ReHo in three clusters within a gray-matter mask (cluster-level p < 0.05, FWE-corrected): the right lingual gyrus, the left supramarginal gyrus, and the left insula. No region showed significantly decreased ReHo, and caudate-seeded FC showed no reliable group difference; the increases reported here are therefore presented as exploratory findings. Two regions showed a positive association with symptom severity that withstood Bonferroni correction: the left supramarginal gyrus (r = 0.51, p = 0.007) and the right lingual gyrus (r = 0.49, p = 0.009). Conclusions: In first-episode, drug-naïve adolescent MDD, exploratory analyses showed elevated ReHo in the lingual gyrus, insula, and supramarginal gyrus, pointing to altered synchrony of local BOLD signals in circuits supporting visual processing, interoception, and somatosensory integration. Caudate-seeded functional connectivity showed no robust group difference. Because the design was cross-sectional and the sample modest, these results await confirmation in larger, prospective cohorts.

items.title: Is Peripheral Nerve Hyperexcitability More Common in Adults with ADHD? A Hypothesis-Generating Perspective.
items.authors: Țocu L, Pleșea Condratovici A, Mihailov R, Ștefănescu BI, Luțenco V, Stavăr Matei L, Mihailov OM, Țocu G.

sections.text: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in adults involves heterogeneous alterations of catecholaminergic signalling and inhibitory motor control. Dopamine and gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) interact within cortical and subcortical networks, while transcranial magnetic stimulation studies suggest altered cortical inhibition in some ADHD populations. These observations raise a separate, unresolved question: could adults with ADHD have a higher prevalence of peripheral nerve hyperexcitability (PNH) than adults without ADHD? This perspective critically distinguishes central motor disinhibition from spontaneous peripheral motor-axonal activity and examines clinical phenotypes, electrophysiological findings, medication effects and rare genetic disorders. The literature identified provides indirect mechanistic support and isolated clinical observations but does not establish an increased prevalence of electrophysiologically confirmed peripheral nerve hyperexcitability in typical adult ADHD. Negative cortical findings, non-uniform GABA measurements and substantial confounding further constrain interpretation. Three alternative explanatory models are considered: independent coexistence, shared biological predisposition, and indirect influences mediated by treatment, sleep or stress. A testable research framework combines standardised clinical phenotyping with electromyography, peripheral nerve stimulation and, where feasible, complementary central and axonal excitability measurements. The epidemiological hypothesis must be tested before neurotransmitter mechanisms are inferred. Appropriately controlled studies, particularly involving medication-naïve adults, are required; the present hypothesis does not justify routine electrophysiological screening of all adults with ADHD.

items.title: Peritraumatic Distress, Dissociation, and ICU Memories in Relation to Post-Traumatic Stress Symptoms After Intensive Care.
items.authors: Polat S, Şahin ŞK, Hepsağ AE, Aybal E, Ünlü N, Esquinas AM.

sections.heading: Background/objectives
sections.text: Psychological symptoms are common after intensive care. Early distress, dissociation, and disturbing ICU memories may contribute to later post-traumatic stress symptoms. This prospective observational study examined these relationships in adult ICU patients.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Peritraumatic distress, dissociation, anxiety, depression, and ICU memories were assessed during the ICU stay. PTSD symptoms and HADS scores were assessed one month later. Sixty-eight patients were enrolled. Thirteen died before follow-up and two could not be reached. Follow-up data were available for 53 patients.

sections.heading: Result
sections.text: The mean one-month PCL-5 score was 16.1 ± 11.4. No participant reached the selected PCL-5 screening threshold of 47; this does not exclude clinical PTSD. Higher baseline PDI scores were associated with higher PCL-5 scores (r = 0.288, p = 0.037). Delusional ICU memories were also associated with higher PCL-5 scores (r = 0.326, p = 0.018). PDEQ scores were not significantly associated with PCL-5 scores. In the combined regression model, PDI, PDEQ, and delusional memories explained 17.1% of the variance in one-month PCL-5 scores (R^2 = 0.171, p = 0.028). No individual predictor was significant in the primary three-predictor model. In a post hoc exploratory model additionally adjusting for baseline anxiety and depressive symptoms, PDI ( p = 0.012) and delusional ICU memories ( p = 0.027) were significant. Thus, the individual associations differed according to model specification.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Early peritraumatic distress and delusional ICU memories may provide potentially informative indicators of subsequent post-traumatic stress symptom burden. These model-dependent findings require cautious interpretation and do not establish independent predictive utility.

items.title: Psychedelics and Psychedelic-Inspired Compounds for Substance Use Disorders: Are We Treating the Disease or Opening a Learning Window?
items.authors: Buciuc AG, Gold MS, Fuehrlein B.

sections.text: Substance use disorders remain a leading cause of preventable death, and existing care is better described as disease management than as cure. Medications for opioid, alcohol, and tobacco use disorders reduce substance use, and opioid agonist treatment reduces mortality, yet retention is poor and functional recovery is rarely measured. This review asks whether psychedelics treat addiction, or temporarily create a brain state in which treatment, learning, and recovery work differently. By evaluating each pharmacologically unique compound individually, we align cellular mechanisms, animal studies and human trial data across the full spectrum of substance use disorders. Relapse prevention is not a single construct: conditioned place preference, operant reinstatement, extinction learning, and clinical abstinence index different processes, and agreement at one level does not imply agreement at another. Translational concordance is therefore indication- and compound-specific rather than a class property, with the strongest human signals for psilocybin in tobacco and alcohol use disorders, though even the alcohol signal rests on two small randomized trials with discordant results. Risk is compound-specific too: ibogaine is gated by cardiotoxicity, and ketamine carries reinforcing properties and organ toxicity of its own. Plasticity is an opportunity, not an outcome.

items.title: The Muscle-Microglia Axis in Neurodevelopment: Exercise-Induced Exerkines as a Molecular Landscape with Therapeutic Potential for ASD and ADHD During Pubertal Transition.
items.authors: Wang X, Liu J, Li Y, Liu Y, Ji Y, Wang Y, Zheng M.

sections.text: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) are prevalent neurodevelopmental disorders in childhood and adolescence in which neuroimmune dysregulation and altered microglial function have been increasingly implicated, albeit with substantially different levels of human versus preclinical evidence. Preclinical (in vitro and rodent) studies indicate that contracting skeletal muscle secretes bioactive exercise-induced factors (exerkines)-including irisin, cathepsin B, lactate, and extracellular vesicles-that can directly cross or indirectly signal across the blood-brain barrier, modulate microglial inflammatory states, and support synaptic plasticity. However, whether this complete peripheral-to-central cascade operates to normalize synaptic pruning in children and adolescents with ASD or ADHD remains unconfirmed. In this review, we propose the developmental muscle-microglia axis as a hypothesis-generating conceptual framework and specifically focus on its intersection with pubertal maturation. We critically synthesize in vitro, animal, and human evidence on how key exerkines and multi-pathway brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) regulation may interact with surging sex hormones during the pubertal transition to influence microglial activity and neuroepigenetic states. Furthermore, we frame modality-specific exercise parameters (FITT-VP model) and multimodal wearable/biomarker closed-loop monitoring as candidate hypotheses and conceptual proposals for future clinical trials in youth with ASD and ADHD, while highlighting methodological limitations, safety considerations, and translational gaps.

items.title: The rs1030757 in GRID2 and Its Sex-Specific Associations with Checking, Hoarding and Neutralization Symptoms in Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder.
items.authors: Oliveira GDSR, Kohlrausch FB, Fontenelle LF.

sections.text: Background: Obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is a complex psychiatric disorder with a lifetime prevalence of about 3%. Because glutamate is thought to play a role in OCD, we investigated its relationship with DLGAP1 and GRID2, genes encoding a scaffold protein involved in glutamatergic signaling and a glutamate receptor predominantly expressed in the cerebellum, respectively. The present study aims to investigate the association of polymorphisms in the GRID2 (rs1030757) and DLGAP1 (rs9952159 and rs11081062) genes with OCD and its phenotypical characteristics. Methods: Case-control study including 200 OCD individuals and 203 healthy controls from the Brazilian population. The samples were genotyped using pre-designed TaqMan^® assays through real-time polymerase chain reaction. Results: No association was observed between the studied polymorphisms and OCD status. However, in a dominant model for the rs1030757 C allele in men with OCD, positive and statistically significant associations were observed with dimensions of hoarding ( p = 0.015, odds ratio (OR) = 3.059, 95% confidence interval (CI = 1.217-7.685) and neutralization ( p = 0.044, OR = 2.429, 95% CI = 1.014-5.815). An effect against checking symptoms in women was observed in both the dominant ( p = 0.029, OR = 0.252, 95% CI 0.068-0.932) and overdominant ( p = 0.006, OR = 0.239, 95% CI 0.082-0.697) models. Conclusions: Our findings reveal preliminary, nominal associations between GRID2 variation and specific symptom dimensions of OCD. Given the exploratory, hypothesis-generating nature of this initial mapping, future confirmatory studies with larger independent sample sizes are essential to validate these trends under strict multiple-testing corrections.

The samples were genotyped using pre-designed TaqMan^® assays through real-time polymerase chain reaction. Results: No association was observed between the studied polymorphisms and OCD status. items.title: Associations of BDNF and NTRK2 Polymorphisms with ADHD in Children with Prenatal Alcohol Exposure.
items.authors: Kukowka A, Białecka M, Rodak M, Malinowski D, Lewandowski K.

sections.heading: Background/objectives
sections.text: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and its receptor TrkB, encoded by NTRK2, are involved in neurodevelopment and may contribute to variability in outcomes following prenatal alcohol exposure. We investigated whether BDNF rs6265, BDNF rs56164415, and NTRK2 rs10868235 were associated with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children with confirmed high prenatal alcohol exposure (hPAE), and whether these associations differed across fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD) phenotype groups.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: The study included 270 children aged 4-17 years with hPAE, comprising 111 with previously established clinical ADHD diagnoses and 159 without ADHD. Participants were classified as having fetal alcohol syndrome (FAS), partial FAS (pFAS), or a non-FAS phenotype. Genotyping was performed using TaqMan real-time PCR assays. Additive genetic associations were evaluated using logistic regression adjusted for sex, FASD phenotype, and age modeled with natural cubic splines. Exploratory genotype-by-FASD phenotype interactions were assessed, with Holm correction for multiple comparisons.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: No statistically significant associations were identified in the adjusted additive models: NTRK2 rs10868235, per C allele (OR = 0.91, 95% CI: 0.63-1.31; p = 0.619); BDNF rs56164415, per T allele (OR = 1.20, 95% CI: 0.48-2.99; p = 0.701); and BDNF rs6265, per A allele (OR = 1.29, 95% CI: 0.79-2.09; p = 0.308). No statistically significant global genotype-by-FASD phenotype interactions were identified. In the pFAS subgroup ( n = 37), the NTRK2 rs10868235 C allele showed a nominal association with lower odds of ADHD (OR = 0.25, 95% CI: 0.07-0.92; p = 0.038), which did not remain significant after Holm correction (adjusted p = 0.114).

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: No statistically significant associations between the investigated variants and ADHD were identified in this hPAE cohort. Limited statistical precision precludes excluding modest genetic effects. The exploratory pFAS finding is compatible with chance and does not establish a phenotype-specific genetic association. Because all participants had hPAE, genotype-by-prenatal alcohol exposure interactions could not be assessed.

items.title: Bridging the Gap in Primary Care for ASD: A Parallel Cross-Perspective Analysis of Physician Self-Efficacy and Parental Perceptions.
items.authors: Domarecki P, Plata-Nazar K.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Autism spectrum disorder carries a psychiatric-comorbidity burden that, depending on the sample, reaches 70-83%-placing the condition at the center of routine child mental-health service delivery. Primary care physicians act as gatekeepers, care coordinators, and frequently the de facto first mental-health contact, yet the mental-health competencies they bring to consultations with autistic children have rarely been characterized in parallel with the perspective of parents. This study evaluated physician self-efficacy in such consultations and compared physicians' and parents' reports of physician situational anxiety and of the implementation of routine clinical strategies.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Two parallel, web-based surveys were distributed between October 2023 and February 2024 to PCPs ( N = 166) and parents of children with ASD ( N = 177) in Poland. Data evaluated demographics, situational anxiety, self-efficacy, and the frequency of utilizing specific autism-tailored clinical accommodations.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Among physicians, higher self-efficacy was associated with lower situational anxiety (ρ = -0.24, p = 0.002) and with more frequent use of clinical strategies (ρ = 0.41, p < 0.001). Physicians reported higher situational anxiety than parents attributed to them ( U = 8545.0, Z = -7.49, p < 0.001). Physicians' reports of routine strategy delivery exceeded parents' reports of receiving them in the three directly comparable domains of clinical strategy use, with a fourth, non-equivalent comparison also differing (physician confidence in adapting the clinical environment versus parental report of the frequency of sensory adjustments); the largest relative difference concerned family-centred needs ( OR = 3.94, 95% CI 2.06-7.54), followed by the discussion of social difficulties ( OR = 3.18), the tracking of ongoing external therapies ( OR = 2.70), and sensory accommodations in the medical setting ( OR = 2.44). Parental reports also highlighted significant organizational barriers, particularly in priority scheduling.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Physicians reported greater situational anxiety than parents perceived in them, and physicians' reports of routine strategy delivery consistently exceeded parents' reports of receiving them. Because the physician and parent samples were independent, these findings indicate different distributions of the two groups' reports rather than within-consultation disagreement. Optimizing primary care for the autistic community may require systemic reforms, standardized communicative checklists, and institutionalized accommodations-directions suggested by the observed pattern that were not tested in the present cross-sectional, self-report design and require future evaluation.
