items.title: Cross-Cultural Adaptation and Psychometric Evaluation of the European Portuguese PHQ-9 Modified for Teens in a Large School-Based Adolescent Sample.
items.authors: Lusquinhos L, Rocha ACM, Pinho LG, João AL.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: Depressive symptoms are a major public health concern during adolescence, and brief, psychometrically sound, culturally adapted instruments are needed to support early identification in school settings. Although the PHQ-9 has previously been validated in European Portuguese adult samples, adolescent-specific evidence for the PHQ-9 Modified for Teens (PHQ-9_T) remains limited. This study aimed to cross-culturally adapt the PHQ-9_T for European Portuguese adolescents and evaluate its structural validity, internal consistency, construct validity, and measurement invariance across sex in a school-based sample. Methods: A cross-sectional psychometric study was conducted among 1089 students aged 14-19 years attending Portuguese public secondary schools during the 2024/2025 academic year. Following a five-stage cross-cultural adaptation process, the sample was randomly divided into exploratory ( n = 554) and confirmatory ( n = 535) subsamples. Exploratory factor analysis used polychoric correlations and unweighted least squares extraction, whereas confirmatory factor analysis used WLSMV. Internal consistency, hypothesis testing for construct validity using the GAD-7 and CD-Quest-T, and measurement invariance across sex assigned at birth were also examined. Results: Exploratory factor analysis supported a unidimensional structure explaining 59.30% of the variance (factor loadings 0.717-0.824). Confirmatory factor analysis provided overall support for the one-factor model (CFI = 0.985; TLI = 0.981; RMSEA = 0.082, 90% CI [0.074, 0.090]; SRMR = 0.036). Internal consistency was high (α = 0.911; ω = 0.910). PHQ-9_T scores showed a strong positive correlation with GAD-7 ( ρ = 0.787) and a moderate positive correlation with CD-Quest-T ( ρ = 0.535) scores. Configural, metric, and scalar measurement invariance across sex was supported. Among participants with complete PHQ-9_T scores ( n = 1070), 41.3% scored within the moderate-or-higher symptom-severity range. Conclusions: The European Portuguese PHQ-9_T demonstrated evidence supporting structural validity, internal consistency, construct validity, and measurement invariance across sex in this school-based adolescent sample, supporting its use as a brief measure of depressive symptom severity within structured, multiprofessional school and community mental health pathways, rather than as a standalone diagnostic tool.

items.title: Factors Associated With Insomnia Among Medical Students Across Latin America During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Multicenter 2020 Benchmark Study.
items.authors: Valladares-Garrido MJ, Zila-Velasque JP, Zeta Solis LA, Rueda DA, Cómina Tamayo MJ, Jiménez-Mozo F, Peralta Chiguala CI, Valdiviezo-Morales CG, Benavides Alburqueque ES, Porras Núñez EC, Dominguez-Troncos H, Vera-Ponce VJ, Hernández-Yépez PJ, Valladares-Garrido D, Ordemar Vasquez PD, Pereira-Victorio CJ, Culquichicón C, Diaz-Velez C.

sections.text: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted medical education and mental health. This multicenter study examined factors associated with insomnia among medical students from 13 Latin American countries during the first pandemic wave. A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted using an online questionnaire. Insomnia was measured with the Insomnia Severity Index. Exposures included physical activity, eating disorder symptoms, burnout, resilience, smoking and alcohol risk, and sociodemographic, educational, and clinical variables. Prevalence ratios with 95% confidence intervals were estimated through regression. Among 2,019 students, the prevalence of insomnia symptoms according to the ISI cutoff was 46.9% (95% CI: 44.7-49.1). Higher prevalence was observed among students who reported being a son or daughter within their family, those with relatives diagnosed or deceased from COVID-19, prior mental health problems, eating disorder symptoms, or smoking risk. Lower prevalence was found among seventh-year students, those with children, those perceiving the pandemic as serious, and students reporting high physical activity or resilience. Almost half of medical students screened positive for insomnia symptoms during the early pandemic. Family COVID-19 impact, prior mental health problems, eating disorder symptoms, and smoking risk were associated factors, while advanced training level, parenthood, physical activity, and resilience were associated with a lower prevalence of insomnia symptoms. These findings provide evidence for sleep health in Latin American medical students and may guide post-pandemic comparisons and interventions.

items.title: Ibogaine and 5-MeO-DMT Treatment in Mexico: Adverse Events, Suicidal Ideation, Mental Health, and Psychological Flexibility Among United States Military Veterans.
items.authors: Davis AK, Sepeda ND, Armstrong SB, Douglas A, Lewis BR, Xin Y, Romanella T, Ellis S.

sections.heading: Background/objectives
sections.text: Retrospective survey and clinical chart review studies have demonstrated the real-world effectiveness of ibogaine and 5-methoxy-N,N-dimethyltryptamine (5-MeO-DMT) in addressing a range of mental health challenges among military Veterans in the United States (US), but no prospective research study has examined safety and effectiveness in this population.

sections.heading: Design/methods
sections.text: We prospectively followed Veterans (n=113; male=95%; Age=45.7 [SD=6.9]) planning to attend an ibogaine and 5-MeO-DMT treatment in Mexico to evaluate safety (i.e., adverse events and suicidal ideation), mental health outcomes (post-traumatic stress disorder [PTSD], depression, and anxiety symptoms; psychological flexibility) from baseline (i.e., pre-treatment) to 1-week, 3-months, and 9-months post-treatment, and to explore whether changes in psychological flexibility mediated relationships between acute drug effects and mental health outcomes.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Adverse events were transient and infrequent (4-9% per timepoint). Significant reductions in PTSD (η_p ^2 = 0.74), depression (η_p ^2 = 0.64), anxiety (η_p ^2 = 0.64), and suicidal ideation (η_p ^2 = 0.24) were reported from baseline through 9-months (all p s <.001), with improvements emerging by 1-week and largely remaining stable through follow-up. Acute psychedelic experience intensity predicted greater PTSD and anxiety reductions, and psychological flexibility mediated the relationship between acute effects and PTSD improvement.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Despite the lack of objective reports, data suggest ibogaine and 5-MeO-DMT treatment is experienced as safe and has potential to provide prolonged improvements in self-reported mental health conditions among Veterans, with durable effects for up to 9-months. Future randomized controlled trials with larger, more diverse populations are urgently needed before this treatment is made available in the US.

items.authors: Vedati S, Grossberg A, Navaratnam K, McCarragher R.

items.title: Neurobiological Mechanisms of Mental Disorders in Relation to Epilepsy: A Narrative Review.
items.authors: Que BJ, Lekatompessy JC, Idrus CL.

sections.text: Depression, anxiety and psychosis occur in people with epilepsy far more often than in the general population, and each can precede the first unprovoked seizure, which suggests shared neurobiology in addition to psychosocial reaction. This narrative review examined original human research published between 2016 and 2026, identified by keyword searching and selected purposively. Of eighteen included studies, thirteen provided direct mechanistic evidence, two provided prognostic clinical evidence and three were retained as adjacent evidence. Imaging findings differed by phenotype, with reduced network connectivity in depression and parietal grey matter and white matter changes in psychosis, but each phenotype was studied with different methods in small, separate cohorts. Peripheral brain-derived neurotrophic factor did not distinguish patients with and without comorbid depression and was strongly influenced by anti-seizure medication, which limits its biomarker value without excluding a central neurotrophic role. Serotonergic and hippocampal glutamatergic measures were associated with depression in single studies, and circulating cytokine findings were inconsistent in direction. Genome-wide analyses identified shared loci including SCN1A, Mendelian randomisation was consistent with major depressive disorder liability increasing epilepsy risk, and suicidality at diagnosis predicted treatment resistance. These findings generate hypotheses rather than establish mechanisms.

items.title: Identifying youth at risk for suicidal ideation using machine learning: Integrating clinical utility and model interpretability.
items.authors: Sim K, Bae SM.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: Using youth suicidal ideation classification as a clinically important case, this study aimed to classify concurrent suicidal ideation and examine the value of evaluating machine learning models across discrimination, calibration, clinical utility, and interpretability.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Data were drawn from Wave 7 (collected August-November 2024) of the Korean Children and Youth Panel Survey 2018, a nationally representative panel of Korean adolescents and emerging adults (N = 4,196). Five classifiers-logistic regression, elastic net, random forest, XGBoost, and support vector machine (SVM)-were developed using 18 bio-psycho-social predictors and compared across discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility within a sensitivity-prioritized selection framework. Probability calibration was assessed for all models, with selective recalibration applied where indicated; clinical utility was assessed using decision curve analysis, and interpretability was examined using Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). Reporting followed the TRIPOD+AI guideline.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The five classifiers achieved strong and broadly comparable discrimination (AUROC 0.93-0.94). The selected isotonic-recalibrated XGBoost model achieved a sensitivity of 0.93, a negative predictive value of 0.99, a balanced accuracy of 0.87, and consistent net benefit across clinically relevant screening thresholds. SHAP analysis indicated that influential predictors spanned all three bio-psycho-social domains, with depression emerging as the dominant contributor.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The findings support the importance of clinically meaningful evaluation of prediction models by jointly considering calibration, clinical utility, and interpretability rather than discrimination alone. Because all measures were obtained concurrently, the results should be interpreted as same-time-point identification of suicidal ideation rather than prospective prediction.

items.title: Lipopolysaccharide and cytokine levels differ by disease severity in major depressive disorder.
items.authors: Milasauskiene E, Burkauskas J, Jesmanas S, Gleizniene R, Borutaite V, Raskauskiene N, Skemiene K, Adomaitiene V, Gradauskiene B, Brown GC, Steibliene V.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Major depressive disorder (MDD) lacks established biological markers, although immune dysregulation and gut-derived inflammation have been implicated in a subset of patients; however, their diagnostic utility across levels of depression severity and impact of psychotropic treatment remain unclear.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This cross-sectional study examined circulating lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-10, IFN-γ) in 95 patients with MDD and 51 healthy controls (HC), evaluating their diagnostic utility across depression severity and the influence of psychotropic medication. Depression severity was assessed using the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale, with patients stratified into mild-to-moderate and severe groups.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Compared with HC, patients with MDD showed elevated LPS and TNF-α levels and reduced IL-10, while IL-6 and IFN-γ did not differ. A combined model including LPS, TNF-α, and IL-10 demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy for MDD (AUC = 0.778) and mild-to-moderate MDD (AUC = 0.818). TNF-α alone was the strongest predictor of severe MDD (AUC = 0.677), while LPS alone distinguished mild-to-moderate from severe MDD (AUC = 0.679). These associations remained significant after adjusting for age, sex, BMI, smoking status, and psychotropic medication use. LPS levels were higher in mild-to-moderate MDD during antidepressant monotherapy and lower with combination therapy regardless of severity.

sections.text: Mild-to-moderate MDD is associated with elevated LPS, reflecting gut-derived inflammation and a distinct subtype, whereas severe MDD is linked to TNF-α. These biomarkers may aid in distinguishing MDD subtypes and inform targeted therapeutic strategies.

This cross-sectional study examined circulating lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6, IL-10, IFN-γ) in 95 patients with MDD and 51 healthy controls (HC), evaluating their diagnostic utility across depression severity and the influence of psychotropic medication. Depression severity was assessed using the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale, with patients stratified into mild-to-moderate and severe groups.

LPS elevation was specific to mild-to-moderate MDD, whereas TNF-α was consistently elevated across all severity levels. TNF-α alone was the strongest predictor of severe MDD (AUC = 0.677), while LPS alone distinguished mild-to-moderate from severe MDD (AUC = 0.679). These associations remained significant after adjusting for age, sex, BMI, smoking status, and psychotropic medication use. LPS levels were higher in mild-to-moderate MDD during antidepressant monotherapy and lower with combination therapy regardless of severity.

Mild-to-moderate MDD is associated with elevated LPS, reflecting gut-derived inflammation and a distinct subtype, whereas severe MDD is linked to TNF-α. These biomarkers may aid in distinguishing MDD subtypes and inform targeted therapeutic strategies.

items.title: From tradition to performance and mental health: antidepressant, anti-fatigue, and neuropsychological mechanisms of ashwagandha, ginseng, and caffeine in physical and cognitive optimization.
items.authors: Wang Y.

sections.text: This comprehensive review synthesizes the ergogenic and neuropsychological effects of ashwagandha ( Withania somnifera ), Panax ginseng, and caffeine, focusing on their integration across peripheral performance and central fatigue frameworks. While the existing literature frequently evaluates these performance enhancing compounds in isolation, this study provides a novel, multi compound comparison that distinguishes it from previous work by simultaneously mapping central nervous system fatigue, neuropsychological mechanisms, and physical outcomes. Rather than assuming uniform positive effects, we critically analyze the inherent heterogeneity in current clinical and preclinical data, highlighting how physiological outcomes are strictly dependent on extract standardization, precise dosage, population characteristics, and environmental context. Specifically, the narrative moves beyond broad metabolic interactions to delineate concrete physiological pathways, including upstream hypothalamic pituitary adrenal axis regulation, central dopaminergic and serotonergic monoamine modulation, adenosine receptor antagonism, and the attenuation of localized neuroinflammatory processes. By stratifying these evidence based findings across distinct target populations, including competitive athletes seeking physical adaptations, occupational working adults managing high cognitive workloads, and clinical cohorts experiencing prolonged exhaustion or anxiety, this review bridges the gap between molecular neurobiology and applied human performance. Ultimately, we establish a rigorous translational framework that clarifies the distinct therapeutic windows, cross domain tradeoffs, and synergistic potentials of these agents for optimizing total physical and cognitive resilience.

items.title: Atomoxetine-associated Raynaud's phenomenon in children: an under-recognized risk of non-stimulant ADHD therapy.
items.authors: Mo W, Liu L, Cui Z, Li Y, Mao H.

sections.text: Raynaud's phenomenon (RP) is an increasingly recognized yet still underreported adverse effect of ADHD pharmacotherapy. Whereas stimulant-associated RP is well documented, atomoxetine-related RP has surfaced only in isolated pediatric cases, leaving a gap in our understanding of non-stimulant toxicity. This narrative review reports the first Asian pediatric case identified in English- and regional-language literature and synthesizes the global evidence base, integrating five pediatric cases, targeted literature retrieval, and disproportionality analyses of FAERS and WHO VigiBase. Atomoxetine carries a consistent pharmacovigilance signal for RP. Beyond the elevation of synaptic cleft norepinephrine, the five cases point to suspected contributors: plasma drug concentration, CYP2D6-mediated metabolic variability-particularly relevant in East Asian populations-and individual susceptibility with superimposed triggers. Onset latency is highly variable (hours to years), and the course in reported cases is milder and fully reversible, without digital ulceration, features consistent with, though not determined by, the sustained, gradual peripheral noradrenergic elevation produced by selective norepinephrine transporter inhibition, in contrast to the rapid catecholamine surges typical of stimulants. These findings call for longitudinal vigilance beyond the titration phase, prompt exclusion of secondary causes, and systematic pharmacovigilance reporting.

items.title: A comparison of identity development and mindfulness levels between adolescents with and without non-suicidal self-injury.
items.authors: Yazgılı Kahveci NG, Çuhadaroğlu FÇ.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is common but poorly understood in adolescence, and the relative contributions of identity development, mindfulness, family functioning, and comorbid depression to its occurrence remain unclear.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: In this cross-sectional study we compared these four dimensions in 118 adolescents aged 12-18 years recruited at a tertiary university hospital in Türkiye, in three groups: 41 with NSSI, 40 psychiatric controls, and 37 non-psychiatric outpatient controls. Participants underwent a semi-structured diagnostic interview and completed measures of identity development, mindfulness, and family functioning.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Adolescents who engaged in NSSI showed greater identity confusion and lower mindfulness than either control group, and identity confusion was linked to lower scores across all mindfulness facets. The NSSI group was also older, predominantly female, and had a substantially higher rate of depression than the psychiatric control group (63.4% vs. 25.0%). In a logistic regression model adjusted for age and sex, a current diagnosis of depression was associated with markedly higher odds of NSSI (adjusted odds ratio 6.5, 95% confidence interval 2.4-17.9), as was identity confusion (adjusted odds ratio 3.5, 95% confidence interval 1.3-9.3), although the estimate for identity confusion was attenuated when overall mindfulness was added. In an exploratory model of the mindfulness facets, higher non-reactivity to inner experience showed a weak inverse association with NSSI (odds ratio 0.90, 95% confidence interval 0.81-0.997), which we regard as hypothesis-generating.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Identity confusion and low mindfulness most clearly distinguished adolescents who engaged in NSSI from both control groups. The findings identify identity development and mindfulness, alongside depression and family functioning, as candidate targets for clinical assessment and future intervention research in adolescent NSSI, although the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

items.title: From cutting to ear piercing: evolution of self-injurious behavior in an adolescent with treatment-resistant bipolar disorder: a case report.
items.authors: Lv L, Guan MY, Zhang XY, Shen Y.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Bipolar disorder is frequently associated with non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI), the manifestations of which vary across the illness course. Ear piercing may represent a covert alternative form of self-injury with an NSSI-like function that is commonly overlooked in clinical practice; consequently, reports documenting this phenomenon remain scarce.

sections.heading: Case summary
sections.text: This report describes an 18-year-old female with treatment-resistant bipolar disorder whose self-injurious behavior evolved from wrist cutting to periungual skin picking and, ultimately, to 11 self-inflicted ear piercings within 48 hours, complicated by localized infection. The patient reported transient relief of agitation following these procedures, with no suicidal intent.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Repeated self-inflicted ear piercing within a short period, impaired behavioral control, disregard for infection risk, and use as an emotion-regulation strategy may be consistent with an NSSI-like pattern. Ear piercing may thus represent a covert NSSI-like substitute in some adolescents with bipolar disorder; however, such behavior should not be automatically classified as NSSI. Clinicians should maintain vigilance for this practice and carefully differentiate NSSI-like behavior from routine body adornment.

items.title: The Werther effect: media influence, psychosocial mechanisms, and suicide prevention (a narrative review).
items.authors: Erdem Z, Kaya D, Akpınar Ö, Keskiner FZ, Kaya K.

sections.text: Suicide-related media communication may contribute to both harmful and protective outcomes, depending on the characteristics of the content, individual vulnerability, and the broader communication context. The Werther effect describes increased suicidal behavior associated with certain forms of suicide-related media exposure, whereas the Papageno effect refers to potentially protective responses to narratives emphasizing coping, recovery, and alternatives to suicide. This narrative review critically synthesizes evidence concerning these contrasting effects, their proposed psychosocial mechanisms, and their implications for contemporary suicide prevention. Literature searches were conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science Core Collection, initially in July 2026 and subsequently updated in October 2026. Relevant historical publications and recent studies addressing digital communication, algorithmic exposure, and artificial intelligence were also considered. Evidence from traditional media research supports associations between particular reporting practices and subsequent suicide mortality, especially following highly publicized celebrity suicides. In contrast, experimental studies of recovery-oriented communication suggest favorable short-term psychological responses, although evidence of sustained behavioral benefits remains limited. Emerging research highlights the complexity of digital suicide-related communication, including algorithmically mediated exposure, real-time audience interactions, and the potential role of emotional contagion, although their specific contributions to suicidal outcomes remain uncertain. The clinical effectiveness and safety of artificial intelligence-based suicide prevention applications also remain insufficiently established. Interpretation of these findings is complicated by methodological heterogeneity, potential confounding, and differences in measured outcomes. Overall, responsible suicide communication should be integrated into comprehensive prevention strategies, with greater emphasis on evaluating clinically meaningful outcomes and distinguishing harmful exposure from protective communication.

items.title: Mental health, facial congruence, and social recognition after facial gender-affirming surgery: A mixed-methods study.
items.authors: Lins-Kusterer L, Celestino LDNS, Travenzoli IMA, Meneses JVL, Pimentel RFW.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Transgender women experience disproportionate mental health burdens related to gender dysphoria, social stigma, and barriers to gender-affirming care. This study examined the psychosocial and mental health impact of facial gender-affirming surgery using a mixed-methods approach within a public healthcare setting.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Between January 2024 and December 2025, we conducted a case series of eight transgender women who underwent facial gender-affirming surgery at a public university hospital in Brazil. Quantitative outcomes included the FACE-Q Satisfaction with Facial Appearance scale and the Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI), administered preoperatively and six months postoperatively. Qualitative data were collected through in-depth semi-structured interviews at follow-up and analyzed using thematic analysis based on Bardin's framework.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Quantitative analysis showed marked postoperative improvements in facial appearance satisfaction, with a very large within-participant effect size for the FACE-Q total score (Cohen's d_x = 7.68), alongside substantial reductions in anxiety symptoms measured by the BAI (Cohen's d_x = 2.76). Qualitative analysis identified six convergent themes, including facial appearance as central to gender recognition, cumulative facial-related stigma, anxiety and psychological distress, surgery as survival rather than aesthetics, transformation of self-image and everyday freedom, and the role of public healthcare and humanized care as social reparation. Narratives contextualized quantitative findings, highlighting reduced misgendering, decreased social avoidance, enhanced self-recognition, and increased social and professional participation.

sections.heading: Health equity implications
sections.text: Access to facial gender-affirming surgery within public health systems may contribute to improved mental well-being and social functioning among transgender women, supporting its role in addressing health inequities in gender-affirming care.

items.title: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy for Pregnant Women: A Scoping Review.
items.authors: Wu LY, Li S, Ruan JY.

sections.text: Background: Pregnancy represents a period of elevated vulnerability to psychological distress. Anxiety and depression affect a large proportion of pregnant individuals, and symptoms may persist into the postpartum period. Acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT), a third-wave cognitive behavioral therapy that aims to enhance psychological flexibility, has been increasingly adopted to improve psychological well-being in pregnancy. However, the existing evidence on the scope and characteristics of ACT-based interventions for pregnant women has not been comprehensively mapped. Methods: This scoping review adopted the five-stage framework proposed by Arksey and O'Malley and was reported following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. A comprehensive search of eight English and three Chinese databases was conducted from database inception to 30 September 2026. Studies evaluating ACT-based interventions targeting pregnant women were eligible for inclusion. Results: Fourteen studies published between 2015 and 2025, involving a total of 862 participants (mean age: 29.70 years; mean gestational age: 28.82 weeks), were included. Quasi-experimental designs were most common ( n = 8), followed by randomized controlled trials ( n = 4) and mixed-methods studies ( n = 2). Across the included studies, 24 distinct outcomes were assessed using 37 measurements. The most frequently assessed outcomes included pregnancy-related anxiety, coping strategies, psychological flexibility, and fear of childbirth. Findings suggested that ACT-based interventions may enhance psychological flexibility and alleviate psychological symptoms. However, considerable heterogeneity was observed in intervention characteristics and outcome assessment, alongside limited reporting of intervention development and treatment fidelity. Conclusions: ACT shows promise for promoting psychological well-being during pregnancy. Nevertheless, future research should prioritize well-designed randomized controlled trials, standardized intervention and outcome reporting, longer-term follow-up assessments, and transparent documentation of intervention development and fidelity to strengthen the evidence base, enhance reproducibility, and support clinical translation.

items.title: Mapping Suicidality Among Sexual and Gender Minority Adults in Thailand: A Network Analysis of Minority Stress, General Stress, and Interpersonal Factors.
items.authors: Matthews AK, Steffen AD, Kittiteerasack P, Elkefi S, Gumbs C, Rompala-Matthews E, Lelutiu-Weinberger C.

sections.heading: Background/objectives
sections.text: Sexual and gender minorities (SGMs) face elevated suicidality risk, yet underlying network structures remain unexamined. This study's purpose was to examine interrelationships among suicidality and other factors, integrating key constructs from Minority Stress Theory and the Interpersonal Theory of Suicide.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This cross-sectional study analyzed survey data from 411 Thai SGM adults assessing minority stress, interpersonal factors, and suicidality. A mixed graphical model was used to examine conditional associations among variables and estimated centrality indices to identify highly interconnected constructs within the network.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Participants reported a 19.0% prevalence of past-year suicidal ideation and a 13.1% prevalence of lifetime suicide attempts. Network analysis identified stress, social isolation, hopelessness, and loneliness as core correlates of suicidality, with stress being the most central. Victimization emerged as an important connection, connecting minority stressors with general stress and suicidality-related constructs. Outness was associated with lower loneliness and social isolation but also with greater victimization. Centrality analyses were stable, supporting the importance of stress, social isolation, and loneliness within the network.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Among SGM adults, minority-specific and general stressors, interpersonal disconnection, and suicidality formed an interconnected psychosocial network, with stress, social isolation, and loneliness showing the highest interconnectivity. Integrating both frameworks reveals how SGM minority stressors directly fuel core interpersonal suicide pathways, providing a theoretical bridge between identity-based stress and suicidal ideation. Targeting stress and isolation through interventions is critical to reducing suicidality.

items.title: Poorer Health-Related Quality of Life Is Associated with Psychological Distress in Women with Overweight and Obesity.
items.authors: Soto-Sánchez J, Filomeno-Nicolás EM, Fuentes-Salazar GS, López-Sánchez CA.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: Obesity is a multifactorial disease that affects both physical and mental health, deteriorating health-related quality of life (HRQoL). This is an exploratory cross-sectional study aimed to evaluate the association between HRQoL and psychological distress in women with overweight and obesity. Methods: This study included 128 women aged 18-44 years with a BMI ≥ 25 kg/m^2. Participants completed the Impact of Weight on Quality of Life-Lite (IWQOL-Lite) and Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scales-21 (DASS-21) questionnaires; anthropometric and biochemical measures were also assessed, and insulin resistance indices were calculated. Associations were evaluated using Spearman's correlation coefficients and linear regression. Results: Women with obesity exhibited significantly higher insulin resistance and lower HRQoL than those with overweight. This difference was particularly evident in domains such as physical function, sexual life, and public distress ( p < 0.05). Additionally, higher levels of depression, anxiety, and stress symptoms were consistently associated with a poorer quality of life in both groups (ρ = -0.434 to -0.625). Self-esteem, public distress, and work were the domains most strongly correlated with psychological distress, and these associations largely remained significant after Bonferroni correction. Waist circumference (WC) and hip circumference (HC) were associated with public distress among women with obesity independently of age ( p < 0.001), but not after further adjustment for BMI. No significant associations were found between central adiposity and DASS-21 subscales. Conclusions: HRQoL was associated with psychological distress in women with overweight and obesity, whereas central adiposity and surrogate measures of insulin resistance were not associated with DASS-21 scores. These exploratory findings serve to generate hypotheses and should be confirmed in longitudinal studies.

Participants completed the Impact of Weight on Quality of Life-Lite (IWQOL-Lite) and Depression, Anxiety, and Stress Scales-21 (DASS-21) questionnaires; anthropometric and biochemical measures were also assessed, and insulin resistance indices were calculated. Associations were evaluated using Spearman's correlation coefficients and linear regression. Results: Women with obesity exhibited significantly higher insulin resistance and lower HRQoL than those with overweight. This difference was particularly evident in domains such as physical function, sexual life, and public distress ( p < 0.05). Additionally, higher levels of depression, anxiety, and stress symptoms were consistently associated with a poorer quality of life in both groups (ρ = -0.434 to -0.625). Self-esteem, public distress, and work were the domains most strongly correlated with psychological distress, and these associations largely remained significant after Bonferroni correction. Waist circumference (WC) and hip circumference (HC) were associated with public distress among women with obesity independently of age ( p < 0.001), but not after further adjustment for BMI. No significant associations were found between central adiposity and DASS-21 subscales. Conclusions: HRQoL was associated with psychological distress in women with overweight and obesity, whereas central adiposity and surrogate measures of insulin resistance were not associated with DASS-21 scores. These exploratory findings serve to generate hypotheses and should be confirmed in longitudinal studies.

items.title: Protocol for a Double-Blind Randomized Pilot Trial on the Augmentative Effect of Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation Combined with Maintenance Medication in Adolescents with Major Depressive Disorder.
items.authors: Wang W, Luo X, Chen H, Qiu T, Li X, Zhang L, Jiang X, Wei Y, Wan N, Xu D, Wang T, Li X, Zhou X.

sections.text: Background: Adolescent major depressive disorder (MDD) is associated with substantial functional impairment and represents a major public health concern. Although pharmacotherapy and psychotherapy are established treatments, a considerable proportion of adolescents experience inadequate treatment response, adverse effects, or poor adherence. Transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) is an emerging non-invasive neuromodulation approach with potential therapeutic benefits; however, its feasibility, safety, and preliminary clinical effects in adolescents with MDD remain insufficiently investigated. This study will evaluate the feasibility, safety, and preliminary clinical outcomes of adjunctive tACS treatment in adolescents with MDD. Methods: This randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled pilot trial will enroll 30 adolescents aged 12-18 years with MDD, who will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive active or sham stimulation. Participants will undergo a 4-week intervention phase consisting of 20 stimulation sessions, followed by a 12-week follow-up phase, resulting in a total study duration of 16 weeks. Feasibility outcomes will include recruitment performance, treatment completion, and participant retention throughout the study period. Safety will be evaluated through systematic monitoring and recording of adverse events and serious adverse events. Exploratory clinical outcomes will include CDRS-R-defined response and remission, as well as changes in depressive symptoms, anxiety, suicidality, sleep quality, Clinical Global Impression scores, rumination, and health-related quality of life. Exploratory assessments will examine cognitive, neurophysiological, and behavioral changes associated with tACS treatment. Discussion: This pilot trial will provide preliminary evidence regarding the feasibility, acceptability, and safety of adjunctive tACS treatment for adolescents with MDD. The findings will help estimate potential clinical effects and inform the design of a future adequately powered randomized controlled trial.

items.title: Unique Associations of Childhood Trauma and Disgust Sensitivity with Disordered Eating Attitudes: A Structural Equation Modeling Study in Adult Women.
items.authors: Rabito-Alcón MF, Antuña-Camblor C, González-Vázquez A, Baile JI.

sections.heading: Background/objectives
sections.text: Childhood trauma is associated with eating psychopathology, but the psychological processes that may contribute to this association remain insufficiently understood. Disgust sensitivity, the predisposition to experience disgust in response to a range of elicitors, is an underexplored affective trait that has been associated with both developmental adversity and eating pathology. This study examined the unique associations of childhood trauma and disgust sensitivity with disordered eating attitudes in adult women, examining whether disgust sensitivity was associated with disordered eating attitudes beyond childhood trauma, and assessing whether these associations differed in relation to self-reported eating-disorder status.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: In this cross-sectional online study, 292 adult women ( M age = 37.13 years, SD = 10.34) were recruited without diagnostic pre-screening. Nearly half of the sample ( n = 134, 45.9%) reported a current ( n = 50) or past ( n = 46) eating-disorder diagnosis or self-identified as having an eating disorder without a formal diagnosis ( n = 38). Participants completed the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire-Short Form, the Multidimensional Disgust Sensitivity Scale, and the Eating Attitudes Test-26 (EAT-26). Structural equation models in which EAT-26 scores were regressed on latent trauma and disgust factors were estimated as the primary analysis, followed by sensitivity and secondary analyses.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The final model, which included two residual covariances added post hoc on the basis of modification indices, showed acceptable but not good fit (CFI = 0.939, RMSEA = 0.067, SRMR = 0.054). Childhood trauma (β = 0.26, 95% CI [0.10, 0.41]) and disgust sensitivity (β = 0.27, 95% CI [0.11, 0.42]) each showed a unique association with disordered eating attitudes, jointly accounting for 19% of the variance in EAT-26 scores. The two structural coefficients did not differ significantly in magnitude. Both associations were attenuated but remained statistically significant after adjustment for age, BMI, and self-reported eating-disorder status (β = 0.17 and 0.15), and within-group estimates were smaller and non-significant in the eating-disorder group. No specific maltreatment subtype or non-hygiene disgust domain added unique prediction beyond the general factors.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: In this cross-sectional sample enriched for eating-disorder history, childhood trauma and disgust sensitivity showed unique associations of similar magnitude with disordered eating attitudes, which were attenuated after accounting for eating-disorder status. Assessment of disordered eating may benefit from considering both developmental adversity and disgust sensitivity. Longitudinal studies with clinically characterized samples are needed to establish the temporal ordering and clinical relevance of these associations.

items.title: Exploring the Recurrence of Hazardous Drinking in Alcohol Use Disorders Through the Lens of the Theory of Planned Behavior: A Qualitative Study in China.
items.authors: Huang W, Chen J, Song C, Gu L.

sections.heading: Aim
sections.text: This study aimed to explore the experiences of alcohol cessation, recurrence of hazardous drinking, and prevention of such recurrence among Chinese individuals with alcohol use disorder (AUD), grounded in the theory of planned behavior.

sections.heading: Design
sections.text: A qualitative phenomenological study was adopted, with the theory of planned behavior as the theoretical framework to guide the exploration and thematic analysis of participants' subjective experiences.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Using purposive sampling, this study enrolled 11 Chinese male inpatients diagnosed with AUD and characterized by persistent harmful drinking. Insights were gathered via semi-structured interviews, followed by data analysis using Colaizzi's phenomenological approach.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Three primary themes emerged: (1) attitude (relief of negative emotions, tolerant views toward drinking in social contexts, and mental conflict); (2) subjective norms (family members' passive acceptance, Chinese drinking culture, peer influence, and information support from medical authorities); (3) perceived behavioral control (insufficient self-efficacy, limited treatment resources, and lack of emotional support).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Findings reveal that AUD individuals' decision toward drinking recurrence is shaped by their behavioral beliefs, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control. Thus, culturally sensitive care from mental health nurses, tailored family involvement, and targeted health education are critical to enhancing patients' self-efficacy and supporting their recovery.

items.title: NDUFV2P1, a Schizophrenia-Associated Pseudogene, Regulates Mitochondrial and Neuronal Function: Implications for Schizophrenia.
items.authors: Lapiro Y, Karry R, Binah O, Ben-Shachar D.

sections.text: Schizophrenia (SZ) is a severe mental disorder affecting emotion, cognitive and social functioning. Mitochondria, which are dysfunctional in the disease, are essential for neuronal function, synaptic plasticity and behavior, all impaired in SZ. A major driver of mitochondrial dysfunction in SZ is Complex I, particularly its NDUFV2 core subunit. We showed that NDUFV2 pseudogene ( NDUFV2P1; PG) is upregulated in brain and peripheral cells of SZ patients and inversely correlates with NDUFV2 expression in brain specimens and with mitochondrial respiration in Epstein-Barr-virus-transformed lymphocyte cell lines (LCLs). Recently, we reported that PG competes with NDUFV2 mRNA for binding to RNA-binding proteins. We hypothesized that PG is a biologically functional pseudogene that regulates NDUFV2 expression, thereby affecting mitochondrial function and neuronal activity. Accordingly, we modulated PG abundance in LCLs and rat primary cortical neurons. PG overexpression in healthy-derived LCLs impaired mitochondrial membrane potential (Δψm), network dynamics, and oxygen consumption, while PG downregulation in SZ-derived LCLs normalized these parameters. In rat cortical neurons, PG overexpression induced comparable mitochondrial disruptions alongside impaired synapse formation and reduced spontaneous neuronal firing. This study provides evidence for a cellular pathway through which PG interference with NDUFV2 leads to SZ-related mitochondrial and neuronal deficits and suggests therapeutic potential for PG downregulation in diseases with bioenergetic impairments such as SZ.

items.title: Surveillance of healthcare utilisation related to cannabis following the introduction of medical cannabis in Thailand.
items.authors: Sornpaisarn B, Dejkriengkraikul N, Thitipraserth W, Lamyai W, Lamyai W, Teerawattananon Y, Sornpaisarn S, Mitsungnern T, Pongpat W, Limjindaporn C, Wittayachamnankul B, Laohakul P, Angkurawaranon C, Hanvoravongchai P, Chunharas S, Rehm J.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Thailand introduced medical cannabis in February 2019. This study aims to monitor cannabis-related healthcare utilisation after this introduction.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A three-year surveillance system was established in 2021, comprising: (1) monitoring cannabis-related healthcare visits within the medical cannabis-service system and (2) assessing cannabis use outside of this system in psychiatric hospitals, youth detention centres, and emergency departments.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: During the first surveillance year (June 2021-May 2022), the Thai healthcare system rapidly expanded cannabis services, with 90.4% (95%CI: 84.4%, 96.4%) of hospitals providing medical cannabis clinics in 2022, up from just 2.8% in 2019. Nearly all providers followed clinical assessment guidelines, though about a third of them did not perform the recommended blood tests before prescribing. Of patients who received prescribed medical cannabis, 86.4% (CI: 81.4%, 91.3%) operated a vehicle within 12 h of cannabis use in the past three months. As well, 24.3% (18.5%, 30.1%) of juvenile detainees and 5.6% (4.6%, 6.5%) of the patients with psychosis admitted to psychiatric hospitals reported cannabis use in the past three months, predominantly of illegal forms like flowers (over 70%). No significant evidence of diversion of medical cannabis to these two vulnerable groups was observed during surveillance, with less than 2.5% in either group reporting using medical cannabis. The one emergency department sampled saw an average of 3.5 (1.4, 7.6) cannabis-related cases per month.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This pioneering surveillance project provides critical baseline data on cannabis-related health service utilisation in Thailand, following the introduction of medical cannabis. The findings highlight the need for ongoing, comprehensive monitoring systems to inform policy as recreational use becomes more prevalent.

items.title: Changes in Depressive Symptoms Across the COVID-19 Pandemic and Recovery Periods Among Korean Adults: A Repeated Cross-Sectional Analysis of KNHANES 2018-2024.
items.authors: Lee MH, Lee DY.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with changes in population mental health, but whether elevated depressive symptoms persisted during subsequent recovery periods remains unclear. This study examined changes in depressive symptoms before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic among Korean adults and explored whether temporal patterns differed by sex. Methods: Data were obtained from 21,228 adults aged ≥20 years who participated in the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES) in 2018, 2020, 2022, and 2024, representing the pre-pandemic, pandemic, early recovery, and later recovery periods, respectively. Clinically relevant depressive symptoms were defined as a Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) score ≥ 10. Survey-weighted analyses accounting for the complex sampling design was performed, including multivariable logistic regression and period-by-sex interaction analysis. Results: The weighted prevalence of depressive symptoms was 4.3% in 2018, increased to 5.3% in 2020, decreased to 4.7% in 2022, and was 4.3% in 2024, the same point estimate as in 2018. In the fully adjusted model, the odds of depressive symptoms were higher in 2020 than in 2018 (odds ratio [OR] = 1.316, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.056-1.641), whereas the estimates for 2022 (OR = 1.187, 95% CI: 0.945-1.490) and 2024 (OR = 1.125, 95% CI: 0.905-1.398) were not statistically significant. Weighted mean PHQ-9 scores differed across periods ( p = 0.037). Sex-stratified analyses indicated greater temporal variation among men; however, the period-by-sex interaction was not statistically significant ( p = 0.069). Conclusions: Depressive symptoms showed modest worsening during the COVID-19 pandemic, but no statistically significant differences from 2018 were detected in 2022 or 2024. Although temporal variation appeared more pronounced among men, the period-by-sex interaction was not statistically significant ( p = 0.069), and the observed sex-specific differences should be interpreted with caution.

items.title: Covitality in the Association Between Depressive Symptoms and Suicidality Among Italian University Students: A Cross-Sectional Study of Indirect Associations.
items.authors: Błońska K, Zdybek P, Geraci A, D'Amico A.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: University students may experience depressive symptoms and suicidality. Covitality-the combination of belief in self, belief in others, emotional competence, and engaged living-may be a relevant positive mental-health resource. This study examined whether depressive symptoms were indirectly associated with suicidality through covitality among Italian university students. Methods: A cross-sectional survey included 482 Italian university students aged 18-51 years (M = 21.2, SD = 4.48); 81.1% were women. Covitality was assessed with the Social Emotional Health Survey-Higher Education, depressive symptoms with the Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21 depression subscale, and suicidality with a seven-item self-report index adapted from the Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale screener (not used as a diagnostic interview). Structural equation modeling with 5000 bootstrap samples tested the indirect association. Results: The model showed good fit. Depressive symptoms were negatively associated with covitality and positively associated with suicidality, and covitality was negatively associated with suicidality. The indirect association through covitality was statistically significant and accounted for 16.3% of the total association; the estimate was similar without the non-suicidal self-injury item but not significant among complete responders. Conclusions: Covitality was statistically associated with suicidality and accounted for a small part of the association between depressive symptoms and suicidality. Because the data are cross-sectional, these findings do not establish mediation as a temporal or causal process. Social-emotional strengths may complement, but not replace, symptom-focused assessment in university mental-health and suicide-prevention research; longitudinal and intervention studies are needed.

items.title: Body schema distortion in adolescent patients with anorexia nervosa and depression compared to healthy controls.
items.authors: Beer CS, Martin F, Stemann C, Stemann K, Baumann P, Holtmann M, Diers M, Legenbauer T.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Body image distortion is a well-established key facet of anorexia nervosa (AN) and has also been found in patients with depression. However, research examining the body schema in both patient groups is scarce. While studies with adult participants indicate a distortion of the body schema in patients with AN, the present study is the first to explore this both in adolescent patients with AN and adolescent patients with depression.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Patients diagnosed with AN (n = 14), depression (n = 14), and a non-clinical control group (n = 13) were recruited from a child and adolescent psychiatric hospital and through social media. To explore the unconscious body schema, patients were told a cover story. The patients passed through a door-like aperture that varied in width depending on the individual's shoulder width. The minimum ratio of aperture width to shoulder width was defined as perceived body width. A one-way ANOVA was conducted to examine group differences.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Significant group differences emerged, with the strongest body schema distortion found in patients with AN compared to non-clinical participants. The differences were no longer significant after the inclusion of BMI age percentile and age as covariates. An initial association between body image distortion and body schema distortion was observed, but this association was no longer statistically significant after controlling for diagnostic group.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The present findings indicate pronounced body image distortion in adolescents with AN, whereas evidence for group-specific differences in body schema distortion was less robust after adjustment for age and BMI age percentile. Moreover, the initial association between body image distortion and body schema distortion was no longer statistically significant after controlling for diagnostic group, suggesting that this relationship should be interpreted cautiously.

items.title: The Double Burden of Malnutrition and Associated Factors Among School-Going Adolescents in Grand-Lomé and Kara, Togo: A Cross-Sectional Multistage Survey, 2025.
items.authors: Sadio AJ, Gbeasor-Komlanvi FA, Tchankoni MK, Fayeu C, Djarikaka N, Agbetoglo GA, Gabkiangbe I, Koglo G, Djeri M, Konu R, Atoun R, Adama OIW, Tchade E, Alfa AK, Agoro S, Belo M, Ekouevi DK.
items.journal: Journal of epidemiology and global health

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: The coexistence of thinness and overweight/obesity within a population, commonly described as the double burden of malnutrition (DBM), poses a public health challenge in low-income countries. Data on these forms of malnutrition among Togolese adolescents remain scarce. This study estimated the prevalence of thinness and overweight/obesity and examined associated factors among school-going adolescents enrolled in Grand-Lomé and Kara, Togo.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional study was carried out from February to March 2025. Adolescents aged 10-19 years were selected through multistage stratified random sampling. Body mass index (BMI) was classified using age- and sex-specific Cole cutoffs through age 18 years and WHO adult thresholds thereafter. Bayesian mixed-effects multinomial logistic regression models were fitted using MCMCglmm, with normal weight as the reference outcome. Associations were summarized as adjusted posterior odds ratios (aORs), 95% credible intervals (CrIs), and Bayesian posterior-tail probabilities (p).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Overall, 2,586 school-going adolescents (56.0% girls) were included; median age was 16 years (IQR: 14-17). Overall, 25.9% had either thinness (15.4% [95% CI: 14.1-16.9]) or overweight/obesity (10.5% [95% CI: 9.4-11.8]); overweight and obesity prevalences were 7.8% and 2.7%, respectively. Male sex was associated with higher odds of thinness (aOR: 1.52, 95% CrI: 1.16-1.99; p = 0.001) and lower odds of overweight/obesity (aOR: 0.34, 95% CrI: 0.24-0.47; p < 0.001). Each additional year of age was associated with lower odds of overweight/obesity (aOR: 0.79, 95% CrI: 0.70-0.89; p < 0.001). Overweight/obesity was associated with self-reported parental obesity history (aOR: 3.16, 95% CrI: 2.00-5.02; p < 0.001), potential presence of an eating disorder (aOR: 2.11, 95% CrI: 1.51-2.96; p < 0.001), higher systolic blood pressure per 10 mmHg (aOR: 1.23, 95% CrI: 1.05-1.45; p = 0.013), and higher diastolic blood pressure per 10 mmHg (aOR: 1.44, 95% CrI: 1.19-1.72; p < 0.001). Each one-category increase in the physical-education activity score was associated with lower odds of overweight/obesity (aOR: 0.90, 95% CrI: 0.82-0.97; p = 0.017).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Among school-going adolescents in selected schools in Grand-Lomé and Kara, thinness and overweight/obesity coexisted at the population level. The findings support strengthened school-based nutritional surveillance, promotion of physical activity, referral for potential eating disorders, blood-pressure monitoring, and family involvement in prevention. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify risk factors in this population.

items.title: Psychological Disorders and Vascular Ageing: Is There a Link?
items.authors: Makri F, Anyfanti P, Gkolias V, Ztriva E, Savopoulos C, Panagopoulou E, Triantafyllou A.

sections.text: Psychological disorders are highly prevalent in the general population and are associated with increased cardiovascular risk. Vascular aging is associated with changes in the mechanical and structural properties of the vascular wall, leading to the loss of arterial elasticity and reduced arterial compliance. Arterial stiffness (AS) is a powerful predictor of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality in the general population and in high-risk patients, independent of traditional cardiovascular risk factors. A comprehensive understanding of the association between mental health disorders and AS is critical to refine prevention and treatment strategies. The present review article aims to summarize studies examining the association between psychological factors and AS. Most relevant studies have focused on the association of anxiety and depression with AS, with fewer studies analyzing the impact of other, less common mental health disorders on AS. Although not all of them align, most studies point towards a significant link between psychological disorders and AS. While the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms are still not fully understood, the clinical implications of the observed association might pave the way for the development of novel preventive and therapeutic policies for patients with mental health disorders.

items.title: The Great Irish Hunger: The Mechanisms of Potatoes, Tryptophan, and Depression.
items.authors: Albedawe M, Gardner R, Keenan JP.

sections.text: The Great Hunger (An Gorta Mór) of 1845-1852 caused an estimated one million deaths in Ireland, and at least as many people emigrated. Before the blight, the rural poor lived mainly on a diet of potatoes and buttermilk, which supplied tryptophan, the amino acid involved in serotonin synthesis. After Phytophthora infestans destroyed the potato crop, relief came mostly as unprocessed Indian corn (maize). Maize protein is low in tryptophan, and its niacin is poorly absorbed. In those who contracted typhus, relapsing fever, or dysentery, inflammation may have redistributed part of the remaining tryptophan into the kynurenine pathway; this cannot be quantified for the population as a whole. A dietary reconstruction, reported here with its assumptions, parameter sources, and uncertainty ranges, estimates that the tryptophan supply fell to roughly one-eighth of its pre-1845 level at the height of the crisis and had recovered to about three-fifths of that level by 1859. This Perspective article examines historical evidence that recorded suicide and asylum admissions rose during and after the Great Hunger, series that are biased upward and cannot establish a rise in depression itself; current evidence on rates of depression in Ireland and among the Irish in Britain; and evidence from famines elsewhere linking prenatal undernutrition to affective disorders and to changes in the methylation of serotonin receptor genes. We propose that tryptophan depletion contributed to depression during the Great Hunger and may have increased the risk of depression in those born during and after it.

items.title: Affective Temperaments and Eco-Anxiety Dimensions: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.authors: Lombardo C, Scaramuzzino C, Arena F, Fabio RA, Picciotto G, Bitto F, Zuccalà F, Galletta C, Muscatello MRA, Bruno A, Turiaco F, Scavino G, Lukacs O, Mento C.

sections.text: Background and Objectives: Eco-anxiety is a growing psychological response to climate change, but individual vulnerability factors remain poorly understood. Affective temperaments may contribute to differences in eco-anxiety. Materials and Methods: This cross-sectional online study involved 209 Italian adults recruited between May and December 2024. Participants completed the Hogg Eco-Anxiety Scale and the short version TEMPS-A. Gender differences were assessed using independent-sample t -tests, and multiple linear regression analyses were performed to examine the associations between affective temperaments and eco-anxiety dimensions. Results: Regression models explained 16-22% of variance. Anxious temperament was the most consistent correlate, associating with affective symptoms, rumination, behavioural symptoms, and personal-impact anxiety. Cyclothymic temperament was associated with behavioural symptoms and personal-impact anxiety, but not rumination after correction for multiple testing. Other temperaments showed no significant associations. Females reported higher anxious temperament and personal-impact anxiety. After adjustment for age and gender, associations with personal-impact anxiety did not survive correction for multiple testing. Conclusions: Findings suggest that individual differences in eco-anxiety are associated with affective temperament, although the cross-sectional design and partial overlap between measures call for caution. Considering temperament may improve understanding of psychological responses to climate change and inform future preventive and support strategies.

items.title: Metabolic Signatures of Bipolar Disorder Through a Sex-Informed Lens: Emerging Biomarkers for Precision Psychiatry.
items.authors: Marano G, Valle EL, Di Giacomi O, Traversi G, Mazza O, Sani G, Mazza M.

sections.text: Bipolar disorder (BD) is a clinically heterogeneous condition for which diagnosis, prognostic assessment, and treatment selection continue to rely predominantly on symptom-based evaluation. Metabolomics offers a promising approach to biomarker discovery by capturing the downstream effects of genetic susceptibility, environmental exposures, lifestyle, disease activity, and pharmacological treatment. Studies using peripheral biofluids, post-mortem brain tissue, and in vivo neurometabolic measures have identified alterations involving lipid metabolism, amino acids, energy production, oxidative stress, one-carbon metabolism, tryptophan-kynurenine pathways, and the gut microbiota-derived metabolome. Reproducibility is limited, and the potential influence of biological sex is frequently neglected or treated merely as a statistical covariate. This narrative review critically examines emerging metabolomic and lipidomic biomarkers in BD through a sex-informed perspective. We discuss their potential applications in differential diagnosis, mood-state characterization, illness staging, prediction of treatment response, and identification of cardiometabolic vulnerability. Particular attention is given to sex hormones, reproductive transitions, body composition, immune-metabolic regulation, circadian biology, and sex-dependent pharmacometabolic effects. Major methodological limitations, including small samples, medication exposure, inconsistent mood-state characterization, and insufficient sex-stratified validation, are also considered. Integrating sex as a biological variable into longitudinal, multi-omic, and clinically deeply phenotyped studies may improve biomarker reproducibility and support more individualized approaches to BD.

items.title: Natural language processing application in electronic health records studies for psychosis: a systematic review.
items.authors: Ho RHL, Tsui HKH, Vann-Adibe S, Tsang WYV, Zhou H, So HC, Zhang Q, Chan SKW.

sections.text: Natural language processing (NLP) enables the use of electronic health records (EHRs) for psychosis research in real-world settings and develops precision psychiatry. We conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review of five databases from inception to 9 October 2025 and identified 62 eligible studies with over 1 million participants. Most studies (62.9%) used data from the UK Clinical Record Interactive Search (CRIS) platform. Methodologically, 37.1% applied dictionary-based NLP, 53.2% representation-based machine learning, 9.7% transformer-based NLP, and none applied generative large language models (LLMs). Clinically, 74.2% targeted symptom/information extraction, 19.2% classification, and 16.1% risk prediction. However, 56.5% studies self-reported limited generalizability, 32.3% reported data quality/collection challenges, and only two studies performed external validation. Despite promising proof-of-concept performance, evidence of real-world clinical utility remains limited. Current work remains concentrated on retrospective phenotyping within a single healthcare ecosystem. We highlight priorities for multi-system validation, temporal trajectory modeling, and responsible LLMs deployment in psychosis EHRs research.

items.title: Depressive, Anxiety, and Stress Symptoms and Associated Factors Among Adults with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Attending Outpatient Clinics in Kabul, Afghanistan: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.authors: Rasib AR, Naseri MW, Fawad A, Naseri S, Sarwari N, Fayaz S, Amiri GM, Ahmad Esmat H, Asif Aram M, Aziz Jabarkhil A.

sections.heading: Purpose
sections.text: This study aimed to estimate the prevalence and severity of depressive, anxiety, and stress symptoms and examine associated sociodemographic and clinical factors among adults with T2DM managed in outpatient clinical settings in Kabul, Afghanistan.

sections.heading: Patients and methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 400 adults with T2DM attending two outpatient clinics in Kabul, Afghanistan. Participants were recruited using consecutive sampling method. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire covering sociodemographic characteristics, diabetes-related clinical variables, and the Dari version of the 21-item Depression Anxiety Stress Scales (DASS-21). Psychological symptoms were assessed according to DASS-21 severity categories. Associations between sociodemographic and clinical characteristics and depressive, anxiety, and stress symptoms were assessed using chi-square tests and logistic regression.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Among 400 participants 54.0% were male. Depressive symptoms were identified in 72.0% of participants, anxiety symptoms in 67.8%, and stress symptoms in 48.3%. Female sex was associated with higher odds of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Diabetes duration ≥6 years was associated with depressive and stress symptoms, while HbA1c >7% was associated with depressive and anxiety symptoms. Diabetes-related complications demonstrated consistent associations with depressive, anxiety, and stress symptoms.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Depressive, anxiety, and stress symptoms were highly prevalent in adults with T2DM receiving routine outpatient diabetes care in Kabul. These findings highlight the importance of integrating psychological assessment into routine diabetes care in Afghanistan. Future multicenter, longitudinal, and intervention studies are needed to clarify temporal relationships and evaluate culturally appropriate models of integrated diabetes and mental health care.

items.title: Pharmacovigilance Signal Detection of Vortioxetine in Individuals Aged over 65 Years: A Disproportionality FAERS Analysis Versus Other Antidepressants.
items.authors: Chiappini S, Mosca A, Cavallotto C, Guirguis A, Corkery JM, Di Trana A, Vickers R, Harris DR, Pettorruso M, Martinotti G, Schifano F.

sections.text: Background: Recently, vortioxetine has emerged as a potential safe antidepressant alternative in the elderly population. Safety signals of vortioxetine were evaluated against other antidepressants in patients aged over 65. Methods: Data from the Food and Drug Administration Adverse Events Reporting System (FAERS) database were analyzed to identify potential safety signals by analyzing patterns and trends in adverse-event reports in which the drug was listed as the primary suspect, extracted up to February 2025. Report characteristics (sex, outcome, year, country, and indication) were described, and disproportionality analyses were conducted to compare vortioxetine adverse events between age groups (18-65 vs. >65) and versus other antidepressants. Results: Vortioxetine represented the primary-suspect antidepressant with reporting peaking around 2018. Age-stratified disproportionality analyses showed that older adults had disproportionate reporting of neuropsychiatric events, falls/trauma, cardiovascular rhythm disturbances, and electrolyte/metabolic abnormalities vs. younger adults, suggesting increased vulnerability to multisystem adverse outcomes. Compared to other antidepressants (SSRIs, trazodone, mirtazapine, SNRIs, and the TCAs amitriptyline and nortriptyline), the strongest disproportionality signals for vortioxetine were largely driven by mood-related ADRs, medication errors, and respiratory compromise terms. Conclusions: The findings represent pharmacovigilance signals derived from FAERS data and should be considered hypothesis-generating, requiring confirmation through further clinical and epidemiological studies.

items.title: An Exploratory Model-Informed Precision Dosing Strategy for Atomoxetine Treatment in Chinese Children with ADHD: Integrating Body Weight and CYP2D6 Pharmacogenetics Across Potential Real-World Clinical Scenarios.
items.authors: Fan L, Wu DD, Huang J, Li Y, Xu X, Wang J, Zhang YY, Liu QQ, Guo HL, Chen F.

sections.text: Objective: We aimed to develop and evaluate population pharmacokinetic (PopPK) models of atomoxetine incorporating clinically available patient information and to explore model-informed dose selection in Chinese children and adolescents with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Methods: This retrospective single-center study included a model-building dataset of 102 patients (247 concentrations) and a patient-level holdout dataset of 65 patients (65 concentrations collected approximately 2 h post-dose). A one-compartment model with first-order absorption and elimination was developed. Body weight (BW) and alternative representations of CYP2D6 genetic information-rs1065852 genotype, activity score (AS), and predicted phenotype-were evaluated. Monte Carlo simulations evaluated steady-state 2 h post-dose concentrations ( C _2h) across doses of 0.5-1.4 mg/kg/day; the model-informed dose was the lowest evaluated dose, achieving ≥75% probability of reaching the exploratory C _2h threshold of 268 ng/mL. Results: BW affected apparent clearance ( CL/F ) and volume of distribution, whereas rs1065852 genotype and AS additionally explained CL/F variability. In the holdout dataset, population predictions had limited bias (MdPE, 1.41-3.09%) but modest precision (MdAPE, 33.75-37.83%); CYP2D6 -informed models improved selected performance measures. Simulation-derived doses ranged from 1.0 to 1.4 mg/kg/day across subgroups. No evaluated dose achieved the probability of target attainment (PTA) criterion for AS = 2 at any BW, or for the CC+CT and AS = 1.5 subgroups weighing 17-<30 kg. Alternative K _a assumptions changed median C _2h by at most 3.99% and PTA by 3.58 percentage points. Conclusions: BW and CYP2D6 genetic information explained part of atomoxetine pharmacokinetic variability and influenced simulated concentration attainment. These model-informed findings are exploratory and require prospective, multicenter validation against efficacy, tolerability, and safety outcomes before clinical implementation.

These model-informed findings are exploratory and require prospective, multicenter validation against efficacy, tolerability, and safety outcomes before clinical implementation.

items.title: Targeting α7 Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptors in Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder: Mechanisms and Clinical Implications.
items.authors: Kalinovskii AP, Osmakov DI, Logashina YA, Andreev YA, Trukhan VM.

sections.text: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a severe disorder that is characterized by intrusive thoughts, impaired mood and cognition, hyperarousal, and avoidance in the months and years following a traumatic event. PTSD is comorbid with depression, anxiety, substance abuse, and is challenging for the treatment with psycho- and pharmacotherapy. In light of novel neurobiological findings on the pathogenesis of the disease, innovative approaches to its treatment are investigated. Recently, targeting cholinergic signaling with an antagonist of α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChR), BNC-210, showed a significant promise in clinical trials. This opened up a novel therapeutic strategy that, considering its translational success, calls for a mechanistic understanding. In this review, we dissect the neurobiological role of α7 nAChR in regard of PTSD, and related depression and anxiety states. We discuss the synaptic role of the receptor in fear circuits, immune and endocrine role via the anti-inflammatory cholinergic pathway, and current evidence for the utility of pharmacological modulation of α7 nAChR.

items.title: Methylphenidate-related cardiac and cardiovascular safety: a bibliometric and network analysis.
items.authors: Yilmaz ÖÇ, Açikel SB.

sections.heading: Background/aim
sections.text: Methylphenidate is widely used for the treatment of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD); however, concerns regarding its cardiac and cardiovascular safety remain clinically relevant. This study aimed to delineate the scientific landscape of methylphenidate-related cardiac and cardiovascular safety using bibliometric methods.

sections.heading: Materials and methods
sections.text: The Science Citation Index Expanded, Social Sciences Citation Index, and Emerging Sources Citation Index were used to search the Web of Science Core Collection. A proximity-based search that combined terms related to methylphenidate, cardiovascular health, and safety/adverse events retrieved 263 records. There were 244 publications in the dataset after only including articles and reviews. VOSviewer was used to analyze author coauthorship, country coauthorship, keyword cooccurrence, and source citation networks.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: After author name disambiguation, author coauthorship analysis identified 34 authors in five clusters, with Coghill, Banaschewski, Buitelaar, Wong, McCarthy, and Sonuga-Barke showing the strongest collaborative links. The analysis of countries found 24 countries or regions in five clusters. The USA was the most productive country, and England had the strongest overall link strength. Keyword analysis found 33 standardized keywords in eight clusters. The most common words were "attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder," "methylphenidate," "stimulants," "atomoxetine," and "amphetamines." Source citation analysis showed that CNS Drugs received the highest number of citations, whereas the Journal of Child and Adolescent Psychopharmacology was the most productive source. Neurology showed a notable citation impact despite contributing only two documents.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The literature is structured around ADHD pharmacotherapy, cardiovascular surveillance, severe cardiac outcomes, drug safety, and pharmacoepidemiology. There is a need for more international cooperation and long-term studies that compare safety.

items.title: Genetic, Hormonal, and Psychosocial Factors Underly Sex Differences in Psychotic-Like Experience Trajectories in Adolescence
Altered ROCK1/ROCK2 Expression and RhoA/ROCK-Related Transcriptional Signatures Across Human and Experimental Models of Alcohol Exposure.
items.authors: Segovia-Alonso P, Herrera-Flores C, Costa-Alba P, Inés-Revuelta SM, Rodríguez C, Salete-Granado D, Echeverry-Alzate V, Aguilar ML, Puertas-Miranda D, Andrade Alviárez D, Cicuéndez B, Pérez-Nieto MÁ, Folgueira C, Mora A, López-Moreno JA, Sabio G, Almeida Á, Rojas-Pirela M, Marcos M.

sections.text: Chronic and acute alcohol exposure induce tissue-specific pathophysiological changes across multiple organ systems. Rho-associated coiled-coil kinases (ROCK1 and ROCK2) are key effectors of RhoA GTPases and participate in diverse biological processes, including the regulation of cytoskeletal dynamics, inflammation, fibrosis, apoptosis and redox homeostasis; however, their contribution to alcohol-related disorders remains incompletely understood. In this study, we evaluated ROCK1 and ROCK2 expression by qPCR and performed a cross-tissue, multi-model analysis integrating peripheral blood (PB) from human cohorts with alcohol use disorder (AUD) and acute alcohol consumption (AAC), in vitro cultures of ethanol-treated human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and mouse astrocytes, and animal models. Additionally, pathway-level transcriptional profiling was conducted to assess upstream activators, core Rho/ROCK components, and downstream inflammatory, fibrotic, and apoptotic signatures in PB from AUD patients, liver tissue from the NIAAA mouse model, and astrocyte cultures. Apoptosis-related transcriptional changes were assessed using the BCL2/BAX mRNA ratio. Ethanol exposure was associated with increased expression of ROCK isoforms across several models and tissues. Alterations in ROCK1/ROCK2 expression and in RhoA/ROCK-related transcriptional signatures were accompanied by tissue-specific inflammatory, fibrotic, and apoptosis-related transcriptional changes. These findings suggest that ethanol exposure is associated with alterations in ROCK1/ROCK2 expression and RhoA/ROCK-related transcriptional signatures across different experimental settings. They also support further investigation of the functional relevance of this pathway and its potential implications as a biomarker and therapeutic target in alcohol-related disorders.
