items.title: Creatine Supplementation Across Health and Performance Outcomes: An Umbrella Review of Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses.
items.authors: Almeida NR, Santos MAF, Fernandes JR, Brito MA, Costa KF, Soto DAS, Pérez DV, Aedo-Muñoz E, Aidar FJ, Barreto LBM, Nóbrega OT, Brito CJ.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Creatine supplementation is widely used to enhance physical performance, but its effects across health and performance outcomes remain uncertain.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: To synthesise evidence from systematic reviews and meta-analyses on creatine supplementation, evaluating methodological quality, certainty of evidence, and primary-study overlap.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: An umbrella review was conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Overviews of Reviews (PRIOR) statement and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261501087). PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for systematic reviews with quantitative meta-analyses published during the preceding 20 years. Methodological quality was assessed using AMSTAR-2, and primary-study overlap using the Corrected Covered Area (CCA).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Forty-five systematic reviews were included, and the evidence was organised into seven thematic domains. Most reviews examined healthy, physically active, or athletic populations, whereas clinical cohorts (e.g., chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, depression, or metabolic disease) were represented in approximately one fifth of the reviews, mainly in mixed samples of healthy and clinical participants. Creatine supplementation showed favourable effects on selected measures of muscular strength, power, lean mass, and physical function, with more consistent findings when combined with resistance training. Cognitive findings suggested improvements in selected measures of memory, attention, and processing speed, whereas evidence for endurance, recovery, inflammation, and mental health outcomes remained mixed or outcome-specific. Serum creatinine increased, but Cr-EDTA-measured GFR and urinary kidney-injury markers showed no significant changes; evidence regarding long-term renal safety remains limited. No review achieved high AMSTAR-2 confidence, and nearly half were rated critically low. Primary-study overlap was slight (global CCA: 3.49%), although 395 unique studies accounted for 1001 study-review inclusions, indicating that concordance across reviews does not necessarily represent independent replication.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Creatine supplementation appears to provide outcome-specific benefits, particularly for selected measures of strength, power, lean mass, and physical function. However, these findings are tempered by the absence of high-confidence reviews and substantial reuse of primary studies across syntheses. Interpretation should therefore account for methodological limitations, population and outcome variability, and primary-study overlap.

items.title: Living with cutaneous porphyria: findings from a qualitative survey study.
items.authors: Sani F.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Cutaneous porphyria is a rare skin disorder caused by the build-up of organic chemicals called porphyrins following exposure to sunlight. Clinical cutaneous features may include skin fragility, bullae, neuropathic-type pain, oedema and erythema, depending on the specific type of cutaneous porphyria. In some ultra-rare forms, features may even include severe scarring and mutilation. Although symptoms in most cases can be managed, there is no cure for cutaneous porphyria. Having cutaneous porphyria may have a strong negative impact on a person's mental health and quality of life.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: To explore what it is like to live with cutaneous porphyria and to increase healthcare practitioners' awareness of the difficulties faced by patients with cutaneous porphyria.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A total of 82 adult participants representing 12 nationalities from 5 different continents completed an online qualitative survey about their experiences of living with cutaneous porphyria. Data were subjected to descriptive, inductive thematic analysis.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Four main themes were identified. These concerned (i) the physical symptoms and available treatments for the illness; (ii) the restrictions imposed by the illness; (iii) the impact of the illness on social relations; and (iv) the mental health implications of the illness. Participants' responses highlighted a host of difficulties, ranging from the physical manifestations of the condition, which often include unbearable pain, to restrictions in all spheres of life (e.g. working, travelling, doing outdoor sport and leisure activities, and going out with children, partners and friends) imposed by the necessity to avoid sunlight. In turn, the symptoms of the illness, as well as the restrictions caused by these symptoms, negatively affected participants' social relations, including intimate ones, and mental health, with many participants reporting feeling depressed, lonely, isolated and anxious. The data also showed that patients do not always feel understood or properly cared for by medical practitioners.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Efforts should be made to raise awareness and knowledge among healthcare practitioners of the difficulties faced by patients with cutaneous porphyria, with the aim of improving the quality of interactions, communication and support.

items.title: Adolescents' needs for psychological assistance hotline services: an exploratory sequential mixed methods study.
items.authors: Han Y, Yu Y, Tang Y, Miao Y.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Psychological assistance hotlines provide low-threshold crisis support, but evidence is limited on how Chinese adolescents define useful hotline care.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: To identify adolescents' hotline-service needs and develop a preliminary context-specific scale.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: In an exploratory sequential mixed methods study, 12 adolescent hotline users completed semi-structured interviews analyzed with Colaizzi's method. The resulting 11-item Adolescent Psychological Assistance Hotline Service Need Scale (APAHSNS) was administered to 386 school-based adolescents. The sample was randomly divided for exploratory factor analysis (EFA; n = 193) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA; n = 193). Group comparisons, correlations, and multiple regression were conducted.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Qualitative analysis identified emotional safety, non-judgmental support, and closed-loop empowerment needs. The APAHSNS showed good internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.883) and content validity (S-CVI/Ave = 0.927). EFA explained 69.98% of variance, and CFA supported the three-factor structure (χ²/df = 1.39, CFI = 0.980, TLI = 0.973, RMSEA = 0.045, SRMR = 0.044). The total score was 3.73 ± 0.62. More frequent negative emotions (β = 0.329), prior hotline use (β = 0.258), lower perceived social support (β=-0.194), and older age (β = 0.207) were associated with higher need scores (adjusted R²=0.369; all P < 0.001). Overall, 72.3% were willing to consider AI-enabled functions.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: In this regional school-based sample, adolescents' hotline needs formed a three-dimensional structure. The findings provide preliminary measurement evidence and hypotheses requiring external, longitudinal, and clinical validation.

items.title: The associations between parental gaming attributes and the behavioral intention to reduce gaming time among Chinese adolescents who self-perceived as having internet gaming disorder: mediations via positive outcome expectancy.
items.authors: Yu Y, Ng JH, Li JB, Zhang J, Lau JTF.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Reduction of gaming time is a common means to prevent internet gaming disorder (IGD) among adolescents at risk of IGD. According to the Social Cognitive Theory, environmental factors (e.g., perceived parental IGD and parental invitations to co-play) and cognitive factors (e.g., positive outcome expectancy of internet gaming) are potential determinants of the behavioral intention to reduce gaming time.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: With informed consent, a cross-sectional survey was conducted in two Chinese cities from October 2019 to January 2020 among students who self-perceived as having IGD. The sample size was 1,039.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The prevalence of probable IGD in the sampled at-risk adolescents was 24.4%. The prevalence of behavioral intention to reduce gaming time in this population was 68.6% (55.1% versus 73.2% among probable IGD cases and non-IGD cases; p < .001). Two parental gaming attributes (perceived parental IGD and parental invitations to co-play) and positive outcome expectancies were significantly and negatively associated with the behavioral intention to reduce gaming time. Furthermore, positive outcome expectancy significantly and fully mediated the associations between perceived parental IGD and the behavioral intention to reduce gaming time, and it partially mediated the association between parental invitations to co-play and the intention (6.3%). All structural/indirect paths were invariant by probable IGD status (cases versus non-cases), except that one path from perceived parental IGD to behavioral intention to reduce gaming time was stronger in the probable IGD group than in the non-IGD group.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: High prevalence of behavioral intention to reduce gaming time was observed, which underlies the high motivation among those at risk of IGD to participate in interventions involving a reduction in gaming time. Such interventions may consider parental participation and fostering balanced positive outcome expectancy of internet gaming.

items.title: Impact of a national educational intervention on academic burden and health-related behaviours among children and adolescents in China: a repeated cross-sectional study.
items.authors: Huang JS, Sun Y, Zhang XY, Zhuang DR, Liu WJ, He JR, Lin R.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Excessive academic burden adversely affects health-related behaviours and mental health among children and adolescents. In July 2021, China implemented the "Double Reduction" policy to reduce homework and extracurricular tutoring. However, robust evidence on its impact on academic burden and health behaviours is lacking. We aimed to evaluate the changes in academic burden and related health behaviours among school-aged children in Guangzhou before and after the policy.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We conducted a repeated cross-sectional study using data from the Guangzhou Student Common Diseases and Health Influencing Factors Surveillance Program (2019-2025). Students in Year 4 - Year 12 from 66 schools were included. Academic burden (daily homework and weekly tutoring time) and health-related behaviours (sedentary time, moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), and sleep duration) were assessed via self-report. Mixed-effects models were used to examine the overall and stratified trends by educational stage, sex and location.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Daily homework time decreased significantly from 2019 to 2022 (β = -0.10, 95% CI: -0.11 to -0.09), followed by a rebound from 2022 to 2025 (β = 0.05, 95% CI: 0.04 to 0.06). Weekly tutoring time showed a similar pattern (2019-2022: β = -0.19, 95% CI: -0.20 to -0.18; 2022-2025: β = 0.06, 95% CI: 0.05 to 0.07). The rebound was most pronounced among primary school and suburban students. Urban students showed a rebound primarily in tutoring time, whereas suburban students exhibited a clearer rebound in homework time. Sedentary time followed a comparable U-shaped trajectory. Sleep duration increased initially but declined after 2022. In contrast, compliance with MVPA guidelines improved steadily throughout the study period (2019-2025).

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The "Double Reduction" policy achieved initial reductions in academic burden and short-term improvements in some health behaviours, but these effects were not sustained. Achieving sustainable improvement requires systemic educational reforms beyond mere workload reduction, addressing the fundamental tension between well-being-oriented policies and the enduring examination-centric ecosystem.

items.title: An Exploration of the Cultural Relevance of Narrative Coherence Criteria with Banyamulenge Congolese Refugee Women.
items.authors: Gowen MJ, Nilsson JE, Gowen M, Molitoris A, Oh M, Raziuddin R, Ross J.

sections.text: Due to the extensive violence occurring in the Democratic Republic of the Congo over the past three decades, Congolese refugees account for the largest number of refugees from one country resettled in the United States over the past decade, accounting for 20% of refugee admissions in 2024. Congolese refugees report high levels of trauma, anxiety, depression, and trauma/PTSD and more tools are needed to assess refugees' mental health. In this qualitative content analysis (QCA) study, we critically examined nine interviews with Banyamulenge Congolese refugee women (ages 25-48) to explore the cultural relevance and applicability of Baerger and McAdams' measure of narrative coherence. Narrative coherence theory posits the ability to share one's story in a way that makes sense to the listener indicates the person has integrated and come to terms with their life experiences, which is subsequently related to health and well-being. Participants were also asked to describe their current number and forms of social support, which is documented as a measure of well-being; in this study, it was explored as a potential source of validation for narrative coherence. Responses were placed in two main categories: (a) coherent responses (44% of total responses) and (b) incoherent responses (46% of total responses), indicating that only one of the nine participants demonstrated fully coherent responses to all interview questions. A post-hoc analysis was conducted in an effort to provide a more complete picture of the quality of the narrative coherence among the participants. Hence, a third main category was created, coherent responses without criterion I_8, showing a greater number of coherent ratings. These findings provide initial support for the use of a narrative coherence framework as a means of understanding refugee experiences. Clinical and research implications are discussed.

items.title: Adeno-Associated Virus Gene Therapy for Recurrent and Drug-Resistant Ovarian Cancer: Capsid Engineering, Intraperitoneal Delivery, and Rational Combinations.
items.authors: Iwahashi N, Yahata T, Ino K.

sections.text: Ovarian cancer remains difficult to cure because disseminated peritoneal disease, heterogeneity, and resistance to platinum and poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors limit treatment durability. Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors offer sustained transgene expression and capsid and regulatory cassette engineering, but translation is constrained by incomplete tumor-selective delivery, limited cargo capacity, host immunity, and heterogeneous tumor states. We examine AAV-mediated therapy in the context of recurrent and drug-resistant ovarian cancer. We discuss receptor retargeting, intraperitoneal versus systemic delivery, suicide genes, cytokines, genome editing, tumor suppressor restoration, and secreted antiangiogenic payloads. The most extensive ovarian AAV precedent concerns antiangiogenic and vascular-normalizing approaches; EpCAM-directed delivery and PD-L1-targeted AAV-CRISPR provide early evidence. FOLR1-targeted IL-12 efficacy and immune response findings derive from engineered MC38 colorectal tumors, with ovarian-cell targeting demonstrated separately. Studies do not establish restoration of platinum or PARP inhibitor sensitivity or any clinical benefit in resistant ovarian cancer. Chemotherapy combinations have preclinical support, whereas combinations with PARP inhibitors, checkpoint inhibitors, and antibody-drug conjugates remain hypotheses requiring direct testing. We outline biomarker-informed patient selection, immunological barriers to redosing, manufacturing and regulatory requirements, and a staged clinical development framework. Translation requires clinically representative resistant models and independent validation of delivery, pharmacodynamic activity, and safety before durable benefit can be inferred.

Translation requires clinically representative resistant models and independent validation of delivery, pharmacodynamic activity, and safety before durable benefit can be inferred.

items.title: Dopamine-Altering Medication Use Is Associated with Immune and Sickness-Related Outcomes: A Sex-Stratified Population-Based Study.
items.authors: Martínez-Albert E, Capellino S.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: Dopaminergic signaling regulates immune-cell activity in experimental models, but its association with immune-related outcomes in human populations remains unclear. We examined whether use of dopamine (DA)-altering medications was associated with immune-related symptoms, systemic inflammatory biomarkers, and recent health-related activity limitation. Methods: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data from 53,585 participants aged 16-65 years. Primary analyses compared users of any DA-altering medication with nonusers. Secondary analyses distinguished medications expected to increase or decrease dopaminergic signaling. Outcomes included self-reported colds, infections, and days of reduced usual activity due to health problems in the preceding 30 days, as well as C-reactive protein (CRP) and white blood cell (WBC) counts. We also conducted sex-stratified and sensitivity analyses. Results: DA-altering medication use was associated with greater odds of recent health-related activity limitation (odds ratio 3.38, 95% confidence interval 2.94-3.90), higher CRP (+40.2%), and higher WBC counts (+4.0%) compared with nonuse. Associations with recent colds and infections were not statistically significant in the overall primary analysis. In secondary analyses, DA-decreasing medication use was associated with lower odds of recent colds among males and higher odds of infections among females, and health-related activity limitation and inflammatory biomarker associations were generally stronger for DA-decreasing medications. Elevated CRP and associations with health-related activity limitation persisted in analyses excluding participants with depressive symptoms and mental health-related activity limitation. Conclusions: DA-altering medication use was associated with systemic inflammatory biomarkers and recent health-related activity limitation. Longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether these associations reflect medication effects, underlying treatment indications, or both.

items.title: Home Education and Psychosocial Well-Being in Children and Adolescents: A Scoping Review.
items.authors: Navarrete-Ramírez P, Vásquez-Carrasco E, Hernandez-Martinez J, López-Andaur R, Valdés-Badilla P.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Home education encompasses heterogeneous educational arrangements, and its relationship with psychosocial well-being remains unclear.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study maps empirical evidence on emotional, behavioral, mental health, social, interpersonal, and family-related outcomes and experiences among home education children and adolescents.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This scoping review followed Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and PRISMA-ScR. Eight databases were searched from inception to 9 September 2026 without language or publication-date restrictions. Peer-reviewed original empirical publications involving home education children and adolescents aged 5-18 years were eligible. Mixed-age studies were retained when this age group constituted the primary home education population or when relevant age-disaggregated findings were available; inseparable findings were classified as mixed-age evidence. Two reviewers independently screened records and charted data. Findings were synthesized descriptively and narratively.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Of 4427 records, 23 publications were included and mapped across four psychosocial domains. Comparative findings were heterogeneous, with favorable, null, mixed, and less favorable patterns across outcomes and populations. Qualitative studies described perceived benefits and challenges related to family relationships, individualized support, previous school experiences, and social opportunities. Several publications used overlapping or potentially overlapping samples.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Comparative evidence did not show a consistent association between home education and either better or poorer psychosocial well-being. The available literature was heterogeneous in design, population, educational context, measurement approach, and informant, supporting a context-sensitive interpretation rather than universal conclusions of benefit, equivalence, or harm.

items.title: Applying evolutionary psychiatry in clinical practice: a qualitative study of clinicians.
items.authors: Brar G, Kamran M, Akbar MW, Poobalan K, McFarland J, O'Connell H.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Evolutionary psychiatry applies principles of evolutionary biology to explain vulnerability to mental disorders and has been proposed as a valuable addition to psychiatric training. Despite increasing interest, little is known about how clinicians understand and apply evolutionary perspectives in practice.

sections.heading: Aims
sections.text: To explore psychiatric trainees' and consultants' experiences of evolutionary psychiatry teaching and to examine its perceived relevance to clinical practice and training.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A qualitative study was conducted using semi-structured focus groups with psychiatric trainees and consultant psychiatrists attending workshop-based teaching sessions. Three focus groups ( N  = 18) were conducted. Discussions were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Four overarching themes were identified: (i) Conceptual Reframing of Psychiatry, (ii) Conceptual Value, Curricular Absence, (iii) Tension Between Explanatory Insight and Clinical Utility, and (iv) Barriers to Integration Within Training and Practice. Participants described evolutionary psychiatry as providing a coherent explanatory framework that enhanced understanding and formulation, particularly through concepts such as adaptation, trade-offs, and mismatch. However, exposure during training was limited, and participants reported uncertainty regarding its application in day-to-day clinical decision-making. Structural barriers, including curriculum constraints and limited faculty expertise, were compounded by concerns regarding abstraction and potential misapplication.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Evolutionary psychiatry is experienced by clinicians as conceptually valuable but insufficiently integrated into training and practice. Bridging the gap between explanatory insight and clinical utility will require embedding evolutionary perspectives within existing curricula, linking theory to clinically relevant applications, and supporting faculty development.

items.title: Strengthening healthcare access for adolescent and young adult women: a narrative review of determinants, health system challenges, and emerging strategies for equitable care.
items.authors: Rathored J, Budhbaware T, Upadhyay V.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Due to biological, social, economic, cultural, geographic, and health system restrictions that restrict timely access to high-quality healthcare, adolescent and young adult (AYA) women face significant health disparities. Particularly in low- and middle-income countries, these issues lead to unnecessary maternal morbidity and death, mental health concerns, infectious and non-communicable conditions, and poor sexual and reproductive health. Therefore, achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and Universal Health Coverage (UHC) requires improving equal access to healthcare.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: To synthesize the available literature on the factors influencing healthcare access, health system challenges, and emerging strategies affecting equitable healthcare utilization among adolescent and young adult women, with emphasis on policy priorities and future research directions.

sections.heading: Review approach
sections.text: A narrative review approach was used to synthesize the literature on healthcare access among AYA women. The review considers conceptual frameworks of healthcare access and organizes the literature thematically across individual, sociocultural, economic, geographic, reproductive, mental health, digital, and health-system determinants, as well as vulnerable populations, emerging interventions, policy recommendations, and future research priorities.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: The review shows how complex relationships between individual traits, socioeconomic variables and health system factors influence AYA women's access to healthcare. Insufficient health literacy, gender inequality, poverty, high expenses, insufficient insurance, transportation challenges, stigma, a lack of workers, insufficient facilities, a lack of adolescent-friendly services and the digital divide are all significant obstacles. Accessibility may be further enhanced by new strategies including telemedicine, mobile health technology, artificial intelligence, integrated healthcare models, youth- friendly clinics, community engagement and universal health coverage. Coordinated multisectoral policies, improved healthcare systems, digital inclusion, financial security, and culturally sensitive services catered to the needs of young women and teens are necessary for successful implementation, despite this.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Equitable healthcare access for teenage and young adult women requires integrated, patient-centered, and evidence-based treatments that address structural, financial, societal, and technological barriers simultaneously. Reducing healthcare disparities, increasing healthcare utilization, and achieving long-term improvements in the health and well-being of AYA women worldwide require investments in adolescent-friendly healthcare services, digital health innovations, strengthening the health system, gender responsive policies, and implementation research.

items.title: Therapeutic communication: avoidance of negative influences and application of beneficial suggestions in anesthesia and intensive care, emergency, and pain medicine.
items.authors: Hansen E, Ebell H, Zech N.

sections.text: In anesthesia, and in emergency and intensive care medicine a "therapeutic communication" with the patient is needed that exceeds mere information exchange and that supports patient and treatment. First, ever-present nocebo effects and negative suggestions must be avoided or neutralized. For any medical intervention to be optimally effective, their explicit announcing it and its significance is essential to induce placebo effects. To avoid sources of stress, significant themes derived from the basic psychological needs should be addressed. The patient's own contribution to homeostasis and healing should be appreciated to get him out of prescribed passivity. In an acute existential threat during an emergency, surgery or intensive care, patients tend to enter a naturally occurring trance state as an emergency program and are less rational and particularly susceptible to suggestions. Accordingly, in emergency care "painful" words should be avoided, non-verbal signals of companionship be given, and images of healing induced. Hypnotic language directed at the unconscious, where programs for physiological and mental functions are located and modulable, seems especially appropriate. Induction of nocebo effects during risk information to obtain informed consent can be counteracted by simultaneous offer of positive aspects, such as ways to prevent, detect early, or treat side effects. For support during surgery under regional anesthesia, the patient can be encouraged and guided to dissociation to an inner safe place of well-being and to reframing of sensory impressions. Given recent evidence of perception during unconsciousness, like under anesthesia, during resuscitation, or in coma, communication should not be limited to conscious patients. Positive suggestions during general anesthesia have reduced pain, analgesic and antiemetic use, and PONV. Communication with the unconscious patient during emergencies, resuscitation, surgery or intensive care might prevent generation of PTSD exactly at that critical moment. In chronic pain or disease, the patient's experience of "being-ill" needs consideration on a level equal to the doctor's understanding of the "illness", and such intersubjective resonance is a prerequisite for optimal therapeutic results. Therefore, resonance-based treatment should supplement evidence-based medicine. The same approach in communication that is effective with the patients can reduce stress in the medical staff and improve their intervention.

items.title: Cerebellar climbing fibers in neurodevelopmental disorders.
items.authors: Pickeral PA, van der Heijden ME.

sections.text: The cerebellum is increasingly recognized for its involvement in various neurodevelopmental disorders with deficits in motor and cognitive functioning. In this review, we highlight recent advances in our understanding of abnormal olivocerebellar climbing fiber development in various preclinical models for these disorders. The cerebellum undergoes extensive postnatal development, during which climbing fibers from the inferior olive establish and refine synaptic connections with Purkinje cells, the principal neurons of the cerebellar cortex. Initially, each Purkinje cell receives input from multiple climbing fibers, but developmental synapse elimination ultimately produces a precise one-to-one connection. Increasing evidence indicates that faulty cerebellar circuit formation and function can arise from aberrant climbing fiber development, such as defects in synapse elimination, dendritic translocation, synaptic structure, synaptic number, or neurotransmission. Multiple studies have identified aberrant climbing fiber development in neurodevelopmental and neurological disorders, including autism spectrum disorder, schizophrenia, ataxia, dystonia, and essential tremor. We summarize the cellular and molecular mechanisms governing climbing fiber development and examine how their disruption contributes to disease pathogenesis. This work highlights the olivocerebellar circuit as a critical determinant of typical brain development and neurological function that is often disrupted in neurodevelopmental disorders.

items.title: Physical activity as a psychosocial strategy for promoting mental health in vulnerable youth.
items.authors: He X, Xu Q.

sections.text: Adolescence is a critical developmental window during which mental health disorders often emerge, yet a substantial proportion of young people-particularly those from socially and economically marginalized backgrounds-face significant barriers to accessing traditional mental health services. Structured physical activity and sport-based interventions have been proposed as a low-cost, non-stigmatizing, and accessible adjunctive strategy for promoting psychological well-being in this population. This narrative review provides a conceptual synthesis of findings from 13 studies that examined the effects of physical activity and sport interventions on mental health outcomes in vulnerable youth. Recognizing the heterogeneity of both the target populations and the intervention approaches, this review proposes a conceptual distinction between three overlapping dimensions of psychological distress disproportionately affecting these youth: (a) internalizing disorders (depression, anxiety, and post-traumatic stress); (b) externalizing problems (aggression, conduct issues, and substance use); and (c) social and self-evaluative dysfunction (low self-esteem, loneliness, and diminished self-efficacy). Through thematic synthesis of quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods evidence, the review identifies four interconnected program characteristics associated with improved outcomes: structured facilitation by trained adults, group-based and team formats, cultural adaptation with family engagement, and sustained, long-term delivery. Findings suggest that sport-based interventions hold considerable promise as a public health strategy for this at-risk group. The available evidence, however, remains heterogeneous across populations, interventions, settings, outcome measures, and study designs, and the findings are therefore primarily hypothesis-generating rather than conclusive. The mental health benefits of sport in this population are proposed to arise from the convergence of relational, psychological, and neurobiological mechanisms rather than from physical exercise alone. These issues await further validation and confirmation in future research.

items.title: Perceived importance and preference for mental health management mini-program functions among nurses as second victims: a cross-sectional survey.
items.authors: Chen H, Wang L, Liu H.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: In recent years, mobile health tools represented by WeChat mini-programs have garnered increasing attention in the healthcare domain. However, there is still a gap in digital tool development for the psychological needs of nurses as second victims. It is crucial to understand how to provide these individuals with necessary psychological support and what functionality preferences they have for mental health mini-programs.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study aims to examine the importance and preference of various functions in mental health management mini-programs by nurses as second victims, which would serve as a basis for future designs of mini-programs to improve the mental wellbeing of nurses as second victims.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Between November 2025 and January 2026, 176 nurses who had experienced nursing adverse events were selected via convenience sampling from three Class III Grade A hospitals in Shandong Province. The study employed a general information questionnaire, a questionnaire on perceived importance of mental health management mini-program functions for nurses as second victims and the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The overall mean perceived importance score among the 176 nurses as second victims regarding the mental health management mini-program was 4.21 ± 0.33, with scores for the five core functional modules being: psychological support (4.50 ± 0.42), peer support (4.30 ± 0.54), stress management (4.20 ± 0.47), health education (4.11 ± 0.55) and program design (4.08 ± 0.78). The results of Spearman's correlation analysis showed that the professional title of nurses as second victims ( r_s = -0.260， P_FDR = 0.002), age ( r_s = -0.285, P_FDR < 0.001), and years of service ( r_s = -0.302, P_FDR < 0.001) were negatively correlated with the total perceived importance score, while the number of nursing adverse events experienced was positively correlated with the perceived importance of mini-program functions ( r_s = 0.244, P_FDR = 0.005).

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Nurses as second victims attach high perceived importance to mental health management mini-program functions; however, the extent of this perceived importance varies among nurses as second victims with different professional titles, ages, years of service, and numbers of nursing adverse events experienced.

items.title: Psychiatric referral and admissionprocesses for people with dementia and behaviour that challenges, who live in nursing homes: a socio-ecological model of contextual factors and assumed connections of dementia crises.
items.authors: Henni Rached I, Ledtermann I.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: People with dementia are often repeatedly admitted to geriatric psychiatry due to behaviour that challenges. This can have far-reaching consequences and cause stress for those affected, which can have a negative impact on the recovery process and lead to increased vulnerability to new health problems after hospitalisation. In addition to the behaviour that challenges itself, many other contextual factors, especially those that contribute to dementia crises, can lead to hospitalisation.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Building on previously published studies (integrative review, problem-centred interviews) and a new expert validation, we followed the first step, 'Understanding the problem and its causes,' of Wight et al.'s 'Six Steps in Quality Intervention Development' and developed a socio-ecological model of dementia crises and the associated (re)referrals and (re)admissions of people with dementia to geriatric psychiatry, inspired by McLeroy et al.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The socio-ecological model comprises 20 concepts drawn from contextual factors and outlines assumptions regarding their connections at various levels. The public policy level refers to 'Financing', 'Research' and 'Structural regulations'. The institutional level includes 'Environment', 'Staff', 'Operating and everyday norms', 'Treatment' and 'Admission and discharge interface'. The community level deals with 'Societal attitudes' and 'Social norms and values'. The interpersonal level involves 'Relationships' and 'Roles and hierarchies', 'Information and communication' and 'Interprofessional decision-making'. People with dementia are often repeatedly admitted to geriatric psychiatry due to behaviour that challenges. This can have far-reaching consequences and cause stress for those affected, which can have a negative impact on the recovery process and lead to increased vulnerability to new health problems after hospitalisation. The institutional level includes 'Environment', 'Staff', 'Operating and everyday norms', 'Treatment' and 'Admission and discharge interface'. The community level deals with 'Societal attitudes' and 'Social norms and values'. The interpersonal level involves 'Relationships' and 'Roles and hierarchies', 'Information and communication' and 'Interprofessional decision-making'. Similarly, the individual level appears to influence the institutional and the interpersonal level; the interpersonal level seems to affect the individual and the institutional level. The institutional and community levels appear to interact. Furthermore, the public policy level seems to have an impact on both the institutional and the individual levels.

The socio-ecological model highlights the high complexity of the problem of dementia crises and the associated (re)referrals and (re)admissions of people with dementia to geriatric psychiatry at various levels and provides a basis for future research and the development of programme theories and complex interventions that address actual needs.

items.title: De-escalation training across crisis-response sectors: a scoping review protocol.
items.authors: Szkudlarek P, Lin E, Bucago C, Rocha H, Hilton M, Leroux E, Zaheer J, Sockalingam S, Sikstrom L.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: There is growing concern about violent or harmful encounters between crisis-intervention professionals and practitioners and individuals experiencing acute mental health crises, including those presenting with severe behavioural disturbances related to mental health concerns and/or substance use. In response, healthcare institutions and regulatory bodies are increasingly mandating "de-escalation" training. However, no universally accepted standard exists, and variability in how de-escalation trainings are defined, researched, and implemented may contribute to mixed findings regarding their effectiveness.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This scoping review aims to examine the existing academic literature on de-escalation training for crisis-intervention professionals and practitioners, defined as individuals whose role - whether professional, paraprofessional, or community-based - requires them to intervene in an acute mental health or addictions crisis prior to, or during, transition to formal care. This includes, but is not limited to, paramedics, law enforcement officers, crisis intervention teams, emergency department staff, mobile crisis units, peer support workers, and others trained to intervene in crisis encounters.

sections.heading: Inclusion criteria
sections.text: Eligible studies are primary research articles published in English between June 14 2014 and July 30, 2025, that report on de-escalation training in the context of a crisis encounter between a person in a mental health crisis and a crisis-intervention professional or practitioner tasked with intervening.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: The review will follow the five-stage framework proposed by Arksey and O'Malley (2005), with updates from Levac et al., (2010), and guided by the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Framework. A medical research librarian will conduct searches in Medline, PsycInfo, Scopus, Embase, and the Education Resources Information Centre. Screening will occur in two phases: initial title and abstract review, followed by full-text review based on predefined inclusion criteria. An interprofessional team of clinicians (nursing, psychiatry), social scientists, and a police officer will perform data extraction and analysis using the PRISMA-ScR (2018) guidelines. Both qualitative and quantitative synthesis methods will be used to identify patterns and emergent themes in the literature.

items.title: Temporal Trends of Mortality Due to Obesity in the United States, 1999-2022, an Analysis of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention WONDER Database: A Retrospective Study.
items.authors: Hazazi A, Ijaz H, Abbas MS, Rahman JSU, Ali A, Ali A, Cheema U, Wei CR, Ali B, Akilimali A.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Obesity, the excess body fat, is a chronic problem that disrupts both physical and mental health. Obesity is linked to diabetes, cancer, and cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disorders, making it the second most frequent preventable cause leading to death. Contemporary national trends in obesity-related mortality, including the COVID-19 pandemic period, remain incompletely characterized. We therefore examined temporal trends in obesity-related mortality in the United States from 1999 to 2022 by sex, age group, census region, and place of death.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Deidentified data from CDC WONDER database were used in our study. The International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) code E66 was used to identify cases in which obesity was recorded as an underlying or contributing cause of death between 1999 and 2022. The data were extracted based on age, gender, year, population size, census region, and place of death. Annual percent changes (APC) and age adjusted mortality rates (AAMR) per 100,000 people were utilized in our study to analyse the mortality trends of Obesity in the United States using Joinpoint regression.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: During 1999-2022, obesity caused 840,975 deaths in the United States. The Obesity AAMR was 4.7 per 100,000 in 1999, which rose to 18.9 in 2022, after a peak of 24.73 in 2021. An APC of 6.76 (95% CI 5.68-7.85) was calculated for this increase. Men had an average AAMR of 10.91, while it was 9.03 for women. The young- aged group had an average AAMR of 4.74, it was 19.68 for the middle-aged group, and 27.88 for the old-age group. The South region exhibited the highest mortality burden (most deaths, highest 2022 AAMR [20.35] and steepest APC [7.53%]), although the West had the highest period-average AAMR (10.56), while the Northeast region showed the lowest average AAMR (8.37). Regional differences in mortality rates were observed across all census regions during the study period.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Mortality due to obesity has been increasing significantly (more than fourfold) between 1999 and 2022. Mortality rates were higher in men and older adults, and the South bore the highest regional burden. The rate peaked in 2021 and declined in 2022 but remained about fourfold above its 1999 level. Further research using individual-level data is needed to clarify the drivers of this increase, including changes in death-certification practices and the role of COVID-19.

items.title: Team Influences on Implementation Outcomes: A Mixed-Methods Study of Rural Children's Advocacy Centers.
items.authors: McGuier EA, Wright JD, Campbell KA, Kolko DJ, Keeshin BR, Abdulahad LDS, Byrne KA, Aarons GA.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Teamwork influences implementation processes and outcomes, but knowledge of how specific dimensions of teamwork affect implementation is limited. We used explanatory sequential mixed methods to examine how teamwork influenced implementation outcomes in rural Children's Advocacy Center (CAC) multidisciplinary teams.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: CACs across a single state implemented the Care Process Model for Pediatric Traumatic Stress (CPM-PTS), a mental health screening/referral protocol. We purposively sampled six rural/frontier CACs with variability in reach and interviewed team members in each CAC ( N  = 24). Interview data were coded for potential influencing factors, which were then categorized as general teamwork or innovation-specific teamwork. Influencing factors at each CAC were rated as negative, mixed, or low/moderate/high positive. Ratings and implementation outcomes were organized into a sortable matrix and color-coded to identify patterns. Qualitative and quantitative findings were integrated in a joint display.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Both general and innovation-specific teamwork were related to implementation outcomes. Problems in affective/behavioral functioning (e.g., trust, conflict management) impaired implementation efforts. Shared goals facilitated faster time to adoption, especially when the CPM-PTS was viewed as advancing the team's goals. Teams with better overall performance achieved better reach. Team members were generally supportive of the CPM-PTS despite limited knowledge, but their knowledge and beliefs had little influence on implementation outcomes. Sites where screening results were intentionally and consistently shared with team members had better reach and a quicker time to adoption than sites where results were intentionally or passively withheld from team members.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: In team-based service settings, team performance and shared goals facilitate better implementation outcomes. Positive affective/behavioral functioning may be a necessary precondition for successful implementation but insufficient on its own to improve outcomes. Teams that already work closely together may seek more active involvement in new practices, and their involvement can enhance implementation outcomes.

items.title: Retreat-Based Support for Ukrainian Psychologists and Psychotherapists During the Ongoing War: A Mixed-Methods Study of Changes in Psycho-Emotional Well-Being and Perceived Supportive Elements.
items.authors: Kolisnyk L, Mehlsen MY.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: Ukrainian mental health professionals work under continuous war-related threat. We examined changes in psycho-emotional well-being among Ukrainian psychologists and psychotherapists after a one-week retreat abroad, and the elements they perceived as supportive. Methods: In a mixed-methods study, retreat participants ( n = 28) and a non-randomized comparison group ( n = 31), all women, completed the WHO-5, CORE-10, BSI subscales, and HAAS before and after the retreat and one month later. Changes were analyzed with linear mixed models. Fourteen interviews were analyzed with qualitative content analysis. Results: From pre- to post-assessment, retreat participants improved more than the comparison group on all seven outcomes (|g| = 0.82-2.08), also after adjustment for age and recent vacation. However, demand characteristics may have inflated these effect sizes. At follow-up, the differences were smaller (|g| = 0.79-1.62) and robust only for psychological distress and well-being. Interviewees described stability, calm, emotional relief, and better sleep, attributed to the interplay of care, nature, safety, voluntary participation, and supportive relationships. Conclusions: A one-week retreat was followed by substantial short-term improvement in psycho-emotional well-being, partly sustained one month after returning to the war zone. The design cannot distinguish the effect of the retreat from that of a week in safety.

items.title: Establishing Restorative Pedagogy Within Medical School Curriculum: Iterative Development of Shame and Resilience Discussion Utilizing Restorative Practices.
items.authors: Klasson CL, Sarin S, Raghuram A, Kunz A, Bernat CK, Jung F, Shibli-Rahhal A.
items.journal: MedEdPORTAL : the journal of teaching and learning resources

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Student isolation and negative experiences of power dynamics, including shame, are well-documented contributors to student burnout. Traditional medical education lacks structured processes to promote resilience and minimize isolation. There is a need for intentional dialogue spaces to facilitate interpersonal connections and support. Restorative practices (RPs), such as community-building circles, represent potential tools to address these issues. However, there is no documented evidence of the use of RPs in medical school curricula.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: The authors adapted an existing discussion session on shame and resilience in the first-semester medical school curriculum by incorporating RP community-building circles. At the end of the session, individuals identified resilience strategies to address negative feelings. These structured conversations, led by trained facilitators, aimed to create equitable discussion environments. The approach focused on storytelling, minimizing power dynamics, and fostering a supportive learning environment. Student and facilitator perspectives were collected through anonymous surveys.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Of the 177 students and 78 facilitators who participated, 172 students (97%) and 29 facilitators (37%) completed the anonymous surveys. Survey responses indicated a positive impact on student engagement, feelings of support, and equitable participation. Both students and facilitators found the circling method effective for sharing personal stories and promoting mutual support. They highlighted increased feelings of connection and comfort with vulnerability. However, some perceived structural limitations and discomfort with vulnerability were noted.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: Future work should focus on the long-term evaluation of learners' perceptions of RPs, the intervention's impact on resilience, and students' continued use of identified resilience strategies. In addition, longitudinal incorporation of RPs across the curriculum is recommended.

items.title: The Prevalence and Impact of Obstructive Sleep Apnoea and Periodic Limb Movements in Sleep in Adult Parasomnias.
items.authors: Burgher T, Aleem S, Saqib F, Alrasheedi S, Morris B, Bikov A.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Parasomnias are abnormal behaviours in sleep. Disorders that can cause microarousals, such as obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) and periodic limb movements in sleep (PLMS) are often considered to trigger parasomnias. However, the prevalence and impact of OSA, and its specific clinical phenotypes, such as REM-related OSA (ROSA) and positional OSA (POSA), as well as PLMS in parasomnias are not fully explored.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We analysed the polysomnography reports of 155 patients who were referred to our tertiary service with symptoms of parasomnia. The prevalence of OSA, ROSA, POSA, and PLMS, as well as their severity indices were correlated with the prevalence of specific parasomnias using logistic regression.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The prevalence of OSA and PLMS was 48% and 23%, respectively. Whilst OSA and PLMS were inversely related to NREM parasomnias, PLMS was directly related to RBD ( p < 0.05). Moreover, there was a significant inverse correlation between the severity of PLMS and the prevalence of NREM parasomnias (β = -0.12, p = 0.03) and a direct correlation with RBD (β = 0.02, p = 0.04). However, following adjustments for age, BMI, and gender, only the inverse relationships between OSA and sleep terrors as well as POSA and sleep-related eating disorder remained significant.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The prevalence of OSA and PLMS is high among patients with parasomnia. Due to the exploratory nature of the study, conclusions on the associations need to be validated in interventional trials.

items.title: Exploring enhanced self-esteem reactivity in response to social prediction errors in adolescence.
items.authors: Gregorova K, Will GJ, Burkard P, Romanos M, Reiter AMF.

sections.text: Self-esteem is a cornerstone of mental health across the lifespan. Throughout life, but particularly during adolescence, self-esteem is shaped by social appraisals. Previous work in adults has shown that momentary fluctuations in self-esteem are explained not only by whether we are liked by others but also by whether we are liked more or less than expected (social prediction errors). Here, we examine age-related differences in how social experiences shape self-esteem in 141 participants aged 10-40 years using an experimental social evaluation task and ecological momentary assessment. In the experiment, self-esteem reactivity to unexpected social feedback follows a non-linear age-related pattern, peaking in late adolescence. In daily life, self-esteem reactivity to perceived pleasantness of social interaction and naturalistic social prediction errors is stronger in younger participants. Individual differences in experimental and daily-life self-esteem reactivity are associated, highlighting heightened self-esteem malleability during adolescence.

items.title: Arabic Translation, Cultural Adaptation, and Psychometric Evaluation of the Food Noise Questionnaire in Saudi Adults.
items.authors: Alhazmi A, Alshurtan K, Oraibi O, Mohrag M, Alshehri A, Al Zahib Y, Badawi A, Alfadda A, Abdulrasak M, Le Roux C.

sections.text: Background. Food noise is a persistent, intrusive, and often distressing thought about food that has emerged as a clinically meaningful dimension of appetite dysregulation in the disease of obesity. Yet no validated Arabic-language instrument exists to measure food noise. We aimed to translate, culturally adapt, and evaluate the psychometric properties of an Arabic version of the five-item Food Noise Questionnaire (FNQ) in a community sample of Saudi adults. Methods. In this cross-sectional online validation study, the FNQ underwent forward-backward translation, in accordance with international cross-cultural adaptation guidelines. Adults (≥18 years) who were not currently using obesity medications, had not undergone bariatric surgery, were not pregnant, and had no diagnosed eating disorder completed the Arabic FNQ together with sociodemographic, anthropometric, and behavioural items. The sample was randomly split into two subsamples for exploratory factor analysis (EFA; common factor analysis of polychoric correlations with parallel analysis) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA; robust weighted least squares, WLSMV). Reliability was estimated using Cronbach's alpha (α) and McDonald's omega (ω), and measurement invariance across sex and obesity status was tested with multi-group CFA. Associations with other variables were examined using Spearman correlations and group comparisons with effect sizes. Results. Of 445 respondents, the mean age was 39.4 ± 11.4 years, 70.3% were women, and the mean BMI was 29.4 ± 6.5 kg/m^2. Parallel analysis and the minimum average partial test supported one factor (loadings 0.69-0.90). In CFA, a strictly unidimensional model fitted poorly (CFI = 0.952; RMSEA = 0.294); allowing a residual correlation between the two functional-interference items (FNQ4 and FNQ5) produced good fit on CFI, TLI and SRMR (scaled χ^2 = 12.55, p = 0.014; CFI = 0.996; TLI = 0.989; SRMR = 0.024), with an elevated RMSEA (0.098) in this low-df model. Standardized loadings ranged from 0.56 to 0.92, and the general factor explained 81% of the common variance. Internal consistency was good (α = 0.867, 95% CI 0.847-0.886; ω_h = 0.825; ω_t = 0.866). Scalar invariance held across sex, and partial scalar invariance across obesity status. items.title: Obesity and Associated Factors Among Chinese University Freshmen: A Multicentre Cross-Sectional Study.
items.authors: Zhang H, Chen Z, Guo X, Zhou Z, Zhang J, Tian Q, Gong S, Tian X.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: Obesity constitutes a major public health concern that adversely affects the physical and mental health of adolescents. This study used cross-validated elastic net regression and logistic regression model to identify key associated factors of adolescent obesity among freshmen cross-sectionally sampled at random, and inform targeted interventions. Methods: During autumn 2023 (September-November), 16,092 freshmen aged 16-19 years were recruited randomly from universities in China's seven city/provinces. Questionnaires were used to collect data. Obesity was defined based on body mass index (BMI, weight (kg)/(height(m))^2). An elastic net model combining L1 and L2 regularization penalties (α = 0.5) was used to select variables. A logistic regression model was constructed to identify the significant key factors and their associations with obesity. Results: The adolescent obesity rate was 10.53% (95% CI: 10.07-11.02%) (males: 13.09%; females: 8.76%; p < 0.001). The logistic regression model included 29 variables selected by elastic net regularization, of which 18 dummy variables were statistically significant ( p < 0.05), Key adjusted correlates of obesity were female sex (vs male, OR = 0.75, 95% CI: 0.66-0.85), paternal obesity (vs no, OR = 1.45, 95% CI: 1.14-1.82), small food portions (vs large portions, OR = 0.35, 95% CI: 0.26-0.47), very slow eating (vs fast, OR = 0.58, 95% CI: 0.46-0.73), rare physical activity (vs competitive sports, OR = 1.36, 95% CI: 1.18-1.57), occasional breakfast (vs daily, OR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.07-1.47), no romantic experience (vs Yes, OR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.11-1.41), and lower water intake (vs high water intake, OR = 0.44, 95% CI: 0.35-0.55). The model's apparent AUC was 0.666 (95% CI: 0.656-0.683). After Bootstrap internal validation, the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.658, indicating modest discrimination; the corrected calibration intercept was -0.085, and the calibration slope was 0.957. Conclusions: Several demographic, behavioral, psychosocial, and familial factors were associated with obesity among Chinese freshmen; these associations do not establish causality and require independent confirmation.

items.title: A case of dissociative disorder with attenuation of EEG alpha power during a depersonalization episode.
items.authors: Kato T, Soga K, Sakuma K, Mizuno M.
items.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Dissociative disorders are characterized by disruptions in consciousness, memory, identity, and perception. Similar symptoms can occur in patients with frontal lobe epilepsy. Although dissociative disorders are generally classified as psychiatric conditions, several studies have reported electroencephalogram (EEG) abnormalities in only a small proportion of affected patients. The relationship between EEG abnormalities and dissociative symptoms remains poorly understood; further accumulation of similar cases is therefore required.

sections.heading: Case presentation
sections.text: We present the case of an adolescent female with a dissociative disorder, who had experienced depersonalization symptoms since childhood and developed recurrent episodes following COVID-19. The available clinical, magnetic resonance imaging, and scalp video-EEG findings did not support a diagnosis of epilepsy. Inpatient 24-h video-EEG monitoring at age 15 revealed a widespread reduction in alpha power across the brain during an episode of depersonalization.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Previous studies have implicated alpha power in the maintenance of stable perceptual states. In this case, quantitative EEG analysis captured a transient widespread reduction in alpha power coinciding with the patient's depersonalization symptoms. Although the specificity, causality, and reproducibility of this finding remain unknown, it may reflect the patient's dissociative symptoms. This case report suggests that a patient's subjective experiences can be captured using objective neurophysiological measures such as EEG.

items.title: Pulmonary embolism and pulmonary infarction triggered by heparin-induced thrombocytopenia during physical restraint in a psychiatric inpatient: A case report.
items.authors: Inaguma T, Maruyama J, Amemiya K, Sugihara T, Fukuda Y, Shimada M.
items.journal: PCN reports : psychiatry and clinical neurosciences

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Psychiatric inpatients have a high risk of venous thromboembolism because of physical restraint, reduced mobility, and sedation. Although subcutaneous unfractionated heparin (UFH) may be used for thromboprophylaxis during physical restraint, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) can occur even during prophylaxis and remains underrecognized.

sections.heading: Case presentation
sections.text: A man in his 20 s was emergently admitted for acute transient psychotic disorder and received UFH for thromboprophylaxis during physical restraint. Nine days after UFH initiation, he developed fever, pleuritic chest pain, and hypoxemia, and pneumonia was initially suspected. However, pulmonary embolism (PE) was later suspected because the respiratory findings were not fully explained by the localized opacity on chest radiographic and the D-dimer level was markedly elevated. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed bilateral pulmonary artery thrombi and right lower lobe pulmonary infarction. After PE diagnosis, escalation of UFH therapy produced little clinical improvement and thrombocytopenia developed. Anticoagulation was switched to apixaban, a direct oral anticoagulant. after which, oxygenation improved and the platelet count recovered. The 4Ts score, a clinical pretest probability score for HIT, was 6/8, and the HIT antibody test was positive, supporting the diagnosis of HIT, which became clinically apparent during UFH thromboprophylaxis.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: This case highlights HIT as an underrecognized complication of thromboprophylaxis during psychiatric restraint and underscores the diagnostic challenge of PE with pulmonary infarction mimicking pneumonia. Careful platelet monitoring during UFH therapy, regular pulse oximetry, and early suspicion of PE, even when pneumonia is initially suspected, are important in resource-limited psychiatric settings.

items.title: Peri-operative non-surgical determinants of prolonged length of stay following anterior cervical decompression and fusion surgery: a public healthcare perspective.
items.authors: Snowdon E, Raj Krishna G, Biswas S, Wood C, Dorey H, Cheng H, Devlin R, Suresh S, Mehdi SFSY, Sarkar V, George KJ.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Prolonged length of stay (PLOS) following anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) is associated with increased hospital burden. While surgical and comorbidity-related factors have been widely studied, routinely documented non-surgical and social variables are less consistently reported. This study evaluated univariable associations between these factors and PLOS after ACDF.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A retrospective analysis of 1,719 ACDF procedures performed between 2012 and 2022 at a single tertiary centre was conducted. Fifteen preoperative non-surgical and social variables were collected from routine records. PLOS was defined as > = 72 h. Chi-squared tests and unadjusted odds ratios (ORs) were used to evaluate associations with PLOS. No multivariable adjusted model was performed.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: PLOS occurred in 9.89% of cases. Eight factors were associated with post-operative LOS in univariable analysis: age > = 53 years (OR 1.99, p < 0.001), BMI > = 35 (OR 1.66, p = 0.016), ASA grade 3 (OR 4.31 vs ASA grade 1, p < 0.001), male sex (OR 0.64, p = 0.006), limited or aided mobility (OR 3.71, p < 0.001), presence of home social support (OR 0.58, p = 0.0036), chronic pain management issues (OR 3.69, p = 0.014), and recreational drug use (OR 0.23, p = 0.029). Smoking, alcohol use, accommodation type, exercise tolerance, and mental health status were not significantly associated with PLOS. The recreational drug use finding was unadjusted and should not be interpreted as protective.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Several routinely documented non-surgical and social factors were associated with PLOS following ACDF. These findings are hypothesis-generating and may support preoperative discharge planning. Adjusted analyses including operative level, indication, disease severity, complications and pathway variables are needed before these factors are used for day-case selection.

items.title: Brivaracetam in Off-Label Use and Special Populations: A Narrative Review of Current Evidence.
items.authors: Keramida A, Poprelka K, Mousdi M, Kotsali-Peteinelli V, Stefanou MI, Bonakis A, Tsivgoulis G, Kyrozis A, Tsalouchidou PE.

sections.text: Background: Brivaracetam (BRV) is a synaptic vesicle protein 2A (SV2A) ligand approved for the treatment of focal-onset seizures. Its clinical use has increasingly expanded beyond approved indications and into understudied populations. Objective: We aim to review BRV use beyond approved indications and in special populations. Methods: MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception to 30 April 2026. Eligible clinical studies were selected using prespecified criteria and synthesized narratively. Off-label status was determined separately under FDA and EMA labelling. Results: The evidence consisted predominantly of observational studies, real-world cohorts, case series, and subgroup analyses of randomised trials. In genetic generalized epilepsies (GGE), BRV was associated with seizure reduction in several cohorts, whereas findings in developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) were more heterogeneous. Real-world studies demonstrated the feasibility of BRV monotherapy, particularly following transition from levetiracetam. In status epilepticus (SE), intravenous BRV has been associated with SE cessation, although its independent contribution, optimal dose and timing, and role in treatment algorithms remain uncertain. Pregnancy and breastfeeding reports identified no clear safety signal, although exposure and long-term outcome data were scarce. Neonatal evidence was restricted largely to pharmacokinetic and short-term tolerability findings. Observational data indicated that psychiatric or behavioural adverse effects did not recur in some patients switched from levetiracetam; evidence in psychotic disorders remained particularly limited. Conclusions: BRV may be useful in selected off-label settings and special populations. However, evidence remains limited and largely observational, so treatment decisions should be individualized. Prospective controlled studies and dedicated registries are needed.

items.title: Neuropsychiatric Adverse Events Associated with Acyclovir, Valacyclovir, and Famciclovir: A Pharmacovigilance Study Using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS).
items.authors: Biten AA, Süel Eroğlu S, Çetin M, Çetin Ş.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: Acyclovir, valacyclovir, and famciclovir are widely used antiviral agents, but comparative data on neuropsychiatric adverse event reporting are limited. This study's aim was to compare neuropsychiatric adverse event reporting among acyclovir, valacyclovir, and famciclovir and to evaluate the influence of demographic and temporal factors. Methods: A retrospective pharmacovigilance analysis was conducted using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS, Q4 2003-Q3 2025). Unique reports in which acyclovir, valacyclovir, or famciclovir was the primary suspect drug were analyzed. Disproportionality was assessed using the reporting odds ratio (ROR), proportional reporting ratio (PRR), and information component (IC). Between-drug differences in the proportion of neuropsychiatric reports were examined using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, region (with Japan as a separate category), and reporting year, together with overlap and inverse probability weighting and sensitivity analyses. A narrow clinical phenotype (encephalopathy/neurotoxicity, altered consciousness/delirium, hallucination/psychosis, and seizure) was the primary outcome, and a broad System Organ Class (SOC)-based definition was a secondary outcome. Results: Of 16,071 unique primary-suspect reports (acyclovir, 6641; valacyclovir, 8980; famciclovir, 450), 4942 (30.8%) contained at least one nervous system or psychiatric Preferred Term (broad definition), and 2471 (15.4%) contained the narrow phenotype. All three drugs showed strong disproportionality signals for encephalopathy-related terms (e.g., toxic encephalopathy ROR 71.63 for acyclovir and 123.39 for valacyclovir; neurotoxicity ROR 55.74 and 48.57, respectively). For the primary narrow phenotype, reporting did not differ between valacyclovir and acyclovir (aOR 1.06, 95% CI 0.96-1.17) and was not higher for famciclovir (aOR 0.72, 95% CI 0.54-0.96; adjusted p = 0.055). Only with the secondary broad definition was the adjusted proportion of neuropsychiatric reports higher for valacyclovir (aOR 1.15, 95% CI 1.07-1.24) and famciclovir (aOR 1.41, 95% CI 1.14-1.75) than for acyclovir. The valacyclovir difference was confined to reports from Japan (aOR 1.88, 95% CI 1.52-2.33) and was absent elsewhere (aOR 1.06, 95% CI 0.98-1.15; interaction p < 0.001), whereas the famciclovir excess reflected non-specific terms such as dizziness and headache. Older age was independently associated with neuropsychiatric reporting (narrow phenotype: aOR 2.52, 95% CI 2.24-2.82). Conclusions: Acyclovir, valacyclovir, and famciclovir share a consistent, encephalopathy-dominated neuropsychiatric reporting signal in FAERS. Apparent between-drug differences depended on the case definition and on reports from Japan and should not be interpreted as differences in neurotoxic risk. Clinical vigilance for encephalopathy is warranted with all three agents, particularly in older patients, while recognizing that FAERS data cannot establish causality or absolute risk.

items.title: Psychometric Properties of the General Health Questionnaire (GHQ-12) Across Spain and Latin America: Factor Structure and Measurement Invariance.
items.authors: Escobar-Segovia K, Domínguez-Salas S, Allande-Cussó R, Del Pino-Peña R, Fagundo-Rivera J, Yıldırım M, El Khoury-Moreno L, Torrejón-Martínez J, Gómez-Salgado J.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Mental health assessment requires reliable and culturally sensitive instruments. The General Health Questionnaire (GHQ-12) is widely used to screen psychological distress, yet its psychometric properties show variability across cultural contexts. This study evaluates the psychometric properties of the GHQ-12 in Spanish-speaking populations from Spain and Latin America.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional, correlational study was conducted with 22,177 adults from 11 Spanish-speaking countries during the COVID-19 pandemic. Participants completed the GHQ-12, the Sense of Coherence scale (SOC-13), and a self-perceived health item. Confirmatory factor analyses (CFA) using mean-adjusted unweighted least squares (ULSM) compared one-, two-, and three-factor models. Measurement invariance (MI) of the best-fitting model was examined across countries. items.title: Evaluation of EQ-5D-5L and PROMIS-10 performance in older adults: data from the EQ-DAPHNIE project in five English-speaking countries.
items.authors: Nguyen TDB, Ohinmaa A, Short H, Al Sayah F.
items.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.text: This study evaluated the performance of the EQ-5D-5L and PROMIS^® Scale v1.2 - Global Health (PROMIS-10) in measuring health-related quality of life (HRQL) among older adults in five English-speaking countries.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Using cross-sectional data from the "EuroQol Data for Assessment of Population Health Needs and Instrument Evaluation" (EQ-DAPHNIE) project, 5399 respondents aged ≥65 years recruited via online panels from Canada, United States, United Kingdom, Australia, and New Zealand were included, with analyses conducted in each country. Convergent and divergent validity were assessed using correlations between similar and dissimilar constructs, and discriminative validity using the known-groups approach.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Respondents averaged 72.5 (SD 5.5) years and 48.2% were female. Mean EQ-5D-5L index ranged from 0.817 (0.145) in Canada to 0.880 (0.174) in Australia. Mean PROMIS Global Physical Health T-score ranged from 47.1 (SE 4.5) in Canada to 48.6 (4.6) in the UK. Mean PROMIS Global Mental Health T-score ranged from 49.3 (3.9) in Canada to 51.6 (4.0) in New Zealand. Of the 12 a-priori convergent and divergent validity hypotheses, 83-100% were confirmed for convergent validity while 100% were confirmed for divergent validity across the countries. Discriminative ability of the measures was strong in 94% of diseases. Both measures could also distinguish between multi-morbid and healthy individuals.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The findings support the construct validity of both the EQ-5D-5L and PROMIS-10 for assessing HRQL in relatively healthy, community-dwelling older adults in these countries. However, further research is needed to evaluate the performance and validity of these instruments in frail older adults and other clinically vulnerable elderly populations.

items.title: Effects of a virtual reality-based nature video intervention on sleep quality and mental well-being in patients with multiple sclerosis: a randomized controlled trial.
items.authors: Yağci Karamanli H, Bingöl N.

sections.heading: Background/aim
sections.text: Sleep quality and mental health are negatively affected in many patients with multiple sclerosis (MS). The study was conducted to evaluate the effects of virtual reality (VR) on sleep quality and mental well-being.

sections.heading: Materials and methods
sections.text: The study was designed as a randomized controlled trial. Data were collected from patients with MS who presented to a hospital in Türkiye. The study was completed by 21 participants in the experimental group and 22 participants in the control group. Participants in the experimental group watched nature videos using VR headsets for 6 weeks. Participants completed the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and the Warwick-Edinburgh Mental Well-Being Scale (WEMWBS). The study was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT06074419).

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Baseline PSQI and WEMWBS scores were similar between the experimental and control groups (p > 0.05). After the 6-week intervention, the mean total PSQI score was significantly lower in the experimental group than in the control group (p = 0.024), with a moderate-to-large effect size (Cohen's d = 0.679), indicating improved sleep quality. Additionally, the mean WEMWBS score was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p = 0.047), with a moderate-to-large effect size (Cohen's d = 0.687), indicating improved mental well-being. Overall, the VR-based nature video intervention was associated with improvements in sleep quality and mental well-being.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: The VR-based nature video intervention may enhance the quality of nursing care for patients with MS. While the VR-based nature video intervention may enhance nursing care for patients with MS, the absence of any intervention in the comparison group prevents the specific effects of VR from being fully distinguished from placebo or novelty effects. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted with caution. Further research is required to confirm these findings and support their implementation in clinical practice.
