items.title: Associations Between Companion Animal Caregiving Characteristics and Perceived Stress Among Chinese Older Adults: A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study.
items.authors: Xie C, Ruan Y, Jin M, Pan J.

sections.text: Objectives: Pet ownership may affect older adults' health in multiple ways, yet its specific association with perceived stress remains unclear. From a One Welfare perspective, this study examined associations between companion-animal ownership, diverse companion animal caregiving characteristics, and perceived stress among Chinese older adults. Methods: A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted among older adults recruited from five provinces in China between August 2024 and January 2025. Perceived stress was measured using the 14-item Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-14) among 1428 eligible participants aged 60 years or older. Multiple linear regression models were used to examine these associations, adjusting for sociodemographic, socioeconomic, and health-related confounders. Results: In fully adjusted models, companion-animal ownership was associated with significantly lower perceived stress compared with non-ownership. Stratified analyses showed that this association was significant only among exclusive dog owners. Longer ownership duration (>3 years) and frequent hands-on pet care were also associated with lower perceived stress. In contrast, frequent pet illness and weekly dog walking were linked to higher perceived stress. Conclusions: Pet ownership, particularly exclusive dog ownership and long-term companionship, was significantly associated with lower perceived stress in Chinese older adults. However, caregiving burdens, such as managing pet illness and weekly dog walking, may partly explain the weaker observed associations. These findings offered localized empirical evidence and highlighted the need for targeted support systems that consider both older adults' mental health and companion-animal welfare within a One Welfare framework.

items.title: "We Don't Go Abroad for a Vacation": A Qualitative Study Exploring Job Stress and Mental Health Literacy of Overseas Filipino Workers in Thailand.
items.authors: Miranda GMJ, Phukao D, Sherer PP.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Mental health literacy (MHL) could effectively mitigate job stress among Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs). However, within the growing population of OFWs in Thailand, knowledge about perceptions, experiences, and influences on job stress and mental health literacy is limited. There is a need to understand these experiences in order to improve how MHL programs could be applied in this context and population.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: The study aimed to explore experiences related to job stress and MHL among eight (8) OFWs in Thailand.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Drawing from an interpretive qualitative approach with reflexive thematic analysis, OFW respondents were purposively recruited from various church groups and nine online communities for Thailand-based Filipinos. The study utilized key informant interviews conducted in either face-to-face or online format using a semi-structured interview format. Responses were analyzed using Braun and Clarke's six-step reflexive thematic analysis framework. Ethical guidelines were implemented throughout the course of the study.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Results of the thematic analysis revealed three themes: experience of job stress, reasons for job stress, and MHL. Family obligations served as a major influence in the contextualization of mental health and stress, while job stress was more profound when social interactions with co-workers were involved. Findings also revealed that participants could exercise coping through social support and religiosity. Visa-related issues, workplace interactions, and perceptions related to wage discrimination were unique findings within the context of Thailand.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: In Thailand, various personal and sociocultural factors impact OFWs' experiences and perceptions of job stress and mental health literacy. Findings from this study could be used to guide the conduct of comparative and intervention-based research related to stress experiences of OFWs.

items.title: Balancing needs and resources in mental health care through the lens of public and provider perspectives.
items.authors: Abu-Ras W, Idris LB, Al-Quraini M, Amin S.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Telemental health care (TMHC) may offer convenient and private pathways to mental health support, but its feasibility and acceptability depend on the cultural, structural, and operational context in which it is delivered. This qualitative study examined how members of the general population and mental health professionals perceived the barriers and opportunities associated with TMHC in Qatar.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This qualitative study employed semi-structured interviews with 62 participants, comprising members of the general population (n = 34) and mental health professionals (n = 28), using purposive and snowball sampling strategies. Participants were recruited through social media, community outreach, and clinical networks. The study used reflexive thematic analysis, following Braun and Clarke's six-phase approach to identify recurring patterns and generate nuanced, interpretive themes.

sections.heading: Findings
sections.text: Four themes were identified: (1) Cultural Stigma and Social Perceptions of Mental Illness, describing how participants perceived stigma, gender norms, and family reputation as shaping help-seeking and TMHC acceptability; (2) Structural and Logistical Barriers to Mental Health Access, including perceived concerns about wait times, cost, digital literacy, and TMHC infrastructure; (3) Relational Dynamics and Therapeutic Trust in Virtual Care, reflecting concerns that limited provider preparation and discomfort with virtual communication could weaken therapeutic engagement; and (4) Opportunities and Pathways for Culturally Responsive TMHC Integration, emphasizing participants' recommendations for mental health education, provider training, community engagement, and culturally responsive service development.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Participants perceived TMHC as a potentially useful complement to in-person services, particularly because of its convenience and privacy, while identifying stigma, digital access, confidentiality, and relational trust as important barriers. These findings identify context-specific considerations for future TMHC development and evaluation in Qatar; they do not establish TMHC effectiveness or population-level effects on access.

items.title: Gut Microbiota-Associated Molecules in Plasma-Derived Extracellular Vesicle-Enriched Fractions of Patients with Parkinson's Disease.
items.authors: Celik U, Elibol B, Beker M, Kalkan Cakmak R, Ercin N, Sarikamis-Johnson B, Karacan I, Babacan Yildiz G.

sections.text: Background: Microbiota-related metabolites and innate immune signaling molecules transported via plasma-derived extracellular vesicle (EV)-enriched fractions through the gut-brain axis may contribute to neuroinflammation and disease progression in Parkinson's disease (PD). Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the levels of microbiota-associated molecules in plasma-derived EV-enriched fractions and their relationship with clinical parameters in patients with PD. Methods: This study included 38 patients with PD and 38 age-matched healthy spouses. Clinical evaluations, disease staging (Hoehn & Yahr, UPDRS), and cognitive/psychiatric tests (MMSE, BDI, BAI) were conducted. Uncorrected spot urinary indoxyl sulfate concentration and routine serum biochemical markers were analyzed. Plasma-derived EV-enriched fractions were isolated and analyzed for microbiota-related molecules (acetate, TLR2, TLR4, TLR5, LPS, and EGF) using ELISA and functional assays. Results: Clinical evaluations indicated mild-to-moderate disease severity in PD patients. Systemic analyses revealed elevated uncorrected spot urinary indoxyl sulfate alongside reduced serum folate, vitamin B12, and free T4, together with increased copper, iron, and zinc levels in PD. Acetate, LPS, TLR2, and TLR5 levels in the plasma-derived EV-enriched fractions were significantly upregulated. Exploratory correlation analyses (none significant after FDR correction) suggested that lower serum folate and TLR4 levels in the plasma-derived EV-enriched fractions were associated with higher motor symptom severity and treatment complications. ROC analyses showed that TLR2 levels in the plasma-derived EV-enriched fractions had the highest observed AUC among the evaluated markers for PD. Conclusions: In this exploratory cross-sectional study, patients with PD showed differences in microbiota-related molecules (acetate, LPS; urinary indoxyl sulfate as an uncorrected spot concentration) and host-associated innate immune markers (TLR2, TLR5) in plasma-derived EV-enriched fractions, and TLR2 had the highest observed AUC among the evaluated markers. These findings are compatible with, but do not demonstrate, a contribution of the gut microbiota to PD; vesicular association, microbial origin, and causality were not established. Whether dietary or other microbiota-targeted interventions could be beneficial remains an open question for future longitudinal and interventional studies.

items.title: A Multi-Task Learning Framework for Balancing Mental Health and Social Media Usage using Digital Behavioural Data.
items.authors: Swarna SN, D BM, B P, Prathap BR.

sections.text: The fast advancement in technology is constantly changing how people live and having a greater impaction than ever before. Various human emotional changes are largely associated with the evolution of new technology. Instead of treating these changes differently, the contemporary methods predict methods one at a time, this can lead to the loss of common triggers across them. This kind of partitioned approach can lead to the overall weaker predictions. This approach moves ahead by combining those tasks into a single system that learns them all together by using daily life features. Using information like how someone sleeps, their screen habits, and productivity throughout the day, it is found that neural networks with attention mechanisms can predict multiple tasks simultaneously. Each task focuses on its own attention mechanisms that allow it to pick out essential aspects of the latent representation and ignoring noise from the non-relevant tasks' latent representations. Such system can predict numerical outcomes connected to mental wellness, attention, and screen dependence and even predict binary classifications connected with the detection of mental health concerns. Each of these networks works as intended, with strong results in predicting attention and screen usage patterns and binary classifications regarding mental health concerns. By training these networks on multiple tasks simultaneously through multi-task learning approaches with attention mechanisms focusing on individual tasks' needs, stronger results emerge as compared to state-of-the-art single-task learning models. Compared to baseline and ablation studies. this multi-task attention learning model outperforms less complicated approaches with an accuracy of 85.86%. Hence, there is significant proof from the test set to show the strength of multi-task learning with attention focused on individual tasks when analyzing aspects like general view mental wellness. What stands out is that the system built here could grow easily, fitting into digital tools meant to track mental health while spotting risks earlier and tailoring insights to individuals.

items.title: Using Systems Thinking to Address Diet, Food Systems and Mental Health in a Caribbean Small Island Developing State.
items.authors: Brown CR, Guariguata L, Guell C, Campbell MH, Murphy MM.

sections.text: Small island developing states face distinct vulnerabilities driving a nutrition transition toward ultra-processed imports. While global evidence links food security and diet to mental health, Caribbean research remains limited and linear. This study maps dynamic feedback loops governing the food system-mental health nexus in St. Lucia to identify potential leverage points for intervention. Qualitative data were translated into a preliminary causal loop diagram, which was refined using literature triangulation and a group model refinement workshop with multisectoral stakeholders, and finally benchmarked against the World Health Organization's Food Systems Delivering Better Health guide. Four major feedback loops included diet choices and health; local foods and cultural identity; food security and purchasing behaviours; and farming and community. Local food consumption, market shopping and food sharing build social capital, cultural pride and psychological resilience. Conversely, reliance on imported processed foods, food insecurity, and systemic agricultural shocks exacerbate mental distress. Participants proposed multisectoral interventions spanning the socioecological model of health. Interventions should target these systems-informed structural drivers to effectively safeguard population mental health. However, the potential utility of interventions cannot be established without quantitative testing, such as modelling to test leverage points amidst surrounding constraints.

Qualitative data were translated into a preliminary causal loop diagram, which was refined using literature triangulation and a group model refinement workshop with multisectoral stakeholders, and finally benchmarked against the World Health Organization's Food Systems Delivering Better Health guide. Four major feedback loops included diet choices and health; local foods and cultural identity; food security and purchasing behaviours; and farming and community. Local food consumption, market shopping and food sharing build social capital, cultural pride and psychological resilience. Conversely, reliance on imported processed foods, food insecurity, and systemic agricultural shocks exacerbate mental distress. Participants proposed multisectoral interventions spanning the socioecological model of health. Interventions should target these systems-informed structural drivers to effectively safeguard population mental health. However, the potential utility of interventions cannot be established without quantitative testing, such as modelling to test leverage points amidst surrounding constraints.

items.title: System-level challenges and unmet needs in profound autism: an exploratory caregiver survey of non-verbal individuals.
items.authors: Narzisi A, Pizzino F, Cioni G, Milone A, Masi G.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Individuals with profound autism, particularly those with minimal or absent verbal communication, frequently present with very high levels of clinical complexity and support needs. Despite increasing recognition of this subgroup, little is known about the real-world experiences of families and the adequacy of current service systems in responding to these needs. The present study aimed to characterize the lived experience, clinical complexity, and unmet needs of parents of non-verbal individuals with autism within a defined territorial context.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional descriptive survey study was conducted in a defined Italian catchment area. A structured caregiver questionnaire including 128 items across ten thematic domains was administered online. The present analysis was restricted to parents of non-verbal individuals with autism (n = 24), representing the non-verbal subgroup within the broader profound autism population. Domains included diagnostic pathways, medical comorbidities, daily functioning, therapeutic interventions, healthcare access, sensory profile, educational context, and family impact. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and exploratory bivariate analyses.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Parents described a profile characterized by severe functional dependence, pervasive communication impairment, and high levels of medical and behavioral complexity. Sleep disturbances were reported in 75.0% of cases, epilepsy in 20.8%, and current pharmacological treatment in 58.3%. Difficulty recognizing medical conditions because of communication limitations was reported as moderate to extreme in 91.7% of cases. Service use was characterized by heavy reliance on private interventions and limited availability of respite care. Public intervention intensity was low, while substantial family-level impacts were reported in caregiver employment and social participation. Aggressive and self-injurious behaviors were common, and more than half of families reported the need for physical containment at least occasionally.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: The data indicate a potential mismatch between the high and multidimensional support needs of non-verbal individuals with autism and the intensity and availability of formal support. The observed pattern was characterized by low levels of publicly funded intervention, heavy reliance on private care, limited access to respite and home assistance, and marked family-level impacts. These findings support the need to examine how integrated and lifespan-oriented models of care can better address the needs of individuals with profound autism and absent verbal communication.

items.title: Physical exercise and social avoidance and distress among college students: a cross-sectional examination of the chain mediating role of body image and psychological capital.
items.authors: Cao X, Li J, Zhang W, Zhang X.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Social avoidance and distress (SAD) impairs interpersonal functioning among university students, yet the pathways through which modifiable health behaviors are associated with SAD remain poorly specified. Prior work has treated the two mainly as parallel mediators, leaving open whether they operate in sequence. This study tested whether the two are ordered sequentially in their indirect association with SAD.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: A cross-sectional sample of 671 Chinese undergraduates completed the Physical Activity Rating Scale-3, the Social Avoidance and Distress Scale, the Body Appreciation Scale-2 and the Psychological Capital Questionnaire-24. Measurement validity was established by confirmatory factor analysis before the mediation analysis, which used PROCESS Model 6 with 5,000 bias-corrected bootstrap resamples and a mediator ordering specified in advance on theoretical grounds.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Physical exercise was positively associated with body image (β = 0.12) and psychological capital (β = 0.11), and negatively with SAD (r = -0.15). The serial indirect pathway through body image and then psychological capital was significant (-0.014, 95% CI [-0.026, -0.003]), accounting for 9.3% of the total association.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: Physical exercise was associated with lower SAD, and this association was statistically consistent with an indirect pathway through more positive body image and, in turn, greater psychological capital. These findings delineate a sequential psychological pathway linking physical exercise to social functioning and identify two modifiable targets for physical education and mental-health services in higher education.

items.title: Azo-dye adulteration of palm oil: occurrence, detection, toxicological implications, and regulatory gaps.
items.authors: Salimon SS, Ayinla A, Amoah AS, Yakubu RO, Pustovalova MV.

sections.text: The fraudulent adulteration of palm oil with synthetic azo dyes, such as Sudan I-IV and Metanil Yellow, represents a critical, under-reported global public health crisis. Driven by economic arbitrage, illicit vendors utilize these industrial textile colorants to mask oil degradation and simulate a premium, carotene-rich aesthetic. While the immediate chemical fraud is well-documented, this review synthesizes the available mechanistic evidence on plausible insidious, multi-systemic physiological degradation associated with chronic dietary exposure to these dyes, even though, there is currently no direct human epidemiological confirmation. Azo-dyes undergo microbial reduction by enteric bacteria, cleaving their characteristic -N=N- bonds to generate highly carcinogenic aromatic amines. This process induces profound gut dysbiosis, degrading the mucosal barrier and driving systemic endotoxemia. Concurrently, these lipophilic compounds act as potent endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs), destabilizing estrogen receptors and mimicking reproductive hormones. At the cellular level, xenobiotic detoxification overburdens hepatic and renal pathways, generating massive reactive oxygen species (ROS) that disrupt mitochondrial function, facilitating DNA adduct formation, and promote irreversible lipid peroxidation. Permeating the blood-brain barrier (BBB), dye metabolites further provoke neuroinflammation, potentially altering neurotransmitter synthesis via the gut-brain axis to impact mental health. On current evidence, vulnerable, low-income populations reliant on unbranded open-market staples bear a disproportionate share of exposure to these adulterants, though population-level health impact has not been directly quantified. Mitigating this crisis demands a paradigm shift: transitioning from standard laboratory chromatography to rapid, decentralized field-screening technologies, alongside stringent blockchain-backed supply chain traceability and aggressive policy enforcement. Ultimately, addressing azo-dye adulteration of palm oil requires an integrated framework combining advanced analytical chemistry, robust regulatory intervention, and widespread consumer education.

items.title: Navigating stigma before and after an endometriosis diagnosis: A qualitative study on medical stigma and healthcare-seeking behavior with endometriosis in a German sample.
items.authors: Eitze S, Rose S, Best S.

sections.text: Endometriosis is a chronic and often misunderstood condition that exposes affected individuals to public stigma. This qualitative interview study explored how experienced public stigma by healthcare experts shapes women's self-stigma before and after diagnosis and if women change health behaviors after public stigma was experienced and/or self stigma developed. In-depth interviews were conducted with recently diagnosed participants, focusing on public and self-stigma and their impact on health behaviors. Findings show that early and repeated exposure to stigma eroded trust in medical professionals, led to withdrawal from care, and fostered hyper-independence. Receiving a diagnosis provided both validation and emotional strain-strengthening self-confidence for some, while reinforcing distress for others. The study underscores the need for improved awareness and stigma-sensitive communication in healthcare to foster patient-centered, empathetic support and better outcomes for individuals with endometriosis.

items.title: Academic Stress and Mental Well-Being Among Undergraduate Students: A Scoping Review.
items.authors: Wan Omar WN, Atarhim MA, Zakaria R, Mansor NI, Hussein SZ, Abdul Khaiyom JH.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: Academic stress is a recognised threat to the mental health of undergraduate students, and higher stress and psychological distress were reported during the COVID-19 pandemic. This scoping review mapped the global evidence on reported levels and prevalence estimates of academic stress, its associated factors, and related mental health outcomes. Methods: Following PRISMA-ScR and Arksey and O'Malley's framework, we searched MEDLINE, CINAHL, Academic Search Complete and Business Source Complete (all via EBSCOhost), PubMed, and Scopus for peer-reviewed quantitative studies published between 2018 and 2024. Eighteen studies were charted and summarised narratively. Results: Most studies reported moderate to high academic stress, although instruments and cut-off values varied widely. In the largest multinational study, 93.7% of first-year students reported at least one major stressor. Female students more often reported higher academic stress, and one study found higher stress and poorer well-being among non-binary students. Higher academic stress was associated with depressive symptoms, anxiety, burnout, and poorer well-being. Conclusions: Academic stress is widely reported among undergraduates and is consistently associated with poorer mental health. Multilevel strategies addressing academic demands, coping skills, and institutional support are evidence-informed priorities that still require longitudinal and intervention evaluation, in line with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-Being) and SDG 4 (Quality Education).

items.title: Long-Term Cardiopulmonary Sequelae and Rehabilitation After MERS-CoV and COVID-19: A Narrative Review from a Saudi Perspective.
items.authors: Alruwaili R, Albelasi A, Alqahtani MM.

sections.text: Saudi Arabia has carried the largest global burden of Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) and a substantial burden of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), the cause of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). This narrative review, written from the perspectives of clinical immunology and cardiopulmonary rehabilitation, synthesises evidence on long-term sequelae (persisting for at least 3 months) and rehabilitation after MERS-CoV infection and COVID-19, with implications for Saudi Arabia. MERS-CoV survivors show reduced diffusing capacity for at least 12 months, radiographic lung fibrosis in about one-third of recovering patients at short-term follow-up, and high rates of chronic fatigue, depression and post-traumatic stress. A dedicated search of six databases and registries (355 records) found no study of a rehabilitation intervention after MERS-CoV infection. Because most MERS-CoV survivors with sequelae were critically ill, evidence on post-intensive care syndrome and acute respiratory distress syndrome is the closest basis for extrapolation; it shows persistent disability but uncertain benefit from generic post-discharge programmes. After COVID-19, randomised trials show that rehabilitation improves functional capacity, dyspnoea and quality of life, while post-exertional malaise, autonomic dysfunction and myocardial involvement require screening and symptom-titrated or cardiology-guided care. We propose a phenotype-directed rehabilitation pathway with explicit screening criteria, adapted to Saudi factors that include Vision 2030 reforms and virtual care, high metabolic comorbidity, a hot climate, women's access to physical activity and occupational groups at risk of MERS-CoV, and a research agenda that includes MERS-CoV survivor registries and rehabilitation trials.

items.title: When Professional Commitment Is Not Enough: Implementation Lessons from a RE-AIM-Guided Qualitative Study of Adolescent Primary Care Access in Brazil.
items.authors: Paiva Neto FT, Gonçalves Marques R, Costa Santos KV, Ferreira Marcondes CÁ, Moscardini Batarra J, da Costa Palacio D, Borella AC, Crucello da Silva P, Rangel M, Godoi L.

sections.heading: Background/objectives
sections.text: Adolescents are among the least likely to receive primary health care (PHC), even where services are formally available. In Brazil, a companion quantitative evaluation of Chega Junto, a quality-improvement initiative in a socioeconomically vulnerable urban community, documented significant and sustained gains in adolescent access but could not explain how these gains were achieved or why they proved so difficult to sustain. This study examined health professionals' implementation experiences, using the RE-AIM framework (Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, Maintenance) to identify the conditions shaping adolescent access and its sustainability.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Focus groups were conducted with 11 health professionals across three PHC units (Unidades Básicas de Saúde, UBS) in Paraisópolis, São Paulo, Brazil. Transcripts underwent inductive-deductive thematic analysis guided by RE-AIM, with reporting following the COREQ criteria; the study is the qualitative component of a mixed-methods evaluation.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Adolescent reach was built on trust-based therapeutic bonds and the explicit recognition of adolescents' right to consult independently, rather than on increasing the number of outreach contacts. Formal goals, including vaccination, were met. Yet, unaddressed psychosocial and mental-health needs exposed the limits of a numerically bounded scope. Adoption was strong and grounded in participatory co-design, reorienting professionals toward adolescents as autonomous rights-holders. Implementation was enabled by intersectoral partnerships but undermined by productivity metrics that rendered relational work invisible.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Adolescent PHC access depended on relational and organizational conditions that standard metrics fail to capture; sustaining it requires institutional redesign as a foundational precondition rather than an afterthought.

items.title: Nurses' Perceptions on the Use of Mechanical Restraint in Mental Health Facilities: A Narrative Review.
items.authors: Alharbi OA, Ellis K, Hinchliff S.
items.journal: International journal of mental health nursing

sections.text: Mechanical restraint remains a complex practice in some mental health care, requiring nurses to balance safety with ethical and therapeutic considerations. Mechanical restraint refers to the use of devices to restrict a person's movement or ability to freely move parts or all of their body. Previous reviews have reported nurses' negative feelings and ethical conflicts regarding restraint, alongside perceptions of its necessity when less restrictive alternatives were perceived as unavailable. However, a focused qualitative synthesis specifically exploring mechanical restraint can complement this evidence by providing a more in-depth understanding of nurses' perceptions of this practice. This narrative review aimed to explore nurses' perceptions of mechanical restraint in mental health facilities. Four databases were searched for qualitative studies published between 2014 and 2024 (chosen to capture the most current state of knowledge), which identified 950 records, and after screening 13 were included in this review. The findings highlighted that nurses viewed mechanical restraint as necessary to prevent immediate physical harm to patients or staff. They also reported that mechanical restraint could have both a physical and emotional impact on staff and patients, related to concerns about patient well-being, ethical and professional conflict, and reduced trust and increased distance between patients and nurses. Workload, the availability of sufficient and qualified nursing staff, and access to training in restraint prevention and safe restraint practices were factors that influenced nurses' views about mechanical restraint. These findings shed light on the impact of mechanical restraint for mental health nurses and can inform organisational approaches that support nurses and promote education in trauma-informed care, recovery-oriented practice and restraint-reduction strategies including, Safewards model and the 6-Core Strategies.

items.title: Spatial distribution and factors associated with availability of mental health services in Ethiopia: data from national health-facility survey.
items.authors: Tusa BS, Alati R, Ayano G, Getnet F, Dachew B.
items.journal: International journal of mental health systems

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Despite the substantial burden of mental health disorders in Ethiopia, access to mental health services remains limited and unevenly distributed. This study aimed to examine the spatial distribution of mental health services in Ethiopian health facilities and identify factors contributing to their availability.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Data were drawn from the 2021-2022 Ethiopian Service Provision Assessment-Plus (ESPA+) survey, which included a census of hospitals and a representative sample of health centres, posts, and clinics. Spatial patterns were assessed using the Global Moran's Index (Moran's I) to evaluate spatial autocorrelation, while hotspot analysis employing Getis-Ord Gi* statistics identified areas with high and low service availability. A Poisson regression was conducted to assess factors associated with mental health service availability.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Analysis of 1,158 health facilities revealed a significant clustering of mental health services in Ethiopia, with a Global Moran's I value of 0.09 (P < 0.01). Hotspot analysis identified areas of high mental health service availability in Addis Ababa, central and south-western Oromia, and north-western Amhara, while areas with low availability were found in Afar, Benishangul-Gumuz, Gambella, Harari, Dire Dawa, northern Somali, and northern SNNPR. Factors negatively associated with mental health service availability included rural location, primary facility status, a small catchment population (< 10,000), and facilities charging service fees.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text: This study highlights significant disparities in the availability of mental health services in Ethiopia, particularly in rural and underserved regions. Expanding mental health services within primary healthcare units, and revisiting task-shifting strategies to mitigate shortages in the mental health workforce may help to improve access to mental health care. Integrating innovative delivery models,such as telemedicine and community-based initiatives,will be helpful in fostering equitable mental healthcare nationwide.

This study highlights significant disparities in the availability of mental health services in Ethiopia, particularly in rural and underserved regions. Expanding mental health services within primary healthcare units, and revisiting task-shifting strategies to mitigate shortages in the mental health workforce may help to improve access to mental health care. Integrating innovative delivery models,such as telemedicine and community-based initiatives,will be helpful in fostering equitable mental healthcare nationwide.

items.title: Three Pathogenic Axes Underlying Prurigo Nodularis and Its Systemic Comorbidities.
items.authors: Hara R, Nguyen TM, Saito-Sasaki N, Sawada Y.

sections.text: Prurigo nodularis (PN) is a chronic inflammatory skin disease characterized by severe pruritus and hyperkeratotic nodules. Growing epidemiological evidence indicates that PN is associated with a broad spectrum of systemic comorbidities, including cardiovascular, thyroid, renal, hepatic, psychiatric, pulmonary, and skeletal disorders. However, the biological mechanisms underlying these associations remain incompletely understood. In this review, we propose a framework comprising three interconnected pathogenic axes underlying PN: immune dysregulation, neural dysregulation, and tissue remodeling. Type 2 and type 17 inflammatory pathways, neuroimmune interactions, and fibroblast-mediated extracellular matrix remodeling contribute to PN pathogenesis, while selected immune-inflammatory and remodeling pathways may also have extracutaneous relevance. In particular, IL-4, IL-13, IL-17, and IL-31 may participate in inflammatory and remodeling processes across multiple organs. Although current evidence does not establish a causal relationship between PN and its systemic comorbidities, integration of epidemiological and mechanistic findings supports a broader view of PN beyond the skin. This three-axis framework may provide a conceptual basis for future studies aimed at identifying biomarkers, clarifying systemic disease risk, and defining the clinical relevance of shared pathogenic pathways in PN-associated comorbidities.

items.title: Mental health care research priorities for trans and gender-diverse young people: Findings from community consultations on improving trauma-related mental health care for trans and gender-diverse communities.
items.authors: Walker M, Ballendine O, Heit L, Lachowsky N, Devor A.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Research on mental health care with trans and gender-diverse (TGD) people presents unique challenges as it brings together two historically complex contexts for TGD communities. While ethical standards and recommendations for research do exist (e.g. Bauer et al., 2019; Puckett et al., 2023, Veale et al., 2022), it is only recently that there has been a turn toward community-engaged research, with communities calling for research led by TGD people and focused on community goals and needs.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: This article presents findings from a qualitative, community-based project on TGD young people's priorities for future research related to improving trauma-related mental health care. Thirty-four participants engaged across two data collection activities: in-person workshops; and online, semi-structured interviews. Eligibility criteria included: identifying as trans or gender-diverse; being aged 19-30 and having experience accessing, attending, or needing trauma-related mental health supports in British Columbia. Participants shared their experiences with trauma-related mental health care and their priorities for improving mental health care more broadly for TGD communities.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Research priorities included: Practitioner Education and Training; Indigenous Perspectives; Addressing Racism and Cultural Differences; Impact of Geography; Co-Occurring Needs; Understanding Trauma; Disability, Autism, and Neurodivergence; Pathways to Care; and Approaches to Therapy. Participants emphasized that research should be led by TGD communities who are impacted by the research and needs to be based on community priorities.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.text: These findings provide novel insight from young TGD people into community priorities that can guide future research on mental health care. Findings suggest that future researchers be strategic in building projects that shift the focus from research on TGD people to research that focuses on mental health practitioners, practice approaches, and frameworks that acknowledge the multifaceted lived experiences of TGD people. Future research should pushback against deficit-focused narratives and an over-focus on harm experienced by TGD people.

items.title: Interpretation and Translation-Mediated Telemental Health Services for Adults With Limited Language Proficiency: Scoping Review.
items.authors: Lui F, Gany F, Espinosa A, Riobó C, Zhao C, Gao Z, Qi C, Chen RY, Jiang R, Chang F, Boyce L, Diamond L, Gonzalez J, Leng J.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Individuals with limited English proficiency (LEP) or limited host-language proficiency (LLP) represent a growing, medically underserved population at disproportionate risk for poor mental health outcomes. Most mental and behavioral health services provided to individuals with LEP or LLP are delivered by providers who do not speak the patient's preferred language, due to a shortage of bilingual mental health professionals. Since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, the number of telehealth-delivered outpatient mental health (telemental) visits has increased, yet little is understood about the provision of interpretation and/or translation-facilitated telemental health care in populations with LEP and LLP.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: This study is a scoping review that aimed to characterize the existing evidence on interpretation- and translation-mediated telemental health services for adults with LEP or LLP. We examined study characteristics, populations, and settings represented, telemental health modalities used, reported barriers and facilitators, and the methodological quality and gaps within the current evidence base.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Included studies focused on adults receiving interpreter and/or translation-mediated telemental health services. All studies were published in the English language, which may limit generalizability. Studies with bilingual providers, nonbehavioral health care, mobile health (mHealth) applications, or deaf or hard-of-hearing populations were excluded. Online databases were used to identify papers published through May 2026, from which we selected 15 publications from 137 full-text articles retrieved for full-text screening.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: A total of 60% (9/15) of publications reported qualitative or mixed method designs, while 40% (6/15) were quantitative. Most were conducted with Spanish-speaking populations. Of the 15 studies, 12 achieved >4 out of 5 using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Thematic analysis yielded the following four themes across the articles reviewed: (1) facilitators of access, (2) barriers to access, (3) therapeutic process considerations, and (4) recommendations to improve quality of and access to interpreter- or translation-mediated telemental health care in LEP and LLP populations.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: As previous reviews focused primarily on in-person mental health care, this scoping review is among the first to synthesize evidence specifically on interpreter and translation-mediated telemental health for individuals with LEP or LLP. In addition, its inclusion of literature published after COVID-19 allowed for an examination of how the literature has evolved from the prepandemic period to the post-2020 telemental health expansion. Findings underscored the following needs: (1) address access barriers to telemental health care in populations with LEP and LLP, which persist following the postpandemic increase in telemental health adoption; (2) standardize training for clinicians and interpreters; and (3) update clinical guidelines in the context of rapid telehealth uptake in behavioral health care. It also highlighted the potential impact of emerging AI technologies for real-time translation in mental health care, calling for further research on their ethical and clinical implications.

items.title: Correlation of Telomere Length with Cognitive Function, Muscle Strength, and Quality of Life in Normal-Weight and Obese Female Participants.
items.authors: Nonsa-Ard R, Aneknan P, Tong-Un T, Manimmanakorn A, Tunkamnerdthai O, Honsawek S, Alkhatib A, Leelayuwat C, Leelayuwat N.

sections.text: Research linking obesity to cellular aging-associated declines in cognitive, physical, and mental health is limited. This cross-sectional study compared relative blood leukocyte telomere length (RTL), cognition (Montreal Cognitive Assessment), fat-free mass, muscle strength, and health-related quality of life between 68 normal-weight and 66 obese Thai women, while exploring the associations between RTL and these outcomes. The results show that the obese group exhibited significantly shorter RTL, alongside lower body mass-normalized fat-free mass and body mass-normalized hand grip strength, higher absolute hand grip strength, and lower scores in specific physical health-related quality of life subdomains compared to the normal-weight group. The adjusted correlation revealed that RTL was positively related to social functioning in the normal-weight group. However, tests for group interaction showed no significant differences in RTL-outcome relationships between groups. Furthermore, there were no longer significant following false discovery rate correction across both groups. These findings suggest that while obesity is associated with shortened cellular aging markers, reduced muscle mass and strength, and diminished physical function, it does not significantly moderate the link between RTL and these health outcomes. Studies with larger sample sizes may be needed to detect potential subtle interaction effects.

items.title: Iliopsoas Abscess-Advances in Diagnosis and Treatment.
items.authors: Pîrvu MD, Popa CC, Grasa CN, Popescu CG, Ardeleanu V.

sections.text: (1) Background: The iliopsoas abscess is a rare condition with potentially severe evolution, secondary to hematogenous or lymphatic dissemination (primary) or secondary to trauma, vertebral, renal, or gastrointestinal infections. Due to its deep anatomical location and varied etiology, it represents a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge, requiring a multidisciplinary approach (surgery, neurosurgery, orthopedics, urology, imaging, infectious diseases, rheumatology, physical medicine, psychology and psychiatry). The aim is to synthesize the clinical and paraclinical particularities and to update modern diagnostic and treatment methods. (2) Methods: A narrative literature review was conducted using the PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases, including relevant articles addressing the aspects mentioned above. Available evidence remains heterogeneous and is derived predominantly from retrospective and observational studies, limiting direct comparisons between treatment modalities. (3) Results: Elements of etiological, clinical, and paraclinical diagnosis are presented, together with complex therapeutic options, both medical and surgical. All modern drainage methods are highlighted, including interventional imaging, minimally invasive techniques, endoscopic treatment (laparoscopic and retroperitoneoscopic), direct drainage through the inferior lumbar triangle (Jean-Louis Petit), as well as open surgical treatment. Immediate and long-term postoperative management, physical and functional rehabilitation, and psychological and psychiatric support complete the multidisciplinary approach. (4) Conclusions: Ultimately, increasing awareness of this often-debilitating condition contributes to reducing morbidity and mortality.

items.title: Multimodal Detection of Cognitive Impairment in Non-Neurological Rehabilitation Settings: The COGinREHAB Study Protocol.
items.authors: Della Bella S, Martinelli G, Pavan E, Trimarchi PD, Comanducci A, Ingannato A, Bagnoli S, Nacmias B, Guerini FR, Saresella M, Abbate C, Sorbi S, Gallucci A, Polito C, COGinREHAB Study Group.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: Cognitive impairment is highly prevalent among hospitalised adults but often remains under-recognised, particularly in non-neurological rehabilitation settings where clinical attention is mainly focused on physical recovery. Undetected cognitive impairment may adversely affect rehabilitation outcomes, functional recovery, and long-term care planning. Methods: A multicentre, prospective, longitudinal study, with a single-group assignment and a diagnostic purpose, will be conducted across three rehabilitation centres of the Don Carlo Gnocchi Foundation (Italy), enrolling 384 patients aged ≥45 years without severe psychiatric or neurological disorders, other than cognitive impairment, admitted to cardiac, pulmonary, orthopaedic rehabilitation, or intermediate care units for non-neurological conditions. At baseline (T0), all participants will undergo standardised clinical and cognitive screening. Individuals with suspected cognitive impairment, operationally defined as an Equivalent Score (ES) of 1 on the Montreal Cognitive Assessment-MoCA total score and/or an ES of 0 or 1 on at least one MoCA cognitive domain, including the Memory Index Score (MIS), and a random sample of those without, will undergo a comprehensive neuropsychological assessment. Participants with neuropsychologically defined cognitive impairment, based on objective deficits in the comprehensive neuropsychological assessment, will undergo plasma biomarker testing (GFAP, NfL, pTau-217), APOE genotyping, and brain CT. Participants with a MoCA total ES of 0 will be classified as having cognitive impairment on the basis of screening alone. At two prespecified sites, consecutive consenting participants with neuropsychologically defined cognitive impairment will additionally undergo an EEG vigilance protocol, auditory P300 recording, seven-day actigraphy, and overnight polysomnography. Patients with neuropsychologically defined cognitive impairment at T0 will undergo a 12-month follow-up assessment (T1) of the progression of cognitive impairment and plasma biomarkers; those enrolled in the neurophysiological substudy will additionally repeat the EEG vigilance protocol. Expected Results: The study will provide a conservative (lower-bound) estimate of the prevalence of documented and non-documented cognitive impairment, together with an estimate corrected for partial verification bias, in non-neurological rehabilitation settings. It will further characterise the cognitive profiles and examine their correlations with biomarkers of neurodegeneration (GFAP, NfL, pTau-217), APOE genotype, relative EEG spectral power and sleep intrusion measures, P300 latency and amplitude, actigraphy-derived Sleep Efficiency, and polysomnography-derived sleep stage proportions. Longitudinal data will enable the evaluation of cognitive trajectories and their biological correlates. Conclusions: The COGinREHAB study addresses a critical gap in rehabilitation medicine by implementing a structured, multimodal approach to the identification and characterisation of cognitive impairment in patients with non-neurological conditions. Its findings may facilitate earlier detection of cognitive impairment and inform the development of personalised rehabilitation and care pathways. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07731334.

items.title: Primary Healthcare Reform in Greece: Progress, System Challenges and Future Directions.
items.authors: Triantafyllou C, Ntikoudi A, Papachristou A, Psiakis V, Fonseca VR, Weiler G, Breda J.

sections.text: Primary healthcare (PHC) is fundamental to equitable healthcare access, disease prevention, early diagnosis, chronic disease management and coordination across levels of care. In Greece, the development of a comprehensive and integrated PHC system has been constrained by longstanding organizational fragmentation, parallel public and private delivery arrangements; incomplete implementation of successive reforms; and the absence of consistently standardized patient pathways. This narrative review presents a structured analysis of Greek PHC based on the published literature, official policy documents and administrative evidence, organized around accessibility; adequacy; affordability; appropriateness; availability; and additional domains of continuity, digital integration, patient experience and quality assurance. Greece has developed an extensive network of public, publicly financed private and exclusively private providers, while the Personal Doctor reform provides an institutional basis for population registration, first-contact care and longitudinal monitoring. However, the evidence indicates implementation gaps, geographical variation in physician availability and continued reliance on uncoordinated access to multiple providers. Appointment delays, limited access to contracted physicians and private consultation costs remain important barriers, while gaps persist in home-based care; rehabilitation; palliative care; and integration with public health, mental health and social services. Fragmented clinical information further restricts continuity, accountability and performance assessment. Strengthening Greek PHC requires a transition from administrative registration and fragmented provision towards accessible, multidisciplinary and coordinated care. Proposed priorities include standardized patient pathways, interoperable electronic records, systematic assessment of patient experience, strengthened community-based services, expansion of the nursing workforce and a feasible national quality-monitoring system. Population-based capacity planning is proposed conditionally on secured financing, workforce availability and phased verification of operational services; Italy's incomplete implementation illustrates the risk of equating planning standards with delivered care. Sustainable reform will depend on workforce capacity, institutional continuity, professional and patient participation, and the translation of policy commitments into measurable improvements in routine care.

items.title: The neurobiological complexity of brain dynamics: The neurogliovascular unit and its relevance for psychiatry.
items.authors: Turkheimer FE, Hancock F, Rosas FE, Vernon AC, Srivastava DP, So PW, Luppi AI.

sections.text: Modern neuroscience understands the brain as a complex system whose functional properties are determined by the myriad of interactions of its cellular components. In the difficult route to obtain better understanding of this organ, mathematical tools have become ever more effective, and we are now able to simulate the dynamics of brain signals from digital representations that have high fidelity to experimental data. However, these simulations are generated by inherently simple neuronal models that contain assumptions that, by necessity, can be at times far removed from the underlying neurobiology. Here, we develop an integrated view of brain dynamics that describes how the neurovascular units-made of neurons, capillaries, and glia-collectively determine the development of the functional properties of brain neuronal populations and maintain their homeostatic control. These interactions are instructed by genetic programs modulated by local environmental conditions. These complexities can be integrated into generative models and supply helpful analytics able to link the observable data to neurobiological entities if detailed brain mappings of molecular and cellular components are available. We further highlight how the development of these generative models could be relevant to the understanding of psychiatric conditions.

items.title: Creatine Beyond Muscle: Pleiotropic Effects with and Without Exercise-A Critical Narrative Review.
items.authors: Marco-Alacid C, Leon Fierro A.

sections.text: Creatine is an established ergogenic aid, but its benefits beyond its effects in muscles remain uncertain. This critical narrative review examines cognitive, neurological, psychiatric, metabolic, vascular, skeletal, inflammatory, and rehabilitation outcomes. Targeted searches and citation tracing included publications available on 30 October 2026. We distinguished effects without prescribed exercise, incremental benefits within a common programme, interaction, intervention packages, and mediation. Small studies under sleep loss or hypoxia reported selected cognitive signals; findings in rested adults were inconsistent and benefits in the neurodegenerative conditions examined remained unestablished. Psychiatric findings remained heterogeneous and did not establish clinically important average efficacy. A potentially clinically important glycated haemoglobin reduction in one small exercise-add-on trial in type 2 diabetes remains unreplicated and at a high risk of bias. Vascular findings concerned short-term surrogates; bone-density outcomes were largely null, chronic anti-inflammatory efficacy unestablished, and rehabilitation findings inconsistent. Creatine modestly increased lean mass during resistance training, but downstream clinical mediation was unproven. Sparse evidence on randomised creatine-by-exercise interaction and mediation limits causal attribution without invalidating incremental effects estimated in suitable two-arm trials. Heterogeneous regimens preclude a generalisable dose recommendation. Clinical interpretation should remain indication-specific, prioritising the replication of relevant effects and testing interactions or mediations when those are the research questions.

items.title: Urbanization compromises natural immunity - nature-based solutions may help.
items.authors: Haahtela T.

sections.text: Several layers of environment intertwine with human life. Cultural evolution - built on the biological evolution - has led to population explosion, urbanization and overuse of natural resources. It has meant better life for many but has its prize in global warming and nature loss. The ever more common urban environment and lifestyle are alienating individuals and societies from wider nature, i.e., reducing nature contacts. Biodiverse environment challenges humankind but also protects both physical and mental health. Human body is an ecosystem and needs microbiota and biogenic chemicals for balanced immunoregulation, to make a difference between danger and non-danger, self and non-self. Allergic conditions and autoimmune diseases indicate distorted immune recognition and are signalling a public health crisis. All over the urban world, chronic noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) are on the rise. They seem to share compromised natural immunity, i.e., lack of effective crosstalk between innate and adaptive immunity. Nature-based Solutions (NbS) are called for to combine actions to promote public health, mitigate climate change and stop nature loss. The present review gives an environmental perspective of the factors increasing the risk of NCDs in modern societies. Examples of interventions and new guidelines are highlighted to improve health practices and to encourage for change.

items.title: Social identities as conduits for harm: Inequality and secondary stressors among minority ethnic mothers during the COVID-19 pandemic.
items.authors: Ntontis E, Malovic A, Myers R, Rousaki A, Ulber J.
items.journal: The British journal of social psychology

sections.text: Research on the mental health impacts of extreme events has traditionally examined the prevalence of stressors and the macro-level factors that shape outcomes. However, it says little about the psychosocial processes through which secondary stressors, rooted in pre-existing inequalities and institutional arrangements or in inadequate responses to extreme events, become distressing. In response to calls for psychosocial systems thinking, we examine how mothers from minority ethnic backgrounds experienced the COVID-19 pandemic in the UK. Reflexive thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with 15 mothers, informed by the social identity approach and systems thinking, produced five themes. These suggest four social identity processes through which stressors became distressing and, in some accounts, cascaded: the individualization of structural failure, identity-based role overload and captivity, the rupture of social connectedness and the erosion of standing and agency. We argue that social identities, rooted in people's structural positions within systems, are a psychosocial link between secondary stressors. Our analysis extends models of secondary stressors beyond material and institutional conditions, integrates the social identity approach with systems thinking and specifies circumstances in which social identities were protective. We discuss implications for disaster responses that address structural inequalities and not only their symptoms.

items.title: Basic Psychological Need Satisfaction and Frustration in the Association Between Childhood Maltreatment and Adult Stress Response: A Cross-Sectional Study of Chinese Adults.
items.authors: Lei Y, Gu H, Liu C.

sections.text: Childhood maltreatment is associated with self-reported stress response, but the roles of basic psychological need satisfaction and frustration remain unclear. This cross-sectional study examined statistical indirect associations through six need dimensions in 345 Chinese adults, including 74 with and 271 without a reported psychiatric diagnosis. Self-report measures assessed childhood maltreatment, need experiences, and stress response. Regression and mediation models adjusted for age, sex, subjective socioeconomic status, and reported psychiatric diagnosis status. Competence frustration and autonomy frustration were positively associated with stress response, whereas competence satisfaction was negatively associated. In the parallel model, competence frustration was the only specific indirect effect remaining significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction (B = 0.144, β = 0.083, FDR-adjusted p = 0.002). Exploratory subtype analyses suggested partially differentiated patterns involving emotional abuse, emotional neglect, and physical neglect. Exploratory sensitivity analyses provided no robust evidence of moderation by reported psychiatric diagnosis status. The findings provide preliminary support for need-related indirect associations in this sample. They do not establish causal mechanisms, independent subtype-specific pathways, or the superiority of competence frustration over other need dimensions.

items.title: Effects of a Five-Night Residential Early Parenting Program on Unsettled Infant Behaviour and Parenting Self-Efficacy: An Audit of Routinely Collected Clinical Data.
items.authors: Stanzel KA, Nguyen H, Tran T, Thean P, French D, Popplestone S, Fisher J.

sections.text: Residential early parenting services in Australia provide psychoeducational programs for unsettled infant behaviour, which is reported by up to 35% of parents in their child's first year and can negatively affect parenting self-efficacy. This study aimed to evaluate changes in infant behaviour and parenting self-efficacy following a five-night residential early parenting program and to identify demographic, social, and psychological predictors of parenting self-efficacy. An observational pre-post study using routinely collected medical record data from parents and infants aged up to 24 months was analysed. Parenting self-efficacy was assessed pre-admission and post-discharge using seven items from the Karitane Parenting Confidence Scale. Infant sleeping and cry/fuss behaviour was measured at pre-admission, pre-discharge, and at the 6-week follow-up using study-specific questions. N = 1243 completed the program and provided pre-admission and pre-discharge data. N = 540 provided follow-up data. Overall, improvements were observed following participation. Infant sleeping and cry/fuss behaviour improved pre-discharge and remained largely stable at follow-up. Parenting self-efficacy increased from pre-admission to follow-up. An older maternal age, infants aged ≤ 4 months, and the reporting of more borderline personality disorder symptoms were associated with lower improvements in parenting self-efficacy. Residential early parenting programs improve infant behaviour and parental self-efficacy, though targeted follow-up services are indicated to sustain outcomes for vulnerable subgroups.

items.title: Emotional Engagement with AI Chatbots and Subjective Well-Being Among Young Adults: Extending the S-O-R Model Through Psychological Mechanisms.
items.authors: Chung D, Zhang Z, Wang J.

sections.text: In an era where individuals experience increasing stress and burnout from workplace and societal pressures, the growing adoption of digital interventions (e.g., AI chatbots) has been accompanied by increasing interest in psychological and emotional well-being globally. Such trends are also evident in China. However, the psychological processes associated with this emerging form of human-machine interaction remain insufficiently explored. The current research examines the association between emotional engagement with AI chatbots and subjective well-being among Chinese young adults (18-35 years old). Guided by the extended Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework, this study examines the indirect associations through mindfulness and psychological resilience, including their serial mediation, as well as the moderating role of perceived warmth in the association between emotional engagement with AI chatbots and mindfulness. A cross-sectional survey design was employed, and valid data from 325 participants were collected through an online questionnaire platform. The hypotheses were tested using Jamovi and SPSS. The findings indicated a significant indirect association between emotional engagement with AI chatbots and subjective well-being through psychological resilience, as well as a significant serial indirect association through mindfulness and psychological resilience. Nevertheless, the indirect association through mindfulness alone and the hypothesized interaction involving perceived warmth were not statistically supported. Future research could further examine virtual humans, such as embodied conversational agents, in relation to subjective well-being. Moreover, collaboration between content creators and mental health professionals may contribute to the responsible development and use of AI chatbots as emerging tools related to young adults' positive psychological functioning.

items.title: Parental Phubbing and School Adjustment in Chinese Adolescents: The Mediating Role of Parent-Child Conflict and the Moderating Role of Gender.
items.authors: Liu N, Wang X.

sections.text: Parental phubbing, as a family risk factor, is associated with adolescents' mental health. School adjustment represents another important developmental domain among adolescents. Drawing upon ecological systems theory and family systems theory, this cross-sectional study recruited 3973 adolescents (M = 12.79, SD = 0.77). We separately examined whether paternal phubbing and maternal phubbing predicted overall school adjustment via father-child conflict and mother-child conflict, with gender as the moderator. Data analyses were conducted using SPSS 26.0 and Hayes' PROCESS macro for correlation, mediation, and moderated mediation analyses. The results showed that paternal phubbing and maternal phubbing were negatively correlated with adolescents' school adjustment. Father-child conflict partially mediated the association between paternal phubbing and school adjustment. Mother-child conflict partially mediated the association between maternal phubbing and school adjustment. Gender only moderated the path from maternal phubbing to mother-child conflict. The interaction term was significant, indicating that the positive predictive effect of maternal phubbing on mother-child conflict was stronger for girls. These findings enrich ecological systems theory and family systems theory, and provide empirical support for the coordinated development of family and school education.

items.title: Rapid Weight Loss in Competitive Boxers: Salivary Neuroendocrine and Neurotrophic Responses, Executive Function, and Eating Behavior Across Weight Cutting and Recovery.
items.authors: Erkılıç TO, Bayraktar B, Erkılıç AO.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Rapid weight loss (RWL) is widely practiced in boxing, yet its short-term associations with hydration, salivary biomarkers, executive function, and eating-related risk remain incompletely characterized. This prospective observational repeated-measures study examined competitive male boxers across baseline (T1), pre-weigh-in peak RWL (T2), and 12-18 h post-weigh-in recovery (T3).

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: Sixty competitive male boxers were assessed using bioelectrical impedance analysis, urine-specific gravity, salivary osmolality, dietary intake, estimated energy availability (EA), salivary cortisol, testosterone, salivary alpha-amylase (sAA), spexin, apelin, brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), neuron-derived neurotrophic factor (NDNF), computerized executive-function/reaction-time tasks, and psychometric instruments assessing eating attitudes and affective state.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: At T2, body mass decreased by 6.22 ± 1.48%, while estimated EA decreased from 42.8 ± 4.6 to 14.2 ± 3.8 kcal/kg fat-free mass/day ( p < 0.001). Hydration indices worsened, cortisol and sAA increased, and salivary testosterone, spexin, apelin, BDNF, and NDNF decreased. Executive-task performance, reaction time, state anxiety, and mood disturbance also deteriorated. After 12-18 h recovery, several physiological, salivary, and cognitive outcomes remained different from baseline under the observed self-directed recovery conditions. Linear regression identified acute weight-loss magnitude, lower estimated EA, hydration stress, and salivary biomarker shifts as correlates of Stroop slowing; these models are exploratory and associative. Unmeasured salivary flow and assay quantification limitations constrain interpretation of the biomarker associations. In addition, 38.3% of participants exceeded the EAT-26 screening threshold for elevated eating-disorder risk.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: In this cohort, real-world RWL was temporally associated with dehydration, very low estimated EA, salivary stress-marker changes, slower executive-task performance, and elevated eating-risk screening. Given the absence of a non-weight-cutting control group and the concentration-based nature of peripheral salivary measurements, these findings should be interpreted as ecologically relevant observational associations requiring confirmation in controlled, larger cohorts.

items.title: Clinical Translation of Optically Pumped Magnetometer-Based Magnetoencephalography: Current Evidence, Implementation Challenges, and Future Pathways.
items.authors: Peng Y, Ding M.

sections.text: Optically pumped magnetometer-based magnetoencephalography (OPM-MEG) enables cryogen-free, on-scalp recordings with wearable, individually configurable sensor arrays. These features may expand access to MEG for patients poorly accommodated by fixed-helmet superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) systems. This review evaluates current clinical evidence, implementation barriers, and priorities for clinical translation. This narrative review synthesizes OPM-MEG studies in presurgical epilepsy evaluation and functional mapping, alongside exploratory applications in other neurological and psychiatric conditions. Evidence is considered in relation to clinical performance, validation endpoints, and requirements for acquisition, analysis, and implementation across different clinical settings. Patient-based evidence includes comparative and prospective studies of presurgical evaluation in drug-resistant focal epilepsy. Studies support interictal epileptiform discharge detection and localization, with broad concordance with SQUID-MEG and intracranial electrophysiology; early reports also demonstrate ictal recordings. Pediatric and motion-tolerant recordings represent promising applications. Motor mapping has progressed to small patient cohorts with limited intraoperative validation, while language mapping is supported mainly by small studies and case reports. Applications in neurodegenerative, headache, psychiatric, and developmental disorders remain exploratory and currently lack established clinical indications for MEG. Common translational priorities include standardized performance benchmarks, acquisition quality control, motion management, co-registration, analysis, reporting, and personnel training. OPM-MEG shows promise for extending clinical MEG, supported by patient-based feasibility and comparative studies in presurgical epilepsy evaluation. Multicenter prospective studies should establish performance and reproducibility for defined indications. New applications and claims of additional benefit require evaluation of their effects on clinical management and patient outcomes, supported by standardized workflows across systems and centers.

items.title: Developing Culturally Responsive Trauma-Informed Care in Bangladesh: Challenges, Opportunities, and Implications for Children and Youth Well-Being Using Transformational Collaborative Outcomes Management (TCOM).
items.authors: Mithila T, Lyons J, Siddiqi KA, Chowdhury SH, Lardner M.

sections.heading: Background/objectives
sections.text: Children in Bangladesh face high exposure to adversity, including poverty, child labor, violence, early marriage, displacement, and natural disasters, yet the child welfare system remains fragmented and largely reactive, and children's trauma responses are often framed as behavioral problems. This perspective examines the barriers to culturally responsive trauma-informed care (TIC) and proposes Transformational Collaborative Outcomes Management (TCOM) as an organizing framework.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: We conducted a targeted narrative review of peer-reviewed and policy literature on trauma, child welfare, and TIC in Bangladesh, South Asia, and other low- and middle-income settings, interpreted through the authors' experience of developing and implementing TCOM.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: The literature points to stigma, workforce shortages, fragmented multi-ministry governance, short-term project funding, and the absence of a trauma-informed assessment tool or shared data system; no Bangladesh-specific TIC model has been evaluated. We map TCOM's six principles onto these barriers, propose a six-step roadmap anchored in a cross-sector coordinating structure, compare phased with nationwide implementation, and discuss TCOM's limitations and alternative approaches.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: TCOM could provide a common language and data infrastructure for trauma-informed child welfare reform in Bangladesh, but it has limitations and these proposals are untested; phased piloting, cultural validation, and evaluation of costs and outcomes are needed before national scale-up.

items.title: HEADS-ED Under 6: Accuracy in Informing Pathways to Mental Health and Neurodevelopmental Health Care for Infants and Young Children.
items.authors: Robson S, Sheridan N, Cloutier P, Cappelli M.

sections.text: Background/Objectives: To examine the effectiveness of the HEADS-ED Under 6 as a tool for determining the appropriate pathways to care for infants, toddlers, and children under 6. Methods: We used a retrospective cohort design to analyze client acuity and referrals at a centralized mental health and coordinated access program for infants, children, and youth (1Call1Click.ca). Specifically, we examined client acuity using HEADS-ED Under 6 total scores, accuracy of referrals, and the acceptance rate of referrals for clients at the agencies and hospital resources they were referred to. Clients aged 0-6 years who received referrals ( N = 1637) between March 2023 and December 2025 were included in the analyses. Results: The HEADS-ED Under 6 showed high sensitivity (0.95), specificity (0.90), and accuracy (0.91) in guiding referrals to services. Client referrals were made with a high degree of acceptance, with 93.0% of referrals accepted by the referred-to agencies, community and hospital programs. Conclusions: The HEADS-ED Under 6 is a useful tool for assessing need in infants and children under 6 to accurately guide referrals to care resources.

abstract.text: Background/Objectives: To examine the effectiveness of the HEADS-ED Under 6 as a tool for determining the appropriate pathways to care for infants, toddlers, and children under 6. Specifically, we examined client acuity using HEADS-ED Under 6 total scores, accuracy of referrals, and the acceptance rate of referrals for clients at the agencies and hospital resources they were referred to. Clients aged 0-6 years who received referrals ( N = 1637) between March 2023 and December 2025 were included in the analyses. Results: The HEADS-ED Under 6 showed high sensitivity (0.95), specificity (0.90), and accuracy (0.91) in guiding referrals to services. Client referrals were made with a high degree of acceptance, with 93.0% of referrals accepted by the referred-to agencies, community and hospital programs. Conclusions: The HEADS-ED Under 6 is a useful tool for assessing need in infants and children under 6 to accurately guide referrals to care resources.

items.title: Screen Time and Emotional and Behavioral Difficulties Among Children in Spain: A Population-Based Study of the 2023 Spanish Health Survey.
items.authors: Martorell Sánchez C, Domínguez Pérez J, Vicente-Herrero MT, López-González ÁA, Tárraga López PJ, Ramírez-Manent JI.

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Evidence on the association between recreational screen time and emotional and behavioral difficulties in Spanish children remains limited.

sections.heading: Objective
sections.text: To examine this association, including potential nonlinearity and differences across Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire (SDQ) domains.

sections.heading: Methods
sections.text: This cross-sectional study used data from the 2023 Spanish Health Survey. Of 2920 children aged 4-14 years, 2596 were included in the fully adjusted analysis. Recreational screen time was estimated from weekday and weekend reports. Weighted linear regression with robust standard errors assessed associations with the SDQ Total Difficulties Score, adjusting for demographic, socioeconomic, behavioral, family, and health-related factors. Restricted cubic splines assessed nonlinearity.

sections.heading: Results
sections.text: Each additional hour/day of screen time was associated with a 0.356-point higher SDQ Total Difficulties Score (95% CI, 0.127-0.586; p = 0.002). The association was nonlinear ( p = 0.004). Compared with <1 h/day, ≥3 h/day was associated with a 0.787-point higher score (95% CI, 0.036-1.539; p = 0.040). Positive associations were observed for hyperactivity/inattention, emotional symptoms, and conduct problems after correction for multiple comparisons, but not for peer problems or prosocial behavior.

sections.heading: Conclusions
sections.text: Greater recreational screen time was associated with modestly higher emotional and behavioral difficulties, particularly at higher exposure levels. The cross-sectional findings do not establish causality or a specific screen-time threshold.
